conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/26/26
conflicts.issue: 50% Flat After-School Tuition Increase vs. Lower/Phased Rate and Expanded Low-Income Discounts
conflicts.summary: Board members split 5-2 over adopting administration's recommended 50% flat tuition hike while maintaining current financial assistance versus adopting a gentler 40% increase or pairing the 50% rate with a 50% discount for low-income families.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve administration's 50% tuition increase with existing financial assistance to prevent the enterprise fund from running in the red and restore reserves toward $1.5M.
side_a_arguments: Tuition had been frozen for nearly a decade while group-leader wage targets rose toward $19.22/hr and COVID stabilization grants expired.
Even at 50% ($307.50/month or ~$4/hour), DPS after-school care remains well below local market rates and DSS child-care voucher ceilings.
conflicts.side_b_position: Soften the immediate financial shock on working families via a 40% phased increase or a 50% discount offset by higher-income contributions.
side_b_arguments: A sudden 50% increase hits lower-income families disproportionately amid regional layoffs and inflation.
Emily Chávez sought a 50% discount for eligible families (motion died for lack of a second) while Natalie Beyer urged a 40% rate paired with a donor scholarship fund.
conflicts.resolution: Main motion passed 5-2 by voice vote adopting the 50% increase with current assistance, paired with informal board direction to explore donor/DPS Foundation sponsorship options and annual rate reviews.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
conflicts.issue: Legal Services RFP Selection Process, Rubric Transparency, and Deferral (Item 5C)
conflicts.summary: Board members clashed over whether to defer Legal Services RFP presentations (failing 1-6) and over transparency of the scoring rubric used to narrow finalists to Poyner Spruill and Tharrington Smith.
conflicts.side_a_position: Demand full RFP scoring rubrics, fee transparency, and careful evaluation before deciding on legal counsel.
side_a_arguments: Board members had not received complete RFP evaluation matrices and pricing comparisons ahead of the presentations.
Contracting board legal counsel is a core board governance responsibility requiring transparent comparative data.
conflicts.side_b_position: Proceed with hearing both finalist firms as scheduled rather than deferring Item 5C.
side_b_arguments: Both law firms had already been invited and were present in the room to present to the board.
Hearing presentations does not force an immediate final contract vote.
conflicts.resolution: Deferral motion failed 1-6; both Poyner Spruill and Tharrington Smith presented starting at 04:11:53, and no contract vote was taken—instead the board formed a three-member working group to review options.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
conflicts.issue: Policy 2231 Policy Committee Submission Deadlines and Meeting Cadence
conflicts.summary: Members divided in multiple straw polls (5-2 and 3-4) over Policy Committee cadence, rolling vs. fixed deadlines, and whether the policy request deadline should be July 15 or August 31.
conflicts.side_a_position: Set an August 31 submission deadline and structured periodic review cycles rather than continuous rolling submissions or monthly meetings.
side_a_arguments: An August 31 deadline gives newly organized board leadership and staff realistic summer bandwidth.
Fixed review windows prevent overwhelming district staff and legal counsel with continuous ad-hoc policy drafts.
conflicts.side_b_position: Prefer earlier July 15 deadlines, monthly committee meetings, or rolling submissions.
side_b_arguments: More frequent monthly meetings and rolling submissions allow timely board responsiveness to urgent equity and operational policy issues.
conflicts.resolution: Majority favored August 31 in a 5-2 straw poll while monthly cadence and rolling submissions failed with 3 votes each; Policy 2231 then advanced on first reading 7-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) 11% Threshold, Third-Party Verification, and Late-Draft Process
conflicts.summary: The board split 4-3 over adopting last-minute May 22 modifications to Policy 7215 lowering the ERO recognition threshold to 11% and allowing third-party verification.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt the amended May 22 draft immediately with an 11% threshold, mutual-agreement third-party verification, and streamlined ERO language.
side_a_arguments: The 11% threshold and third-party verification respond directly to months of employee advocacy and protect worker privacy while keeping the policy moving before summer.
Striking 'all' and the Section C Appendix and requiring mutual agreement on a third-party certifier address administrative feasibility concerns.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer or reject the May 22 rewrite pending formal legal review and standard public-notice procedures.
side_b_arguments: Circulating major policy changes the day of the meeting circumvents transparent board process and public notice.
Third-party membership verification and ERO record handling raise unresolved North Carolina Public Records Act risks.
conflicts.resolution: Beyer's motion to table to June 10 failed for lack of a second; the amended May 22 Policy 7215 draft passed 4-3.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session
conflicts.issue: Board Community Engagement Policy Scope, Legal Compliance, and Special Meeting (1-6 Split)
conflicts.summary: Board members clashed sharply over a draft Board Community Engagement Policy authored by Harrell-Goff, Chávez, and Carda-Auten, culminating in a 1-6 rejection of a special meeting before a 7-0 referral to the Policy Committee.
conflicts.side_a_position: Fast-track or adopt a structured community engagement policy featuring board school visits, listening protocols, and community QR feedback tools.
side_a_arguments: Board members need consistent, proactive mechanisms to hear families, students, and staff beyond three-minute public comment.
A dedicated special meeting would allow timely refinement before the next school year.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject a rush special meeting and scrutinize staff burden, school visit logistics, Open Meetings Law risks, and document ownership in committee.
side_b_arguments: Unvetted mandates for board school visits and QR-code data collection could burden building staff and create Open Meetings or public-records compliance issues.
The newly structured Policy Committee is the appropriate forum to vet governance drafts.
conflicts.resolution: Chávez's special-meeting motion failed 1-6 (with Harrell-Goff and Carda-Auten voting Nay alongside Beyer, Umstead, Tabb, and Rogers); the board then voted 7-0 to refer the draft to the Policy Committee.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
conflicts.issue: Policy 7215 Meet and Confer ERO Threshold (6% vs. 20%), Committee Structure, and Waiving Second Reading
conflicts.summary: The board split 3-4 on Jessica Carda-Auten's amendment for a 20% ERO threshold and then 4-3 to waive second reading and adopt the administration-backed 6% Policy 7215 draft.
conflicts.side_a_position: Require a 20% ERO threshold or pursue further mediation with DAE rather than adopting a 6% threshold in one meeting.
side_a_arguments: A 6% threshold dilutes representative worker organizations and creates an unbalanced Meet and Confer committee.
Waiving second reading cuts off community and worker feedback on a policy 14 months in the making.
conflicts.side_b_position: Waive second reading and adopt the 6% ERO threshold policy immediately with technical guardrails (Section E1 vice chair and exclusive seat table).
side_b_arguments: Legal counsel advised that lower thresholds avoid improper exclusivity under North Carolina law and ensure broad employee access.
Adopting a baseline policy now lets Meet and Confer begin functioning immediately, with future amendments always possible.
conflicts.resolution: Carda-Auten's 20% threshold amendment failed 3-4 (Tabb joined Rogers, Beyer, Umstead in Nay); on the main motion Tabb voted Nay while Beyer, Umstead, Rogers, and Carda-Auten carried the 6% policy 4-3 (later modified to 11% on May 22).

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/21/24
conflicts.issue: Expanding 2024-25 Local Master's Pay to Certified Instructional Support Staff Amid Existing Budget Shortfall
conflicts.summary: Following revelation of a $1.258M shortfall on classroom-teacher Master's pay and an incomplete FY24 audit, board members clashed over voting immediately to grant Master's pay with back pay to social workers and instructional staff versus requiring a funded budget plan first.
conflicts.side_a_position: Direct immediate equity and 2024-25 Master's pay coverage for all pre-2013 DPI certified teachers and instructional staff (including social workers, coaches, specialists, and coordinators).
side_a_arguments: Spring 2024 board messaging promised 'teachers' Master's pay under state rules, and social workers were sent conflicting confirmation and retraction emails.
Withholding Master's pay from non-classroom certified staff who serve high-need students harms morale and retention.
conflicts.side_b_position: Table or defer any binding commitment until CFO Jeremy Teeter identifies funding offsets and completes FY24 audit clarity.
side_b_arguments: Classroom teacher Master's pay alone is already $1.258M over budget ($2.517M vs $1.259M), requiring 15% department budget holds.
Expanding to additional roles adds at least $272k+ and an unknown liability without verified local revenue.
conflicts.resolution: A tabling motion failed 2-5, after which the board adopted a 7-0 amended compromise motion (passed 6-1) directing administration to present a funded plan for full pre-2013 DPI coverage with 2024-25 back pay at a December 2 special meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 9/26/24
conflicts.issue: Meet and Confer Policy: 50% ERO Membership Threshold vs. Inclusive Multi-Group Consultation and Statutory Caution
conflicts.summary: Following a unanimous referral for collaborative policy drafting, the board split 4-3 on explicitly directing a Meet and Confer policy centered on an Employee Representative Organization (ERO) with 50% employee membership.
conflicts.side_a_position: Mandate a Meet and Confer policy establishing regular meetings with an ERO representing at least 50% of eligible non-administrative DPS employees.
side_a_arguments: Recognizes the democratic majority voice of workers organized through DAE after months of compensation turmoil.
Sets a clear, verifiable threshold rather than watering down representation across small or ad hoc groups.
conflicts.side_b_position: Avoid locking in a 50% ERO exclusivity directive before legal review and input from non-DAE workers.
side_b_arguments: Attorney raised legal concerns under NCGS 95-98 (public bargaining prohibition) and NCGS 115C-335.9 (equal-access obligations).
Setting a strict 50% ERO rule could exclude other employees or organizations (such as Teamsters or non-union workers) before the Superintendent's working group drafts a policy.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 4-3 directing development of the 50%-threshold ERO Meet and Confer policy alongside the 7-0 drafting referral.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
conflicts.issue: Advancing Meet and Confer Draft of Policy 1750/7220 vs Joint Legal/HR Redrafting
conflicts.summary: Board members debated whether to honor Meet and Confer's consensus draft of employee grievance policy 1750/7220 on first read immediately or require joint legal, HR, and union redrafting first.
conflicts.side_a_position: Initially proposed adopting the Meet and Confer draft on first reading and sending it to the August work session for second-read refinements.
side_a_arguments: Educator representatives invested significant Meet and Confer time and deserved to see the product advance rather than stall during board transition.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject first-read passage until HR, board counsel, DAE/NCAE, and DAE counsel resolve operational and legal contradictions.
side_b_arguments: Board counsel and HR had not had sufficient collaborative redrafting sessions with DAE counsel to ensure a legally workable grievance timeline.
Handing an incomplete first-read draft to four incoming board members would create confusion.
conflicts.resolution: The first-read motion failed 0-7 after sponsors joined the consensus, and the board unanimously approved 7-0 a directive for a joint HR, DAE/NCAE, and legal draft due by the September work session.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
conflicts.issue: Approve Policy 1750/7220 (Grievance Procedures for Employees) on First Read as Submitted and Advance to August Work Session
conflicts.summary: Taking up Policy 1750/7220 on employee grievance procedures from the Meet and Confer process, Joy Harrell-Goff initially moved (seconded by Emily Chávez) to accept the Meet and Confer draft as-is on first reading and advance it to the August work session to honor educator collaboration. However, Board Attorney Malone, Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, Millicent Rogers, and Jessica Carda-Auten pointed out unresolved procedural conflicts, unclear timelines, and inconsistencies with existing legal standards that HR and legal counsel had not yet reconciled with DAE. Convinced that advancing an unvetted draft would create confusion for the incoming board, even the sponsors joined the unanimous 0-7 vote against the motion.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 0-7)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (0-7)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/14/26
conflicts.issue: Bypassing Policy Committee Tier Queue (Policy 2231) to Discuss Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer)
conflicts.summary: The board split sharply over whether two board members could use Policy 2330 agenda rules to bring proposed Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) edits directly to the board table without going through Policy 2231's prioritized tiering queue.
conflicts.side_a_position: Permit two board members to place Policy 7215 discussion on the work session agenda and clarify conflicts with Policy 2231 prior to May 31 certification.
side_a_arguments: Policy 2330 grants any two board members the right to place items on an agenda for discussion.
Policies coming out of Meet and Confer face an unresolved procedural conflict with Policy 2231 ahead of the May 31 annual certification deadline.
Full-board discussion is necessary rather than confining debate to Policy Committee members.
conflicts.side_b_position: Enforce Policy 2231 strictly so Policy 7215 cannot jump ahead of 30 tiered policies already voted on by the full board.
side_b_arguments: Policy 2231 was crafted specifically to stop small groups of board members from shopping unprioritized policies outside committee.
Twelve Tier 2 and 18 Tier 3 policies (on seclusion/restraint, K-2 suspensions, AI, lactation, and LGBTQ+ support) wait in the queue.
DAE leadership and administration were not consulted as co-chairs on these redlines.
conflicts.resolution: The two-thirds motion to waive Policy 2231 failed; a subsequent motion by Carda-Auten to refer Policy 7215 to the Policy Committee for the next academic year passed 3-2.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 1/29/26
conflicts.issue: Delaying After-School Fee Decision to Build Sliding-Scale Tuition Models vs. Preserving Camp Registration Timelines
conflicts.summary: The Board divided 4-3 over directing administration to spend four weeks building sliding-scale tuition models comparable in revenue to a 50% hike, knowing it would push summer camp registration from February 16 into March.
conflicts.side_a_position: Require sliding-scale tuition models by February 26 before raising rates so higher-income families can offset lower-income increases.
side_a_arguments: A flat 35%-50% jump burdens low-income Black and Hispanic families disproportionately during economic instability.
Board members criticized being pressured into a major fee increase on short notice without robust community notice or equity options.
conflicts.side_b_position: Avoid delaying summer camp and after-school registration timelines or imposing sliding-scale modeling without reliable family income data.
side_b_arguments: DPS lacks household income records for lottery families and would face revenue uncertainty or require income-tier quotas.
Pushing February 16 summer camp registration into March disrupts working families' childcare planning; Beyer favored signaling a modest floor or targeting 2027-28 for sliding scale.
conflicts.resolution: Emily Chávez's modified motion directing sliding-scale models by February 26 passed 4-3 on a voice vote (returning on Feb 26, where the Board ultimately adopted the 50% flat rate 5-2).

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
conflicts.issue: Immediate Rollout vs. Operational Planning for Magnet/Specialty Express Bus Stops
conflicts.summary: The board deadlocked 3-3 on implementing Express Stops immediately for School for Creative Studies, DSA, and Rogers-Herr before voting 4-2 to authorize planning for January 2025 implementation pending a January 9 operational review.
conflicts.side_a_position: Move immediately or prepare directly for January 2025 Express Stops to end rotational bus coverage.
side_a_arguments: Express Stops save ~8 routes primarily serving secondary magnet students who are older than elementary FRZ riders.
Ending four-day rotational cancellations is urgent for working families and drivers alike.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject mid-year implementation of Express Stops without advance notice, hub logistics, and transparent appeals.
side_b_arguments: Implementing Express Stops mid-year with minimal notice disrupts families who selected magnet schools relying on bus access.
Hub locations, supervision, weather shelter, and Policy 1740/4010 grievance details had not been finalized.
conflicts.resolution: Immediate implementation failed 3-3; Jessica Carda-Auten joined the majority in a 4-2 vote authorizing Express Stop planning to end rotational coverage in January 2025 with detailed plans due January 9.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 7/5/26
conflicts.issue: Contested Election for Board Chair
conflicts.summary: Board members divided between electing incumbent Vice Chair Millicent Rogers or incumbent at-large member Joy Harrell-Goff as Board Chair immediately after four new members took their oaths.
conflicts.side_a_position: Elect incumbent Vice Chair Millicent Rogers as Board Chair.
side_a_arguments: Rogers offered institutional continuity and prior Vice Chair leadership experience during a four-seat board turnover.
conflicts.side_b_position: Elect Joy Harrell-Goff as Board Chair.
side_b_arguments: Supported Harrell-Goff's leadership to guide the newly constituted board cohort.
conflicts.resolution: Millicent Rogers's nomination failed 2-5 by voice vote and Joy Harrell-Goff was elected Board Chair 5-2.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
conflicts.issue: PreK-5 Level 1B Out-of-School Suspensions and EC Principal Supervisor Review (Policy 4301.1)
conflicts.summary: Members debated prohibiting Level 1B suspensions across PreK-5 and requiring principal supervisor review for all PreK-5 suspensions of students with disabilities.
conflicts.side_a_position: Expand oversight to require principal supervisor review before suspending any PreK-5 student with a disability and curb Level 1B exclusions.
side_a_arguments: Addresses severe disproportionality in elementary suspensions of Black, Hispanic, and EC students.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain administrative discretion for escalating safety disruptions and avoid overextending supervisor review beyond PreK-2 capacity.
side_b_arguments: Principals and superintendent Dr. Lewis emphasized staff readiness limits and the need for safety tools in upper elementary.
conflicts.resolution: The board rejected full PreK-5 1B elimination in discussion but narrowly approved (4-3) requiring principal supervisor review prior to suspending PreK-5 students with disabilities.

conflicts.issue: Motion to Schedule a Special Meeting on Draft Board Community Engagement Policy
conflicts.summary: After extensive debate beginning at 03:18:13 over a Board Community Engagement Policy presented by Joy Harrell-Goff, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten, Emily Chávez moved at 04:40:42 (restated at 04:55:29) to schedule a dedicated special meeting to advance the draft policy, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff. conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (1-6)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 1/6/25
conflicts.issue: Policy 6322 FRZ Hardship Exception Standards and Mid-Year Secondary Magnet Express Stops
conflicts.summary: During the special called review, board members split between demanding stricter equity safeguards, accessible hardship waivers, and delays on Express Stops versus empowering staff to deploy standard peer-district transit tools immediately to end rotational busing.
conflicts.side_a_position: Pressed for clear, accessible Policy 6322 hardship exemptions and raised severe equity and safety objections to unsupervised early-morning Express Stops and mid-year walk zones.
side_a_arguments: Emily Chávez and Joy Harrell-Goff warned that 7:15-7:45 AM Express Stops without guaranteed supervision or walkable infrastructure create safety risks in winter darkness and disproportionately burden single and low-income working parents.

Jessica Carda-Auten, Chávez, and Harrell-Goff insisted families facing extreme transportation hardship need a transparent, navigable administrative approval path rather than punitive barriers—even as Dr. Nicholas King cautioned against placing principals in the position of overriding board policy.
conflicts.side_b_position: Supported giving staff operational latitude to implement Express Stops and 1-mile FRZs consistent with large North Carolina peer districts.
side_b_arguments: Natalie Beyer noted that Wake, Charlotte-Mecklenburg, and Guilford school systems already utilize 1.5-mile walk zones and magnet Express Stops to manage driver shortages.
Continuing rotational bus cancellations harms families unpredictably, so staff need board backing to execute structural routing reforms.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; intense board and ThoughtExchange pushback led administration to return on January 9 with a revised plan deferring Express Stops to 2025-26 and drafting a formal Policy 6322 hardship exception form.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Organizational Meeting | 7/1/24
conflicts.issue: Board Vice Chair Election: Institutional Memory vs. Leadership Succession
conflicts.summary: Following Millicent Rogers's election as Chair, board members split publicly over whether former Chair Bettina Umstead or newly reelected Jessica Carda-Auten should serve as Vice Chair during Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's onboarding.
conflicts.side_a_position: Elect outgoing Chair Bettina Umstead as Vice Chair to preserve institutional memory and external stakeholder relationships.
side_a_arguments: After the pay crisis and rapid superintendent transition, Dr. Anthony Lewis needs seasoned board leadership continuity alongside Chair Rogers.
Umstead brought deep relationships with Durham County Commissioners, city officials, community organizations, and DAE/Teamsters.
conflicts.side_b_position: Elect Jessica Carda-Auten as Vice Chair to support leadership succession and structured governance.
side_b_arguments: Joy Harrell-Goff emphasized that leadership rotation and succession planning strengthen an equally weighted seven-member governing body.
Carda-Auten advocated establishing clear governance frameworks and board-superintendent accountability systems.
conflicts.resolution: Wendell Tabb abstained on non-unanimous leadership votes (counted as affirmative under board policy); Bettina Umstead's nomination failed 3-4 and Jessica Carda-Auten was elected Vice Chair 6-1.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
conflicts.issue: Adding 'Briefly' Modifier to Policy 4326 Section A3b on Calming/Comforting Students
conflicts.summary: Board members split 6-1 over adding the word 'briefly' to define permissible physical calming/comforting exceptions in Policy 4326 on seclusion and restraint.
conflicts.side_a_position: Insert 'briefly' before 'calm or comfort' to prevent prolonged physical holds from being misclassified.
side_a_arguments: Aligns with NC statutory boundaries and disability-advocate concerns against disguised restraint.
conflicts.side_b_position: Omit 'briefly' to avoid putting caring educators at vague disciplinary risk while comforting distressed children.
side_b_arguments: The term 'briefly' is unquantified and may chill supportive staff interventions.
conflicts.resolution: Both the amendment and final Policy 4326 adoption passed 6-1 with Wendell Tabb voting Nay.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/12/26
conflicts.issue: Policy 5120 Scope on Immigration Enforcement, Judicial Warrants, and Exigent Circumstances
conflicts.summary: Members and public speakers scrutinized whether draft Policy 5120 clearly assigns decision-making to principals, differentiates federal immigration officers from local law enforcement, and avoids overly broad 'exigent circumstances' exceptions.
conflicts.side_a_position: Tighten wording on principal authority, judicial warrant checks, and immigration enforcement definitions before final adoption.
side_a_arguments: Ambiguous pronouns ('they') could leave front-office staff uncertain of who verifies warrants and denies entry.
Student and community advocates urged eliminating broad exigent-circumstances loopholes.
conflicts.side_b_position: Advance the committee's current draft through First Read now while addressing remaining wording refinements in Policy Committee.
side_b_arguments: Passing First Read keeps the policy timeline on track after multiple committee sessions and legal/sheriff consultations.
conflicts.resolution: Passed First Read 6-0 and referred the policy back to the March 19 Policy Committee for detailed textual revisions.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/26/26
conflicts.issue: Policy Committee Priority Order (Code of Conduct vs. Meet & Confer Grievance/Budget Policies)
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed on the sequencing of ten policies in the Policy Committee queue, resulting in a 6-1 split vote over how early to schedule the Student Code of Conduct relative to Budget Transparency and the Grievance Policy.
conflicts.side_a_position: Prioritize Seclusion & Restraint (1st) and Child Abuse Reporting (2nd), followed by Budget Transparency (3rd) and Student Code of Conduct (4th).
side_a_arguments: Budget Transparency is far along from Meet and Confer and timely during active budget season.
Seclusion & Restraint and Child Abuse Reporting require immediate guidance for principals following recent safety incidents.
conflicts.side_b_position: Place Student Code of Conduct ahead of Budget Transparency so restorative discipline matrices can be finalized before summer handbook printing.
side_b_arguments: Code of Conduct revisions will likely take multiple meetings and must be completed before July year-round school handbooks go to print.
conflicts.resolution: Emily Chávez's retiering motion passed 6-1, with Bettina Umstead explicitly noting her lone dissent on the placement of Student Code of Conduct.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 9/25/25
conflicts.issue: Front-End Community Engagement Mandate in Old Lowe's Grove (4550 South Alston Ave) RFP Motion
conflicts.summary: The board divided 6-1 over whether a motion directing administration to consult with Durham County on non-demolition options for Old Lowe's Grove should explicitly include front-end community engagement requirements.
conflicts.side_a_position: Keep the initial consultation motion broad without pre-defining community values, since staff will return a draft RFP publicly for board and community review before posting.
side_a_arguments: Staff needs flexibility to consult Durham County on RFP mechanics first before prescribing specific public-hearing steps.
The draft RFP will return in BoardDocs for full board approval and public input before any solicitation or disposition.
conflicts.side_b_position: Explicitly require front-end community engagement in the motion itself before consulting on non-demolition reuse.
side_b_arguments: Without explicit front-end engagement language in the motion, the board risks ambiguity and having to revisit expectations after shifting away from earlier demolition plans.
conflicts.resolution: Motion carried 6-1 without the amendment, with Wendell Tabb casting the lone Nay vote on the record.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: FY25-26 Budget Request Timeline and Classified / Bus Monitor / Master's Pay Priorities
conflicts.summary: Board members debated whether to delay or expand the FY25-26 budget request to include a 2% classified raise, $200 bus monitor supplement, and full 2013 Master's pay vs. submitting the recommended request on time.
conflicts.side_a_position: Add classified across-the-board raises, bus monitor supplements, and broader Master's pay—or delay submission—before sending the request to the county.
side_a_arguments: DAE and classified speakers warned that leaving out a classified raise and bus monitors harms retention and student services.
conflicts.side_b_position: Submit the ~$222.1M recommended budget request on schedule and refine line items once county and state funding are known.
side_b_arguments: Statutory county deadlines require timely transmittal, and final line-item priorities can be adjusted in June after county and state allocations solidify.
conflicts.resolution: Board unanimously voted 7-0 to submit the FY25-26 Superintendent's Recommended Budget while flagging classified and support-staff priorities for summer updates.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Adding Unscheduled Closed Session After Public Comment Without Disclosing Context (6-1 Split)
conflicts.summary: Emily Chávez questioned adding a closed session for attorney consultation immediately after public comment without explaining the topic publicly beforehand, casting the sole dissenting vote in a 6-1 decision.
conflicts.side_a_position: Provide greater transparency about the purpose or timing of an unscheduled closed session before voting.
side_a_arguments: Adding an unannounced closed session mid-meeting without explanation undermines board transparency to the public.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold confidential attorney-client consultation immediately after public comment under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(3).
side_b_arguments: Attorney consultation is statutorily confidential and requires receiving legal feedback in closed session rather than open debate.
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 6-1, and the board convened its attorney consultation closed session from 01:51:40 to 03:12:58.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/21/25
conflicts.issue: Creation of Ad Hoc Policy Committee, Board Bandwidth, and Late Agenda Addition Process
conflicts.summary: The board split 6-1 over establishing an Ad Hoc Committee of the Whole to create a standing Policy Committee, alongside pointed procedural criticism from two Aye voters regarding how the Chair added the item late Friday afternoon.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support forming an Ad Hoc Committee of the Whole to build a structured standing Policy Committee and defend the Chair's authority to place timely governance items on the agenda.
side_a_arguments: A standing Policy Committee with legal counsel Rod Malone will create transparent, consistent review of outdated board policies rather than reactive policy changes.
Adding the item Friday afternoon complied with North Carolina Open Meetings notice requirements and board policy.
conflicts.side_b_position: Opposed creating a new committee due to competing crisis priorities (Wendell Tabb), or questioned late Friday agenda placement and alleged closed-door policy drafting (Emily Chávez, Joy Harrell-Goff).
side_b_arguments: Wendell Tabb argued adding another committee would consume excessive board and staff bandwidth needed for urgent bus, safety, and budget crises.

Emily Chávez and Joy Harrell-Goff objected that adding the item late Friday without reaching two board members undermined collaborative trust and appeared tied to policies drafted outside public view.
conflicts.resolution: Motion passed 6-1 on roll call, with Wendell Tabb casting the sole Nay vote while Chávez and Harrell-Goff ultimately voted Aye after registering procedural objections.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/9/25
conflicts.issue: Mid-Year Implementation of Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs), Safety Criteria, and Bus Driver Retention
conflicts.summary: Although staff withdrew mid-year Express Stops to end rotational busing on January 17, the board divided sharply over whether to proceed immediately with December 19-approved FRZs given safety, equity, attendance-data, and bus-driver concerns.
conflicts.side_a_position: Questioned or regretted launching FRZs mid-year in January, arguing neighborhood hazards, bus-driver insights, attendance comparisons, and accessible Policy 6322 hardship exceptions were insufficiently developed.
side_a_arguments: Wendell Tabb and Jessica Carda-Auten warned that excluding neighborhood crime, loitering, abandoned buildings, and loose dogs from hazard criteria leaves students unsafe on routes adults would not walk.

Joy Harrell-Goff stated her position flipped since December after meeting with veteran bus drivers, arguing switching from rotational coverage to mid-year FRZs trades one harmful Band-Aid for another without qualitative driver input.

Emily Chávez demanded direct engagement with the DAE transportation delegation, an inventory of community carpool/nonprofit resources at each school, and an immediate meeting focused on driver retention.
conflicts.side_b_position: Urged moving forward on January 17 with the December 19 decision to end exhausting rotational busing while relying on principal collaboration and the case-by-case Policy 6322 hardship appeal process.
side_b_arguments: Reversing course days before January 17 would undermine trust with overworked transportation staff and leave thousands of families who have already made arrangements scrambling.
Bus drivers have been working two to three extra routes past 6:00 PM under rotational coverage; ending rotational routes provides immediate relief while data on FRZs can be monitored and adjusted.
conflicts.resolution: No motion was introduced to rescind December's FRZ approval, allowing staff to end rotational busing and launch FRZs on January 17 while directing administration to meet with the DAE driver delegation and bring a driver retention plan to the January 23 meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
conflicts.issue: Adoption of Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs) Around Elementary Schools
conflicts.summary: Board members split 6-1 over implementing modified <=1-mile Family Responsibility Zones affecting roughly 864 riders in January 2025 to free up ~20 bus routes and end rotational cancellations.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt FRZs now with hazard exclusions and family support protocols to stabilize systemwide bus service.
side_a_arguments: Frees roughly 20 routes to eliminate unpredictable rotational bus cancellations.
Walk zones exclude roads >=35 mph without enhanced crossings and retain EC/McKinney-Vento service.
conflicts.side_b_position: Do not implement FRZs mid-year due to child safety, winter weather, and family hardship concerns.
side_b_arguments: Parents raised urgent concerns about crossing guards, winter coats, and unwalkable routes near schools like Hope Valley.
Policy 1740/4010 hardship exemptions and family-support logistics were not yet clear enough before implementation.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 to adopt FRZs.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/21/24
conflicts.issue: Reconsidering Removal of Master's Pay Item During Fuller Building Power Outage
conflicts.summary: Board members split 6-1 over whether to add the Local Master's Pay update back onto the agenda after building conditions stabilized enough to restore interpretation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Restore the Master's Pay budget update immediately so employees waiting in the room hear the fiscal report.
side_a_arguments: Spanish interpretation was restored at 00:12:46, removing the primary barrier cited for postponement.
School social workers and DAE members turned out in force during public comment specifically for Master's pay accountability.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep the item deferred to December 2 due to the building outage and its informational status.
side_b_arguments: The Fuller Building remained without lights and air conditioning.
The item was originally scheduled as informational without a scheduled vote.
conflicts.resolution: Reconsideration passed 6-1, and the board voted 7-0 to place the item after Transportation.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/9/26
conflicts.issue: Secondary Magnet Express Bus Stops: Immediate 2027-28 Commitment vs 2026-27 Pilot Only
conflicts.summary: Board members split over whether to give conditional approval now to roll out express bus stops to all secondary magnets in 2027-28 (to give lottery families notice) or limit direction strictly to the 2026-27 pilot at DSA and Brogden DLI.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve planning for Phase 2 expansion to all secondary magnets in 2027-28 now (subject to later rollback if needed) so families know before magnet lotteries.
side_a_arguments: Notifying prospective 2027-28 lottery applicants in advance is fairer than announcing express stops after seats are accepted.
Rolling back from express stops to door-to-door is operationally easier than surprising families late.
conflicts.side_b_position: Separate out the 2026-27 pilot (DSA and Brogden DLI) and withhold any commitment on other secondary magnets until Q1 data is reviewed by the incoming board.
side_b_arguments: Data from the DSA/Brogden pilot will not exist until fall 2026, when four newly elected members take office.
Express stops carry equity risks that could deter lower-income families from secondary magnets and Growing Together programs.
conflicts.resolution: Consensus reached (thumbs up) to proceed with planning/communication for the 2026-27 DSA and Brogden DLI pilot while bringing comprehensive Q1 operational and equity data back in late October or early November 2026—before Showcase of Schools—so the new board can decide 2027-28 expansion.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/11/25
conflicts.issue: Scope of Mandatory Notification and SRO Separation in Law Enforcement Policy 5120
conflicts.summary: Board members debated how strictly to word parental/district notification mandates during law enforcement actions and whether School Resource Officer (SRO) provisions should remain in Policy 5120 or be separated.
conflicts.side_a_position: Preserve flexible 'should, whenever feasible' phrasing or examine all statutory edge cases before tightening language.
side_a_arguments: Legal and committee drafters sought careful alignment with state law and practical feasibility during active school emergencies.
conflicts.side_b_position: Mandate stronger enforceable 'shall, except in cases of emergency' protections, broaden public MOU posting, and pursue a standalone SRO policy.
side_b_arguments: Heightened federal immigration enforcement requires unambiguous, binding protections for students and families rather than discretionary language.
Separating SRO-specific governance from general law enforcement / ICE protocols prevents confusion and strengthens accountability.
conflicts.resolution: Consensus reached by amending Policy 5120 to 'shall, except in cases of emergency,' broadening MOU posting rules, adopting Policy 5120 immediately 7-0, and referring a standalone SRO policy to the January 22 Policy Committee.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting |
conflicts.issue: Sizing the 2026 School Bond and Potential Small-School Consolidation Amid County Capital Constraints
conflicts.summary: While DPS presented ~$965M in immediate FCA needs (~$2B long-term) and highlighted 13 under-enrolled elementary schools (<450 students), county leadership emphasized severe county revenue constraints ($11M sales tax shortfall, county hiring freezes, and >$2B competing 10-year CIP requests) requiring tough trade-offs on bond sizing and school footprint consolidation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Address comprehensive district facility equity, deferred maintenance (~$965M FCA), and modernizations across all campuses through a major 2026 bond while carefully studying 5 consolidation trade-up candidates through the CIP Task Force.
side_a_arguments: Every DPS campus deserves modernized learning environments after years of deferred maintenance.
Community trust requires transparent objective CIP Task Force evaluation before closing or consolidating small neighborhood elementary schools.
conflicts.side_b_position: Align DPS capital requests strictly with Durham County debt capacity, sales tax revenue pressures, and realistic project phasing, while pursuing consolidation efficiencies where elementary schools remain under 450 students.
side_b_arguments: Durham County faces an $11M sales tax shortfall, federal safety-net pressures, and over $2B in countywide capital demands requiring strict debt limits.
Operating 13 elementary schools below 450 students creates ongoing capital and operating inefficiencies unless consolidation or co-location options are weighed.
conflicts.resolution: No formal bond vote was taken; both boards agreed to add an extra Q1 2026 joint budget session before May 12 to coordinate capital and operating requests early.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/20/25
conflicts.issue: Mandatory ('Shall') vs. Permissive ('May') Physical Posting of Immigration Resolution in Schools
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed over whether the Immigration Safety and Privacy Resolution should mandate ('shall be posted') or permit ('may be posted') physical display in all school buildings.
conflicts.side_a_position: Mandate physical posting ('shall be posted') at schools so families and staff see visible institutional solidarity.
side_a_arguments: Visible signage reassures immigrant families and ensures school staff and visitors know district protections clearly.
conflicts.side_b_position: Use permissive language ('may be posted') rather than a rigid posting mandate.
side_b_arguments: Mandatory physical posters could invite vandalism, draw hostile attention, or create compliance burdens for principals when digital communication is safer and more effective.
conflicts.resolution: Emily Chávez agreed to amend the language to 'may be posted,' and the resolution passed unanimously 6-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session
conflicts.issue: 2025-2026 Master's Pay Eligibility Scope (5-1 Split)
conflicts.summary: Emily Chávez dissented (5-1) on limiting 2025-2026 Master's pay eligibility to classroom teachers and 11 school social workers rather than restoring full pre-2013 eligibility across instructional support roles.
conflicts.side_a_position: Restore Master's pay broadly across all licensed roles paid on the teacher schedule as existed prior to the 2013 state elimination.
side_a_arguments: Counselors, media coordinators, psychologists, and other Master's-prepared specialists were promised parity on the teacher pay schedule and remain excluded.
conflicts.side_b_position: Approve classroom teachers and 11 school social workers now within realistic FY25-26 budget capacity.
side_b_arguments: Expanding immediately beyond teachers and social workers without guaranteed county revenue creates unaffordable budget exposure given last year's $1.2M Master's pay shortfall.
conflicts.resolution: Approved 5-1 covering classroom teachers and 11 school social workers (contingent on funding).

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/13/25
conflicts.issue: Policy 7502 (Salary Administration & Employee Compensation) — Binding Experience Raises, Pay Schedule Merging, and Supplement Equity
conflicts.summary: During the 53-minute second reading of Policy 7502, board members disagreed over whether policy text stating 'intent of the board' creates an unsustainable fiscal promise on annual experience steps, how Crutchfield and HIL pay scales should be reconciled, and how to ensure parity between Arts and Extra-Duty supplements.
conflicts.side_a_position: Embed explicit policy commitments protecting annual experience-step progression, preventing arbitrary min/max placement penalties, and guaranteeing equitable treatment of Arts and extra-duty supplements.
side_a_arguments: Employees and union advocates (DAE/Christy Clen) have repeatedly cited classified pay compression and past pay-schedule discrepancies.
Without clear 'intent of the board' and supplement-parity language, workers risk losing expected step recognition during schedule transitions.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep Policy 7502 flexible enough not to legally bind future budgets beyond uncertain county and state appropriations while schedules are still being reconciled.
side_b_arguments: Enshrining annual step guarantees inside board policy risks creating unfunded mandates if state or county revenues fall short.
Technical placement rules and supplement structures require careful HR and legal review across both legacy and new compensation frameworks.
conflicts.resolution: No vote taken on second reading; staff and legal counsel were directed to revise Policy 7502 language and return it for further board review.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/9/25
conflicts.issue: Mandating Timing and Off-Site Format for a Budget 101 Community Forum in the 2025-26 Budget Calendar
conflicts.summary: Board members differed over whether to amend the formal 2025-26 budget calendar motion to lock in a pre-hearing Budget 101 community meeting at high school venues or pass the statutory deadline schedule cleanly.
conflicts.side_a_position: Pushed to embed an accessible Budget 101 community education meeting outside the Fuller Building—before Feb 20 (Chávez/Carda-Auten) or between Feb 20 and Mar 27 (Harrell-Goff)—so residents understand federal/state/local revenues before testifying.
side_a_arguments: Traditional hearings at Fuller Building draw low turnout because families lack accessible background on how school budgets work and cannot easily attend downtown board nights.
Providing infographics and plain-language budget briefings at Southern or Jordan High Schools prior to public hearings leads to more equitable community input.
conflicts.side_b_position: Argued the calendar vote only sets formal Policy 8100 benchmark deadlines and does not require voting on logistics or dates for supplemental community sessions.
side_b_arguments: Adding binding event logistics into the statutory budget calendar motion risked locking staff into unvetted dates and venues.
Supplemental community briefings can be directed operationally without amending the formal deadline calendar.
conflicts.resolution: Rogers withdrew her amended motion at 03:50:04, and the board passed a clean motion approving the benchmark budget timeline (7-0) while recording a formal staff follow-up directive to schedule a community budget meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/21/24
conflicts.issue: Motion to Table Master's Pay Expansion Motion Pending Budget and Audit Clarity
conflicts.summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter reported that 358 classroom teachers receiving Master's pay cost $2.517 million against a $1.259 million budget—creating a $1.258 million shortfall covered by withholding 15% of local department budgets—while adding social workers and other certified instructional staff would cost at least $272,000 more amid an incomplete FY24 audit. Emily Chávez moved (seconded by Wendell Tabb) to grant Master's pay per pre-2013 DPI standards for 2024-25 with back pay for certified teachers and instructional staff including social workers, instructional coaches, specialists, and coordinators. Bettina Umstead moved to table that motion until finance staff identified viable funding sources, seconded by Natalie Beyer, warning against unfunded commitments. Five board members voted Nay and only Umstead and Beyer voted Aye, defeating the tabling motion 2-5.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 2-5)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (2-5)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/7/24
conflicts.issue: Transportation Crisis Mitigation: Walk Zones, Express Stops, and Rotational Coverage vs. Contracting/Vans
conflicts.summary: Board members diverged sharply on which short-term and structural transportation tactics to pursue, splitting in an informal thumb poll over immediate Express Stops and expressing competing concerns over walk zones, rotational coverage, and private/church bus contracting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Reject rotational coverage and elementary walk zones; prioritize private contracting, additional non-CDL vans, and partnering with churches that own 16+ passenger buses.
side_a_arguments: Cutting scheduled bus days via rotational coverage or forcing elementary children to walk a mile in winter weather imposes unacceptable hardship.
DPS already uses private contractors and owns seven 7-passenger vans not requiring CDLs, while church buses >15 passengers are legally usable.
conflicts.side_b_position: Endorse advance-notice rotational coverage as the most equitable immediate bridge while carefully vetting walk zones, Express Stops, CDL incentives, and family opt-outs.
side_b_arguments: Without 31 needed drivers, failing to rotate uncovered routes leaves low-income and ESL families disproportionately stranded without notice.

Informal polling showed only 2 up, 3 down, and 1 middle on immediate Express Stops and mixed middle/down views on walk zones, prompting consensus to rule out bell-time changes and require community feedback and safety analysis before any formal vote.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote taken; informal board polling crossed off Tactic 3 (expanding bell times) and authorized rotational coverage plus further data on Tactics 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/7/24
conflicts.issue: Expanding 2024-25 Master's Pay Beyond Classroom Teachers Despite Existing Budget Deficit
conflicts.summary: Following Dr. Alvera Lesane's report that 358 classroom teachers already pushed Master's pay toward $1.8M+ against a $1.2M budget, board members split over whether DPS is obligated to absorb another ~$245k+ this year for social workers, coaches, and specialists.
conflicts.side_a_position: Cost out and pursue 2024-25 coverage for the ~35-38 excluded certified instructional staff (including 14 social workers) to repair broken trust.
side_a_arguments: Spring 2024 board discussions said 'teachers' broadly without limiting to classroom teachers of record.
Social workers serve hundreds of high-need students and suffered emotional whiplash from contradictory HR eligibility emails.
conflicts.side_b_position: Avoid raising false expectations of mid-year expansion when Master's pay is already over budget and sustainable funding is lacking.
side_b_arguments: Classroom teacher Master's pay already exceeded the $1.2M budget by roughly $600k+, and Wake County saw costs jump by millions.
Promising mid-year pay without an identified funding source risks repeating past fiscal crises; focus should include legislative advocacy to restore state Master's pay.
conflicts.resolution: Staff directed to bring exact cost estimates and potential budget offsets back in December while adding Master's pay to the legislative agenda.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
conflicts.issue: Immediate Authorization of Right-Sizing Consultant vs Reviewing Draft RFP First
conflicts.summary: Administration asked for early green-light support to hire a third-party right-sizing and consolidation consultant, while board members demanded to review a concrete RFP and board-engagement plan first.
conflicts.side_a_position: Require staff to bring a draft RFP with scope, optional plan, budget, and board engagement timeline before authorizing procurement.
side_a_arguments: Right-sizing and potential school consolidation carry major equity stakes and must explicitly incorporate Growing Together and public engagement.
conflicts.side_b_position: Seek early board backing to accelerate third-party facility utilization planning ahead of future bond cycles.
side_b_arguments: Declining enrollment and a $965M 10-year facilities backlog require timely outside analysis.
conflicts.resolution: Unanimous 7-0 directive instructing staff to bring the draft RFP to the June 25 regular meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/26/26
conflicts.issue: Capital Technology Lease ($2.82M Chromebooks & Interactive Displays) vs Facilities/Screen-Time Concerns
conflicts.summary: Public commenters and several board members questioned prioritizing $2.82M in leased Chromebooks and BrightLink replacements over HVAC repairs and screen-time limits.
conflicts.side_a_position: Scrutinize $2.8M technology spending relative to HVAC repairs, teacher pay, and childhood screen-time risks.
side_a_arguments: Voters and parents raised research linking heavy classroom screen time to declining literacy/math outcomes and asked whether all 17,173 Chromebooks and 1,786 displays are strictly needed.
conflicts.side_b_position: Fund multi-year leases to replace failing 13-year-old projectors and out-of-warranty Chromebooks to prevent instructional disruption and digital inequity.
side_b_arguments: NC law bars using capital outlay funds for employee salaries.

Chromebook repairs exceed $500,000 annually, 13-year-old BrightLink bulbs fail mid-lesson, and cutting 1:1 devices widens the digital divide for Black and brown students whose families can opt out online.
conflicts.resolution: Budget passed 5-0 including the $2.82M capital technology leases, paired with requests for future reporting on opt-out rates, classroom screen time, and instructional tech planning.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/12/26
conflicts.issue: Including Extra Duty Pay Increases and 3% Central Office Reductions in FY 2026-27 Budget Draft
conflicts.summary: Board members divided over whether to add an Extra Duty Pay increase (potentially funded via 3% Central Office cuts) into the Phase 2 budget proposal now or resolve school-level stipend inequities and payroll/comp-time compliance first.
conflicts.side_a_position: Include extra duty pay increases in the FY 2026-27 budget ask immediately to recognize specialists, coaches, and staff working beyond contract hours.
side_a_arguments: Extra duty staff and specialists repeatedly testified that stipend inequities and unpaid hours undermine retention.
Waiting another budget cycle delays relief for employees performing vital after-hours and extracurricular duties.
conflicts.side_b_position: Audit and standardize school-level stipend administration, payroll lines, and comp-time rules before committing recurring new dollars.
side_b_arguments: School-by-school inconsistencies and blurred comp-time versus paid-overtime practices mean extra money could reinforce inequities without clear payroll rules.
With tight county revenue projections, priority dollars are needed for the $19.22/hr living wage floor and core continuation costs.
conflicts.resolution: Reconsideration led by Emily Chávez reached only 3.5 informal support at [03:05:42], falling short of a board majority to alter the Phase 2 budget draft.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: 2026 General Obligation Bond Feasibility, LOBS Alternatives, and School Site Reuse vs. Consolidation
conflicts.summary: DPS operations staff outlined massive long-term capital needs including school consolidations and aging infrastructure, while County staff favored smaller LOBS borrowing over a 2026 GO Bond and County Commissioners pressed for adaptive reuse/teacher housing on surplus sites.
conflicts.side_a_position: Pursue bold capital investment to tackle a $965M+ M&R backlog and address under-enrolled aging elementary schools via consolidation and new construction.
side_a_arguments: DPS faces a $965M+ maintenance and repair backlog and 16 small schools needing long-term capacity solutions.
Board members emphasized failing HVAC systems and 60-to-75-year-old buildings requiring major modernization or consolidation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Prioritize finishing the 2022 bond projects and using incremental LOBS debt rather than a 2026 GO Bond, while exploring UNC DFI adaptive reuse for surplus sites.
side_b_arguments: Roughly $200M of the $460M 2022 bond has been spent so far, raising shovel-readiness questions alongside inflated construction and aluminum costs.

Commissioner Jacobs urged UNC School of Government/DFI partnerships for educator/affordable housing at Old Northern and the DSA campus rather than demolition; Umstead noted UNC SOG feasibility work is already underway.
conflicts.resolution: Informational joint discussion only; both boards deferred further capital and MOU planning to future budget and May joint discussions.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: FY 2026-27 County Tax Capacity vs. DPS Classified Wage Parity and Local Staffing Levels
conflicts.summary: County budget officials argued Durham County is at a fiscal inflection point limiting major new DPS increases without unpopular tax hikes, while DPS Board members defended living-wage parity ($19.22/hr), facility repairs, and local positions amid rising charter pass-through costs.
conflicts.side_a_position: County revenues cannot sustain large annual funding deltas without further property tax increases, requiring scrutiny of DPS local position growth (24%) amid declining ADM (~29,000).
side_a_arguments: County faces only $8.7M in natural revenue growth against $13.5M in baseline expenditure increases before any DPS or county staff raises.
Sales tax growth flattened (+$770K), federal ARPA/SNAP dollars are expiring, and residents have absorbed back-to-back 6% property tax rate increases.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain county-matched living wages ($19.22/hr), fix failing school HVAC systems, and recognize that $51M in local funding flows out to charter schools.
side_b_arguments: Board members Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten argued DPS cannot retain classified staff without matching county wage floors and addressing inflation.
DPS has already stabilized its finances, ended lapsed-salary dependency, and absorbed rising charter school tuition shares.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote taken; presentations set the framework for April-June County and DPS budget deliberations.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/26
conflicts.issue: $4.6M/Year Student Device Model, Screen-Time Guardrails, and Work Session Action Authority
conflicts.summary: Board members differed sharply over the urgency and cost of a $23M five-year student device refresh, leading to a unanimous roll-call vote to table the plan for stronger academic and screen-time guardrails.
conflicts.side_a_position: Delay approval pending instructional evidence, screen-time limits, cost reductions, and compliance with Policy 2235.
side_a_arguments: Sustaining 1:1 devices at $4.6M/year consumes scarce capital and local funds without clear proof of academic return on investment.
Elementary screen-time usage and instructional guidelines should precede multi-year hardware commitments, and Policy 2235 bars final action at a work session.
conflicts.side_b_position: Treat student devices as essential academic and testing infrastructure requiring predictable refresh funding.
side_b_arguments: Modern curriculum, state testing, and classroom instruction depend on reliable devices without aging hardware failures.
conflicts.resolution: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved (seconded by Emily Chávez) to table the Student Device Model and refer it to a future work session and subsequent regular board meeting; passed unanimously on roll call.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/15/26
conflicts.issue: Discipline Data Gaps, Pre-K Suspensions, and Falling Panorama Survey Participation
conflicts.summary: While administration highlighted a 29%-30% drop in overall discipline incidents, public commenters and board scrutiny surfaced unresolved gaps in Pre-K suspension tracking, opt-in survey decline (90% to 60%), and EC restorative implementation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Address gaps in Pre-K suspension data tracking, restore Panorama student/family survey participation, and verify restorative compliance.
side_a_arguments: Opt-in rules cut Panorama survey participation from 90% to 60%, weakening school climate diagnostics.
Public testimony and board review noted Pre-K suspensions lack dedicated data tracking even as the district partners with Duke Children's Law Clinic on restorative discipline.
conflicts.side_b_position: Build on the 29% year-over-year and 30% first-quarter incident reductions through continued RPC/STS support and Code of Conduct implementation.
side_b_arguments: District-wide discipline data demonstrates measurable reductions in incidents under current Priority 2 restorative initiatives.
conflicts.resolution: Informational work session update; follow-up items assigned for continued Code of Conduct and discipline reporting ahead of Policy Committee work.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/20/25
conflicts.issue: Middle School Cell Phone Rules: Bell-to-Bell Ban vs. Lunchtime Access in Policy 4318
conflicts.summary: Following the Policy Committee's draft favoring a strict bell-to-bell ban for elementary and middle schools, a majority of the full board amended Policy 4318 to allow middle school students phone access during lunch.
conflicts.side_a_position: Maintain a full bell-to-bell wireless device prohibition for middle school students (consistent with Policy Committee recommendation).
side_a_arguments: Research and educator feedback indicate lunchtime phone use fuels cyberbullying, social conflict, and distraction back into afternoon classes.
conflicts.side_b_position: Allow middle school students to access phones during lunch alongside high schoolers.
side_b_arguments: Aligning middle and high school rules avoids an abrupt mid-year enforcement shock on January 1 and allows families a smoother transition.
Consistent secondary-level rules give principals clearer operational expectations during non-instructional lunch periods.
conflicts.resolution: Policy 4318 was amended to permit middle school phone access during lunch while prohibiting class-change use and smart glasses, passing 6-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 9/11/25
conflicts.issue: Capping Mechanics and Farmers Bank School Checking Accounts at 'Up to Six'
conflicts.summary: During approval of the district's banking migration to JP Morgan Chase, debate centered on whether limiting Mechanics and Farmers Bank retention to 'up to six' schools unfairly restricted other principals from partnering with Durham's historic Black-owned bank.
conflicts.side_a_position: Keep the motion strictly framed as 'up to six' Mechanics and Farmers school accounts while migrating the remaining 51 schools and central funds to JP Morgan Chase.
side_a_arguments: Consolidating accounts at JP Morgan Chase captures $600,000+ in annual interest, waives fees above $2.5M combined balances, and simplifies central accounting.
Future requests from additional principals to bank with Mechanics and Farmers can always return to the board separately.
conflicts.side_b_position: Avoid locking out additional principals who may wish to bank with Mechanics and Farmers Bank, or clarify how new M&F partnerships could be approved.
side_b_arguments: Durham Public Schools has a longstanding community partnership with Mechanics and Farmers Bank that principals should not be automatically barred from joining.
conflicts.resolution: Motion carried 5-1 as written ('up to six'), with CFO Jeremy Teter confirming that any future school requests to join or transition could be brought back to the board.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 8/28/25
conflicts.issue: Formal Board Extension vs. Informal Rolling Consideration of August 31 Policy Portal Deadline
conflicts.summary: Board members differed briefly on whether extending the Policy Committee's August 31 submission deadline required formal board action and re-advertising, or whether the committee could simply consider early September submissions under rolling intake.
conflicts.side_a_position: Allow the Policy Committee to consider submissions arriving before its September 18 meeting informally without formally altering the policy deadline or redoing social media posts.
side_a_arguments: Policy 2231 already allows rolling submissions, so formally extending the initial cutoff could unnecessarily trigger duplicate outreach.
conflicts.side_b_position: Formally vote to extend the initial priority deadline by one week to September 7 and publish updated notices.
side_b_arguments: Because the bilingual portal and Spark newsletter only publicized the August 31 date days earlier, an official extension notifies the public clearly that early-September proposals count toward 2025-26 prioritization.
conflicts.resolution: Natalie Beyer moved and Emily Chávez seconded extending the deadline to September 7, passing 7-0 with updated communications from Public Affairs.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/14/25
conflicts.issue: Accelerated February Budget Deadline vs. Waiting for State and County Budget Clarity
conflicts.summary: Board members debated whether adopting the FY 2026-27 district budget ask by the end of February—more than two months before the May 15 statutory deadline—risked locking DPS into underfunded requests before the General Assembly acts or competing county expansion requests emerge.
conflicts.side_a_position: Hold flexibility beyond February and explicitly label any February submission an 'initial' or 'projected' funding request.
side_a_arguments: State budget delays leave key teacher and classified cost variables unresolved in February.
Locking in a number too early could leave DPS short relative to Sheriff, Durham Tech, or other competing county requests.
conflicts.side_b_position: Adopt an aggressive early timeline targeting late-February approval and add a standalone budget public hearing date.
side_b_arguments: County commissioners previously finalized budget presentations before receiving DPS numbers; hitting March 1 ensures DPS priorities are on the county manager's table from day one.
Planning early preserves room to revise if state or fiscal circumstances change.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved through a friendly amendment replacing final adoption language with 'authorize initial funding request to county commissioners,' passing 6-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Policy 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion) Timing and Safeguards
conflicts.summary: Board members split over whether to adopt the revised Policy 4326 immediately or hold it for stronger limits on seclusion and demographic data reporting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Require stronger seclusion limits, parent-notification timelines, and disaggregated data reporting before finalizing policy language.
side_a_arguments: Seclusion and restraint disproportionately affect students with disabilities and Black and brown students, requiring explicit demographic data reporting.
Delaying finalization or immediately committing to Policy Committee revisions protects vulnerable students.
conflicts.side_b_position: Pass the baseline policy update now to align with state training rules without holding up Policies 3520 and 7800.
side_b_arguments: Baseline policy language is needed promptly so district training and compliance remain current for the upcoming school year.
Further refinements can be processed systematically through the Policy Committee.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved via Carda-Auten's compromise amendment passing the baseline policy 7-0 while simultaneously referring Policy 4326 back to the Policy Committee for revisions.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/13/25
conflicts.issue: Equity Impacts of Fee-Based Summer Camps Following ESSER Expiration
conflicts.summary: After pulling Summer Programs from the Consent Agenda, board members questioned shifting three enrichment camps to a fee-based model as ESSER pandemic funds ended, raising access barriers for low-income families.
conflicts.side_a_position: Questioned charging tuition fees for three summer camps and demanded accountability metrics to ensure low-income students are not excluded from summer enrichment.
side_a_arguments: Fee-based programs risk creating a two-tier summer experience when federal ESSER funding expires.
Families without discretionary income rely on DPS summer camps for safe enrichment and academic continuity.
conflicts.side_b_position: Administration and fiscal-minded members noted the district still preserves targeted free academic camps while using fees only to sustain optional enrichment camps without pandemic funding.
side_b_arguments: Ending ESSER grants leaves no dedicated recurring general-fund dollars to subsidize every optional camp.
Targeted academic recovery camps remain free for qualifying students with highest need.
conflicts.resolution: Board directed administration to conduct and report a post-summer demographic, scholarship, and student outcome audit.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 10/10/24
conflicts.issue: Classified Salary Schedule Revisions, Live Spreadsheet Edits, and Retro Pay Implementation
conflicts.summary: Public testimony from DAE physical therapist Christy Clem triggered sharp board questioning of HR and legal counsel over unannounced edits to live Google Doc salary scales, temporary removal of scales from the website, and delayed or omitted classified retro pay under the 'higher of last year + 3% or new scale' policy.
conflicts.side_a_position: Unannounced live edits, missing website scales, and unfulfilled retro pay promises represent ongoing breaches of employee trust requiring locked documentation and transparent fixes.
side_a_arguments: Watching a consultant adjust pay numbers on a live Google Doc after board adoption eroded confidence that adopted pay scales were authoritative.
Employees received no retro pay for the 'higher of' option, experienced up to multi-week HR email delays, and got contradictory Hurricane Helene workday directives.
conflicts.side_b_position: Spreadsheet adjustments reflected routine post-vote error cleanup rather than intentional deception, and staff are actively working through hundreds of individual payroll tickets.
side_b_arguments: Chief Legal Officer Tanya Giovanni explained consultants corrected minor formula errors without changing core adopted pay logic and re-uploaded scales once reviewed.
HR and finance faced severe backlog volume and legacy payroll system limitations while working to audit individual Master's, EC, and classified retro inquiries.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote; board members directed staff to replace live editable Google Docs with locked, date-stamped PDFs and clarify written communication on retro pay and pay-scale updates.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Work Session | 9/12/24
conflicts.issue: Omission of Conflict-of-Interest Disclosures and Background Screening Edits in Board Training RFP
conflicts.summary: During consideration of the Request for Proposals for board training and consultation, Natalie Beyer objected that edits she submitted—regarding disclosing consultants' prior relationships with individual board members and background concerns—were omitted from the committee draft.
conflicts.side_a_position: Require RFP applicants to disclose existing relationships with specific board members and address concerns regarding consultants' backgrounds.
side_a_arguments: Disclosing existing relationships between prospective consultants and individual board members is important for transparency during selection.
Consultants' backgrounds should be vetted as part of the board training RFP criteria.
conflicts.side_b_position: Advance the committee-drafted RFP reviewed by the board attorney for immediate approval.
side_b_arguments: All board members had an opportunity to submit feedback that was reviewed with counsel prior to public posting.
conflicts.resolution: Joy Harrell-Goff moved and Emily Chávez seconded adopting the RFP as posted; Natalie Beyer voiced her concerns on the record before the digest's middle truncation cut off the concluding vote.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
conflicts.issue: Splitting Substitute Teacher Hourly Methodology From Proposed Rate Increase
conflicts.summary: Administration proposed simultaneously moving substitutes to hourly pay and increasing hourly rates, drawing pushback over raising substitute pay while classified staff raises remained stalled by the state budget.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve only the structural shift to hourly pay methodology now and defer substitute rate increases until fall alongside classified salary scales.
side_a_arguments: Raising substitute pay before classified employees receive raises and before state appropriations are finalized sends the wrong priority signal.
Budget certainty is needed before committing recurring compensation increases.
conflicts.side_b_position: Original staff recommendation paired hourly methodology with $18/$19.40 hourly rate increases to strengthen substitute fill rates.
side_b_arguments: Competitive substitute pay addresses classroom coverage shortages alongside moving away from flat daily rates.
conflicts.resolution: The board unanimously voted 7-0 to approve only the hourly pay methodology for 2026-27 and bring rate adjustments back in fall with classified salary scales.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
conflicts.issue: Allocating Coordinator/Director Raises at 3% vs 5% to Reallocate $263k to Lower Wage Grades
conflicts.summary: During the budget update, board members debated whether to cap coordinator and director salary increases at 3% instead of 5% so roughly $263,000 could be shifted to lower-paid classified staff.
conflicts.side_a_position: Stress-test reducing coordinator/director raises from 5% to 3% to free $263,000 for lower-paid workers.
side_a_arguments: Prioritizes limited expansion dollars for front-line and lower-wage staff facing higher cost-of-living burdens.
conflicts.side_b_position: Preserve uniform scale adjustments and avoid worsening salary compression among mid-level administrators.
side_b_arguments: Cutting percentage increases for coordinators creates compression against supervised roles and undermines retention.
conflicts.resolution: Informational budget stress-test; CFO Teeter noted options would be further analyzed alongside final state appropriations.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 5/28/26
conflicts.issue: Scheduling Second Reading of Policy 8600 (Work Session vs Monthly Meeting)
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed briefly over whether to waive work-session rules to adopt Policy 8600 on second reading at the June 9 work session or hold final action for the June 25 regular monthly meeting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Bring Policy 8600 back to the June 9 work session (with a policy waiver if needed) to avoid delay.
side_a_arguments: Earlier review keeps momentum behind the Meet and Confer transparency milestone.
conflicts.side_b_position: Send Policy 8600 to the June 25 regular monthly meeting without waiving the work-session discussion policy.
side_b_arguments: Work sessions should stay focused on discussion while final policy action occurs at regular monthly meetings.
Policy 8600 takes effect July 1, and CFO Teeter confirmed June 25 adoption poses no operational problem.
conflicts.resolution: Emily Chávez modified her motion to send Policy 8600 to the June 25 monthly meeting for second read, passing unanimously 7-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/14/26
conflicts.issue: Extent of PreK-5 Suspension Prohibitions and Staffing Support Under Policy 4301
conflicts.summary: Members agreed on expanding restorative practices in Policy 4301 but differed on whether to ban Level 1B/all suspensions up through Grade 3 or Grade 5 immediately given budget and staffing cuts.
conflicts.side_a_position: Prohibit Level 1B suspensions (disrespect/non-compliance) for young students, include PreK-3 explicitly, and expand supervisor/EC checks across K-5.
side_a_arguments: Thirty kindergarteners were already suspended this year, disproportionately Black and disabled students.
