Exclusionary discipline worsens chronic absenteeism and causes developmental harm.
conflicts.side_b_position: Start with PreK-2 limits, preserve principal/supervisor discretion for serious safety issues, and ensure staff capacity before banning higher grades.
side_b_arguments: Grades 3-5 have New Directions support while K-2 does not, and staffing cuts under an uncertain county/state budget strain school-level capacity.
Restorative practices must be taught proactively rather than imposed without resources late in the school year.
conflicts.resolution: Approved on first read 6-0 directing staff to gather additional counselor, teacher, and family input ahead of June second reading.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/23/26
conflicts.issue: Legislative Priorities Framing on School Vouchers and Charter Expansion
conflicts.summary: Board members debated how forcefully to frame opposition to private school vouchers and charter school expansion while maintaining coalition appeal with rural North Carolina school districts.
conflicts.side_a_position: Use 'school vouchers' instead of 'opportunity scholarships', standardize behind a full moratorium, and avoid wording implying support for charter expansion.
side_a_arguments: 'Opportunity scholarships' sanitizes public subsidies for private schools.
Charter study wording must not sound like DPS endorses expanding single-operator charter chains.
conflicts.side_b_position: Use statutory/NCSBA terminology ('opportunity scholarships', pause/phase-out, accountability & transparency) to maximize coalition reach with rural boards.
side_b_arguments: Focusing on public accountability and adequate K-12 funding attracts non-traditional rural partners.
Phasing out recognizes lower-income families currently relying on scholarships while transitioning back.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted 7-0 keeping NCSBA-consistent 'opportunity scholarship' phrasing for coalition alignment while revising the charter bullet to 'ensure if expansion is necessary, it is done responsibly'.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/23/26
conflicts.issue: Policy 5120 Federal Immigration Enforcement Entry & Main-Office Protocol (F1 & F2)
conflicts.summary: Members and district safety leadership debated whether Policy 5120 Section F1 should remove 'report to the school's main office' and instruct principals to ask unannounced immigration officers to wait outside or in the main office.
conflicts.side_a_position: Remove 'report to the school's main office' from F1 so policy clearly expects contact with the Superintendent's office first, and require principals in F2 to ask agents to wait outside or in the main office.
side_a_arguments: Telling agents to contact central office and simultaneously report to a school's main office contradicts itself.
Clear written boundaries protect students and limit campus disruption while central legal counsel verifies judicial warrants.
conflicts.side_b_position: Preserve practical main-office containment without putting unarmed school principals in confrontational standoffs telling federal agents to leave.
side_b_arguments: Executive Director Miklo Bynum and Dr. Lewis warned agents arrive already inside buildings in uniform and directing principals to turn them away risks resist-delay-obstruct liability.
conflicts.resolution: Compromise amendments adopted 7-0: F1 directs officers to contact the Superintendent's office or district administrators before visiting, while F2 directs principals at the site to ask officers to wait outside or in the main office while notifying district leadership.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/9/26
conflicts.issue: International Teacher J-1 to H-1B Visa Renewal Policy and Retention Exemptions
conflicts.summary: Following public outcry over Murray Massenberg art teacher Elvin Herrera, board members questioned administration's refusal to pursue H-1B visa transitions for J-1 international teachers.
conflicts.side_a_position: Question why pandemic-era H-1B exceptions ended without board notice and explore retention pathways for exemplary international teachers.
side_a_arguments: DPS relies on over 300 international educators across dual-language, IB, ESL, and hard-to-staff subjects, and charter schools are hiring them away.
Board members were not consulted when HR shifted back from pandemic-era visa extensions.
conflicts.side_b_position: Standard practice always limited J-1 cultural exchange contracts to 3+2 years with mandatory two-year home residency, and pandemic H-1Bs were strictly temporary exceptions.
side_b_arguments: Participants and partner agencies explicitly contract under J-1 cultural exchange rules rather than permanent H-1B immigration tracks.
No board policy was changed; administration simply resumed standard compliance.
conflicts.resolution: Board majority gave thumbs-up consensus to schedule a deeper future board briefing and discussion on international teacher visa policies.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/11/25
conflicts.issue: Immediate Termination vs. Delayed ROI Review of SiteLogic Energy Management Contract
conflicts.summary: Board members split over whether to terminate SiteLogic's energy management contract immediately alongside two underperforming vendor contracts or pause until January to evaluate sustainability ROI and historical data.
conflicts.side_a_position: Defer terminating SiteLogic until staff brings an ROI and sustainability analysis in January.
side_a_arguments: Wanted administration to present cost-benefit data and clarity on prior energy savings and district sustainability commitments before cutting the vendor.
conflicts.side_b_position: Terminate the SiteLogic contract immediately while bringing a broader sustainability and climate action plan review in January.
side_b_arguments: The district faces a $4.7 million charter school shortfall and urgent budget constraints requiring immediate expenditure cuts.
Student advocates and board members noted SiteLogic's public energy dashboard had not been updated since April 2023, undermining confidence in active contract value.
conflicts.resolution: Resolved when Natalie Beyer amended her motion to terminate SiteLogic immediately alongside B&B Triangle Enterprises and BJNL Painting while directing a January sustainability report, passing 7-0.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/11/25
conflicts.issue: Naloxone Policy 5023 Facility Coverage, Full-Time Staff Requirement, and Good Samaritan Liability
conflicts.summary: Members debated operational details of Policy 5023 regarding which facilities must stock Naloxone, whether trained staff minimums must specify full-time employees, and phrasing that could restrict emergency responders.
conflicts.side_a_position: Require full-time staff certification at sites to guarantee daytime coverage and retain explicit trained-personnel framing.
side_a_arguments: Full-time staff requirement ensures trained staff are reliably on site rather than part-time or itinerant personnel.
conflicts.side_b_position: Cover all DPS buildings (not just schools), keep staffing requirements flexible for principals excluding nurses/SROs, and remove 'only' trained language.
side_b_arguments: Principals need flexibility in selecting three trained staff per building without rigid full-time mandates.
Removing 'only' prevents chilling anyone from administering life-saving Naloxone in an emergency.
conflicts.resolution: Board reached 7-0 first-reading consensus expanding to all DPS buildings, requiring >=2 devices and >=3 trained staff (excluding nurses/SROs) without a rigid full-time clause, and removing 'only.'

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/6/25
conflicts.issue: Policy 4318 Middle School Phone Access, Smart Devices, and Language Access
conflicts.summary: Board members split during first reading over whether middle school students should face an all-day bell-to-bell cell phone ban or be allowed device access at lunch, as well as how to regulate smartwatches and smart glasses.
conflicts.side_a_position: Apply a full bell-to-bell ban for middle schoolers and explicitly restrict smartwatches/smart glasses to prevent classroom and hallway disruption.
side_a_arguments: Educators and parents expressed concern that lunch-period access drives hallway conflicts, social media drama, and enforcement confusion.
conflicts.side_b_position: Permit middle school lunchtime access for continuity with high schools while carefully verifying medical/IEP accommodations for smart glasses and multilingual outreach.
side_b_arguments: Allowing lunch access provides consistency across secondary grades during the mid-year transition.
Policies must not penalize students needing smart glasses for IEP/504 accessibility or families needing Spanish communication.
conflicts.resolution: Approved first reading 7-0 and referred all board questions to the November 10 Policy Committee for revision before second reading.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/6/25
conflicts.issue: Duration and Scope of $675,000 CDW Chromebook Repair Contract Ahead of 1:1 Refresh Plan
conflicts.summary: Board members questioned signing a full-year not-to-exceed $675,000 Chromebook repair contract with CDW Government LLC prior to reviewing the district's long-term 1:1 device refresh and grade-band strategy.
conflicts.side_a_position: Questioned committing to a full-year $675,000 repair contract without first aligning repair spending to the forthcoming 1:1 refresh plan.
side_a_arguments: Unclear whether the district needs a full year of external repairs if elementary or middle school 1:1 take-home models shift in spring.
conflicts.side_b_position: Approve the CDW repair contract up to $675,000 now as a not-to-exceed ceiling so broken devices are promptly restored for instruction and testing.
side_b_arguments: Not-to-exceed spending caps protect the budget while preventing instructional disruption from damaged devices already in circulation.
conflicts.resolution: Contract was pulled from consent, re-uploaded with corrected wording, and approved unanimously as a not-to-exceed $675,000 ceiling.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting
conflicts.issue: Election of Board Chair - Nomination of Millicent Rogers
conflicts.summary: Outgoing Chair Millicent Rogers opened the organizational session at 00:00:39 and turned the floor over to Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis at 00:01:02 to conduct the election of the Board Chair for 2025-2026. Both Millicent Rogers (00:01:56) and Bettina Umstead (00:02:28) were placed in nomination by colleagues. Dr. Lewis called for a vote on the first nomination, Millicent Rogers, at 00:02:38. The nomination received two votes in favor and four opposed, falling short of the majority needed to re-elect Rogers as Chair.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 2-4)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (2-4)

conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education & Durham County Board of Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
conflicts.issue: FY25-26 Funding Gap Between DPS Budget Request and County Manager's Recommended Allocation
conflicts.summary: DPS officials and county leaders differed in fiscal framing over the $5.6M operating gap and $2M annual capital outlay gap between DPS's budget request ($15.9M operating expansion, $8M capital) and County Manager Claudia Hager's recommended $10.35M operating expansion and $6M capital (+ $10M multi-year CIP reserve).
conflicts.side_a_position: Urge county funding closer to DPS's $15.9M operating and $8M capital request to preserve student-facing priorities, teacher/staff investments, and ongoing maintenance.
side_a_arguments: DPS has already absorbed $30M+ in prior shortfall fixes and eliminated 27 central office positions to stabilize finances.
A $5.6M operating shortfall and $2M capital reduction force hard trade-offs on Master's pay, bus driver retention, EC funding, and school upkeep amid $4M federal Medicaid risks.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold DPS FY25-26 expansion to $10.35M operating and $6M annual capital (+$10M CIP reserve) given countywide fiscal constraints.
side_b_arguments: Slowing sales tax collections and a 60% property revaluation already require a 3.5-cent tax increase above the 51.92-cent revenue-neutral rate.
DPS remains the county's top budget recipient at $224M total allocation plus dedicated multi-year CIP reserve planning for ~$2B in long-term facility needs.
conflicts.resolution: Intergovernmental budget dialogue only (no formal vote); County Commissioners proceeded toward their June 9 budget adoption while DPS recalibrated priorities at its May 22 and June 26 meetings.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Policy 2310 Public Comment 30-Minute Cap Enforcement vs. Waiver
conflicts.summary: With 48 speakers signed up, Chair Millicent Rogers initially prepared to enforce the 30-minute public comment limit, prompting pushback from members who moved to waive the cap so everyone could speak.
conflicts.side_a_position: Waive Policy 2310's 30-minute cap and allow all 48 registered speakers one minute each.
side_a_arguments: Community members and staff waited in person during a pivotal budget night and should not be silenced by procedural time caps.
conflicts.side_b_position: Initially enforce Policy 2310's 30-minute limit to keep the meeting on schedule.
side_b_arguments: Long public comment periods delay substantive budget and RIF deliberations late into the evening.
conflicts.resolution: Board voted unanimously 7-0 to waive Policy 2310's 30-minute limit for the evening.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
conflicts.issue: Amendment to Policy 7215: Raise ERO Threshold from 6% to 20%
conflicts.summary: At 04:21:48, Jessica Carda-Auten moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded an amendment to replace the proposed 6% membership threshold for Employee Representative Organizations (EROs) with 20%. Supporters argued a 20% threshold avoided splintering worker representation across tiny groups while giving recognized organizations credible standing with the superintendent, whereas opponents backed the administration's 6% floor to preserve broad inclusion and avoid an exclusive threshold seen as biased toward DAE. Following the unanimous cloture vote, Wendell Tabb called the roll between 05:04:28 and 05:04:55. Harrell-Goff, Chávez, and Carda-Auten voted Aye, while Beyer, Umstead, Rogers, and Tabb voted Nay, defeating the amendment 3-4.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 3-4)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (3-4)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/26/26
conflicts.issue: Flat 12.08% vs Graduated Classified Pay Scale Raise Distribution
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed philosophically over applying a flat 12.08% raise across all classified steps versus graduating percentages downward for senior central administrators.
conflicts.side_a_position: Explore a graduated raise model awarding 12% to lower-paid staff and smaller percentages at the coordinator-and-above tiers.
side_a_arguments: A uniform 12% raise grants roughly $19,000 to a step-zero assistant superintendent versus $4,336 to a transportation safety assistant.
Equity requires lifting workers at the bottom of the wage scale proportionally more.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain uniform 12.08% modeling in the county request to avoid pay compression and protect upward career incentives.
side_b_arguments: Trimming percentages at upper tiers worsens salary compression between supervisors and staff and impacts employees nearing retirement.
Final salary-scale adjustments should wait until Durham County announces actual June funding.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the full budget request 5-0 while CFO Jeremy Teeter agreed to partner with the board to revisit distribution philosophy once final county appropriations arrive in June.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Budget Hearing | 3/5/26
conflicts.issue: Classified Wage Levels, Custodian Overtime/80-Hour Caps, and OT/PT Assistant Inclusion Amid County Revenue Limits
conflicts.summary: While no split votes occurred during the public hearing, speakers and board members surfaced a sharp policy tension between employee demands for comprehensive classified pay, custodial workload reform, and COTA/PTA inclusion versus Durham County's warning of constrained tax capacity.
conflicts.side_a_position: Substantially exceed a 5% baseline raise by eliminating custodian 80-hour caps/unpaid overtime, including OT/PT assistants in salary realignment, and matching county/regional living wages.
side_a_arguments: Custodians testified they are capped at 80 hours while pressured to finish excessive workloads, forcing unpaid labor at poverty-level wages.
EC instructional assistants earning ~$28,000 and therapists/assistants warned that excluding COTAs/PTAs or limiting raises to 5% will worsen vacancies and turnover.
conflicts.side_b_position: Balance classified compensation priorities against Durham County's tight fiscal outlook, continuation cost pressures, and competing capital/HVAC needs.
side_b_arguments: CFO Jeremy Teter noted the draft already seeks $16M in current expense and $3.7M in capital outlay amid state budget uncertainty and a 5% state raise assumption.
Board members acknowledged County Manager Hager's sobering fiscal forecast requires careful prioritization between starting wages, compression, EC funding, and 60-year-old facilities.
conflicts.resolution: Testimony and board reflections were carried forward into the March 12 work session budget simulator and Phase 2 draft revisions.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/26
conflicts.issue: Structure and Cost of DAE Meet & Confer Classified Pay Proposal ($29.5M)
conflicts.summary: During the budget update, CFO Jeremy Teter and Board member Natalie Beyer challenged the equity and fiscal structure of DAE's $22/hr plus 0.75% step proposal estimated at $29.5M.
conflicts.side_a_position: Critique DAE's $22/hr proposal excluding administrators as fiscally unsustainable and inequitable in structure.
side_a_arguments: Pricing the proposal at $29.5M far exceeds foreseeable local county revenue capacity alongside $7.2M in state losses and $6.6M in charter expansion.
Both Teter and Beyer described aspects of the proposal's exclusion of administrators as 'arbitrary and capricious.'
conflicts.side_b_position: Continue exploring aggressive classified wage scenarios that lift lowest-paid workers and address compression for future simulator iterations.
side_b_arguments: Board follow-up directives asked staff to model aggressive starting-wage scenarios alongside step/compression options and clarify stipends vs. supplements.
conflicts.resolution: Staff incorporated follow-up compensation modeling directives into the Phase 1 and Phase 2 budget simulator work.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 10/7/25
conflicts.issue: Day-User Chromebook Restrictions for Grades 6-12 and Technology Fee Equity
conflicts.summary: Board members and the student representative pushed back strongly against IT and academic leadership's plan to move middle schools to a 'day-user' model in January and consider extending it to high schools, as well as inconsistent enforcement of the district technology fee.
conflicts.side_a_position: Transition grades 6-8 to a day-user model in January (with optional check-out for home needs) and study a day-user approach for grades 9-12 to curb heavy device losses.
side_a_arguments: Middle and high schools drove the vast majority of nearly 5,000 initially unreconciled Chromebooks, whereas K-5 day-user schools kept losses minimal.
Middle school principals actively requested moving to a day-user model to improve asset accountability.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject day-user take-home barriers for grades 6-12 (especially high school) and guarantee zero students are denied devices over unpaid technology fees.
side_b_arguments: Restricting take-home laptops undermines digital literacy, dual enrollment, homework completion, and college applications for families without home computers.
Sixth-grade families and low-income students are unfairly penalized for district inventory gaps and uneven school-level fee enforcement.
conflicts.resolution: Board approved the 2,000-device purchase 7-0 while logging follow-up directives requiring staff to detail how any day-user policy protects equity, digital textbooks, and home access before bringing a comprehensive 1:1 plan back by March.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting
conflicts.issue: Board Chair and Vice Chair Leadership Elections (2025-2026)
conflicts.summary: The six present board members divided over retaining outgoing Chair Millicent Rogers as Chair (failing 2-4) and subsequently split 3-3 before electing Rogers 4-2 as Vice Chair over Joy Harrell-Goff.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support Bettina Umstead for Chair and Millicent Rogers for Vice Chair.
side_a_arguments: Transitioning the gavel to Bettina Umstead achieved unanimous 6-0 board consensus after Rogers's Chair bid fell short 2-4.
Retaining outgoing Chair Rogers in the Vice Chair slot preserved leadership continuity by a 4-2 majority on the re-vote.
conflicts.side_b_position: Initially support Millicent Rogers for Chair (2 votes) or Joy Harrell-Goff for Vice Chair (3 votes initially, 2 on re-vote).
side_b_arguments: Three members initially backed Harrell-Goff for Vice Chair, resulting in a 3-3 deadlock requiring legal guidance for a show-of-hands re-vote.
conflicts.resolution: Bettina Umstead was unanimously elected Chair 6-0, and Millicent Rogers won the Vice Chair re-vote 4-2 over Joy Harrell-Goff.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Immediate $200/Month Bus Monitor Supplement vs. Awaiting State Budget and Classified Pay Study
conflicts.summary: During the budget prioritization update, members disagreed over whether to commit ~$140,000 immediately for a $200/month bus monitor weather/retention supplement or preserve flexible funds until state action and a broader classified salary study.
conflicts.side_a_position: Fund the $200/month bus monitor supplement now alongside the bus driver supplement.
side_a_arguments: Bus monitors work alongside bus drivers on the same routes and face the same weather-related pay interruptions and retention challenges.
Waiting months leaves low-paid classified transportation staff behind.
conflicts.side_b_position: Hold remaining flexible funds pending state legislative budget numbers and a comprehensive classified pay study.
side_b_arguments: Committing recurring local expansion dollars piecemeal before seeing the state budget risks exacerbating mid-year shortfalls or salary compression.
A systematic classified compensation review ensures equitable alignment across job groups.
conflicts.resolution: Informational budget discussion only; no final allocation vote was taken at the June 26 meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session
conflicts.issue: Policy 7502 Extra-Duty Pay During Regular School Hours
conflicts.summary: Board members debated whether Policy 7502's restriction against double-compensation/extra-duty pay during regular contracted school hours unfairly penalizes teachers covering classes or duties during planning periods.
conflicts.side_a_position: Preserve flexibility to compensate staff when taking on extra instructional coverage during the school day.
side_a_arguments: Staff routinely give up planning periods or perform additional duties due to substitute shortages and deserve fair recognition.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain strict payroll guardrails barring overlapping pay during contracted hours unless specifically structured.
side_b_arguments: Clear boundaries are essential to satisfy audit rules and prevent improper double-compensation flagged in prior payroll reviews.
conflicts.resolution: Policy 7502 advanced on first reading 6-0 for June 10 second reading with clarifying language requested from HR.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/6/25
conflicts.issue: School Showcase Selection and Racial/EC Discipline Disparities in Strategic Plan Priority 2 Report
conflicts.summary: Joy Harrell-Goff challenged district leadership for selecting Durham School of the Arts—one of DPS's least diverse schools—to model student-belonging gains while Black, Hispanic, and Exceptional Children students continue to experience disproportionate short-term suspensions.
conflicts.side_a_position: Critiqued showcasing DSA as unrepresentative of districtwide equity challenges and pressed for centering schools most impacted by suspension disparities during Policy 4301 revisions.
side_a_arguments: Highlighting one of the least diverse schools in DPS risks masking persistent suspension inequities affecting Black, Hispanic, and EC learners elsewhere.
Authentic equity work requires examining belonging and discipline interventions at schools facing the steepest disparities.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defended sharing positive Panorama belonging data and Policy 4301 work in progress across the district while acknowledging further work is needed on discipline gaps.
side_b_arguments: Presentations highlight promising instructional and climate practices that can inform broader district improvements alongside ongoing Code of Conduct updates.
conflicts.resolution: Staff noted the feedback as Policy 4301 and Priority 2 equity interventions continued to be refined.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/7/24
conflicts.issue: District Liability for Community-Organized Carpools and Walking Groups
conflicts.summary: Board members questioned whether DPS could actively organize parent volunteers and neighborhood walking/carpool networks to offset walk zones and bus shortages, drawing legal caution from staff.
conflicts.side_a_position: Assess DPS capacity to mobilize and organize volunteers, churches, and carpool/walking networks quickly.
side_a_arguments: Working families need practical carpool and walking-group support if elementary walk zones are introduced.
Community members offered to volunteer and step up to help alleviate the crisis.
conflicts.side_b_position: DPS cannot formally organize or guarantee parent-led carpools/walks due to legal and insurance liability.
side_b_arguments: Chief Legal Officer Tanya Giovanni and Chair Millicent Rogers noted a major legal distinction between parents informally forming phone trees and the school district organizing student rides.
Unvetted non-school rides create serious accident and supervision liability risks for the district.
conflicts.resolution: Staff directed to consult legal and insurance counsel on liability boundaries for volunteer driving and church partnerships.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Work Session | 8/8/24
conflicts.issue: Scope of Deferrals on Storm-Impacted Virtual Work Session Agenda
conflicts.summary: At the start of the storm-triggered virtual meeting, board members discussed whether to keep informational items such as the Durham School of the Arts (DSA) recap and Board travel reimbursement items on the agenda or postpone non-essential business until the August 22 in-person meeting.
conflicts.side_a_position: Defer non-essential presentations (including the full DSA item) and Board items to the August 22 meeting so the community can participate fully in person.
side_a_arguments: Tropical storm conditions forced a virtual meeting without live spoken public comment.
Deferring the full DSA item allows the public to hear the presentation and respond together at the next meeting.
conflicts.side_b_position: Proceed with informational recaps (including DSA) while deferring formal DSA action to August 22 consent agenda, and retain Board items due to policy deadlines.
side_b_arguments: Presenting the DSA overview gives the public two weeks to review materials before August 22, when any board member can pull it from consent after public comment.
Board Policy 2130 requires travel reimbursement requests within 45 days, making August 22 close to the cutoff.
conflicts.resolution: Natalie Beyer accepted the clarification and voted with colleagues to approve the agenda 6-0-1 (with Joy Harrell-Goff muted).

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 7/5/26
conflicts.issue: Timing of Board Committee and Community Liaison Appointments
conflicts.summary: Members debated whether to postpone all committee and liaison appointments until August onboarding or appoint standing committees immediately to support district operations.
conflicts.side_a_position: Defer committee and liaison assignments until August after board onboarding and retreat.
side_a_arguments: New board members needed onboarding and governance retreat alignment before committing to committee roles.
conflicts.side_b_position: Make core standing committee and liaison appointments immediately in July.
side_b_arguments: Administrators needed active Finance, Facilities, and Academics committees prior to August work sessions, and community partners rely on board liaisons.
conflicts.resolution: Wendell Tabb and Gabrielle (Gabby) Rivero proposed a compromise adopted 7-0: appoint Finance, Facilities, Academics, and interim liaisons immediately while deferring Policy, Legislative Steering, and NCSBA delegates to August.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
conflicts.issue: Policy 4301 'Must' vs 'May' IEP/504 Compliance Language
conflicts.summary: Following legal counsel advice, the board voted 6-1 to soften 'must' to 'may' and remove a trailing legal compliance sentence in Policy 4301 regarding IEP/504 reviews.
conflicts.side_a_position: Adopt counsel's edit from 'must' to 'may' and trim redundant statutory compliance language from the handbook matrix.
side_a_arguments: Avoids unintended legal liability and redundancy because Policy 4307 and federal IDEA/504 statutes remain binding.
conflicts.side_b_position: Preserve mandatory 'must' language inside Policy 4301 so school staff see binding disability protections directly in the Code of Conduct.
side_b_arguments: Cross-referencing Policy 4307 is weaker in day-to-day school enforcement than mandatory Code of Conduct language.
conflicts.resolution: Amendment passed 6-1.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: School Resource Officer (SRO) Uniforms vs. Plain-Clothes Options
conflicts.summary: Board members questioned Sheriff Clarence Birkhead on whether SROs could wear softer or plain-clothes attire on campus, while the Sheriff insisted on standard recognizable uniforms.
conflicts.side_a_position: Explore plain-clothes or less-militarized attire for campus SROs.
side_a_arguments: Standard tactical/police uniforms can feel intimidating or traumatic to students and undermine non-punitive school climate goals.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain standard identifiable law-enforcement uniforms for campus SROs.
side_b_arguments: Clear uniform visibility ensures students, staff, and responding emergency personnel can immediately identify sworn officers during a crisis.
conflicts.resolution: Sheriff Birkhead retained uniform policy; the board subsequently voted 6-0 to renew the SRO MOU.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
conflicts.issue: PreK and Kindergarten 1:1 Chromebook Deployment vs. Screen-Time Concerns
conflicts.summary: During the technology fee discussion, Emily Chávez and Chair Bettina Umstead challenged district administration on whether PreK and kindergarten students should receive 1:1 Chromebooks.
conflicts.side_a_position: Question 1:1 Chromebooks for PreK and kindergarten learners on developmental and cost grounds.
side_a_arguments: Excessive screen exposure in PreK and kindergarten classrooms is developmentally questionable when shared classroom sets could suffice.
conflicts.side_b_position: Maintain districtwide 1:1 device provisioning across elementary grades.
side_b_arguments: Consistent 1:1 devices support diagnostic assessments, digital literacy integration, and standardized fleet management across schools.
conflicts.resolution: Board approved the annual technology fee 7-0 while flagging early-grade device utilization for ongoing administrative review.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer Committee) Modifications - Amended May 22 Draft
conflicts.summary: Reconvening around 02:30:17 and formally refining the motion at 03:33:55, Emily Chávez moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded adopting the May 22 draft of Policy 7215 establishing an 11% membership threshold for Employee Representative Organization (ERO) participation, defining EROs, and permitting HR or third-party verification. Natalie Beyer, Bettina Umstead, and Wendell Tabb objected strongly to acting on an eleventh-hour rewrite without legal vetting on North Carolina Public Records Act confidentiality for membership lists and tried to table the vote to June 10 (failing for lack of a second at 03:16:07). During floor negotiation, sponsors agreed to strike 'all', strike the Section C Appendix, and mandate mutual agreement on any third-party certifier. In the roll call between 03:59:13 and 04:01:36, Chávez, Harrell-Goff, Carda-Auten, and Chair Millicent Rogers voted Aye while Tabb, Beyer, and Umstead voted Nay, passing the modified policy 4-3.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 4-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (4-3)

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
conflicts.issue: Main Motion: Waive Second Reading & Adopt Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer Committee, 6% Threshold)
conflicts.summary: Natalie Beyer moved at 03:59:36 (restated at 05:05:26) and Millicent Rogers seconded waiving second reading and adopting Policy 7215 with a 6% ERO threshold, amended Section E1 naming the largest ERO as committee vice chair, mutually exclusive percentage bands in the seat table, and deletion of 'other employees' in Section C3. Supporters argued passing a workable policy immediately ended 14 months of delay and complied with board legal counsel's equal-access guidance, while Chávez, Harrell-Goff, and Tabb objected that a 6% threshold and committee structure undermined DAE's collective-voice proposal and urged mediation or a 20% compromise. On the roll call starting at 05:06:48, Chávez, Harrell-Goff, and Tabb voted No while Umstead and Beyer voted Aye alongside seconder Rogers and Carda-Auten (whose roll-call audio dropped in ASR before the next item), adopting the 6% policy 4-3 (later revisited and modified May 22).
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 4-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (4-3)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/6/25
conflicts.issue: Public Posting of Non-FRZ Schools List and GoDurham Transit Viability
conflicts.summary: During the transportation update, Wendell Tabb disagreed with Chair Millicent Rogers and staff over publishing a list of schools unaffected by Family Responsibility Zones and questioned whether GoDurham bus frequency adequately serves high school students.
conflicts.side_a_position: Urged transparency by posting which schools lack FRZs and expressed skepticism that GoDurham schedules reliably match student school commutes.
side_a_arguments: Families deserve complete clarity on which schools are and are not subject to FRZ walk zones.
Infrequent or misaligned GoDurham municipal routes cannot simply replace school bus coverage without burdening students.
conflicts.side_b_position: Cautioned that publishing a separate list of unaffected schools could confuse families and noted coordination with the City of Durham on GoDurham and crossing guards is ongoing.
side_b_arguments: Communicating directly to impacted school communities avoids unnecessary alarm or misinterpretation across non-FRZ campuses.
Joint city-county advocacy—including updating the 2014 list of 15 crossing guards across 13 schools—is the proper venue to address transit gaps.
conflicts.resolution: Informational discussion concluded with plans to raise crossing-guard and GoDurham coordination at the upcoming joint city-county-board meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
conflicts.issue: Implement Express Bus Stops for School for Creative Studies, Durham School of the Arts, and Rogers-Herr
conflicts.summary: Transportation staff proposed converting bus service at School for Creative Studies (SCS), Durham School of the Arts (DSA), and Rogers-Herr Middle School to regional Express Stops to save approximately eight bus routes needed to end rotational coverage. Natalie Beyer, seconded by Emily Chávez, moved to implement Express Stops immediately for those three magnet/specialty campuses rather than waiting until 2025-26. Opponents including Bettina Umstead, Jessica Carda-Auten, and Chair Millicent Rogers expressed concern about imposing major routing changes mid-year without detailed hub site logistics, student weather shelter, family outreach, and clear hardship appeals. With Wendell Tabb having stepped out/left the meeting, the roll call ended in a 3-3 tie, causing the motion to fail.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 3-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (3-3)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 9/26/24
conflicts.issue: Direct Meet and Confer Policy Establishing Regular Meetings with an ERO at 50% Membership Threshold
conflicts.summary: Even after referring collaborative drafting to the Superintendent and DAE leadership, board members remained divided over whether to give explicit policy direction recognizing an Employee Representative Organization (ERO) based on majority membership. Joy Harrell-Goff moved, seconded by Emily Chávez, to direct development of a Meet and Confer policy establishing regular meetings with an ERO demonstrating 50% membership among non-administrative, non-managerial active DPS employees as of the end of the prior school year. Supporters argued clear democratic benchmarks honor unionized workers and prevent exclusion, while opponents warned against legal exposure under NCGS 95-98/115C-335.9 and potential exclusion of non-member employee groups. On roll call, Chávez, Carda-Auten, Harrell-Goff, and Umstead voted Aye while Tabb, Beyer, and Chair Rogers voted Nay, carrying the motion 4-3.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 4-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (4-3)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 9/19/24
conflicts.issue: Administrative Discretion vs. Explicit Board Specification of $3M Local Supplement Recipients
conflicts.summary: When reviewing the ~12.5% ($3M+) local supplement funding covering roughly 2,900 employees, board members pushed back against leaving recipient selection to administrative discretion before defining exact job titles.
conflicts.side_a_position: Do not grant administration open discretion to decide which employee groups receive the local supplement increase without explicit Board designation.
side_a_arguments: The Board must know exactly which employee classifications are included before approving funds.
Pausing via recess avoids ambiguity and unintended exclusions across certified and support roles.
conflicts.side_b_position: Administration initially presented the ~2,900-employee cost pool based on prior-year supplement recipients without finalized group-by-group designations.
side_b_arguments: Cost projections were modeled on the prior year's 2,900 supplement recipients totaling just over $3 million.
conflicts.resolution: Following a ~29-minute recess, Natalie Beyer moved and the Board unanimously approved (6-0) an explicit $80/month local supplement increase for SLPs, psychologists, audiologists, school counselors, teachers, nurses, and instructional support personnel.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
conflicts.issue: Scope of Meet and Confer Policy and Inclusion of Non-Union Staff
conflicts.summary: Public commenters from DAE and supporting labor unions clashed with Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's update advocating non-union worker representation alongside DAE in Meet and Confer drafts.
conflicts.side_a_position: Include mechanisms for non-union classified and staff voices alongside DAE in administration's Meet and Confer draft.
side_a_arguments: Roughly 30-40% of workers or non-union employees still deserve structured representation in workplace discussions.
Administration must ensure compliance with North Carolina law while fostering inclusive communication.
conflicts.side_b_position: Honor the board's September 26 directive establishing Meet and Confer with an ERO meeting the 50% threshold (DAE).
side_b_arguments: Labor leaders argued administration's counter-draft undermined democratic worker representation and the board's 4-3 September vote.
Employees repeatedly cited broken trust between cabinet leadership and frontline classified/certified staff.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote taken on Meet and Confer on December 19.

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
conflicts.issue: Authorize Administration to Plan Express Stop Service to End Rotational Coverage in January 2025 and Return January 9 with Details
conflicts.summary: After the 3-3 tie on immediate Express Stop implementation, board members debated how to give families relief from rotational bus cancellations without forcing an unvetted rollout before winter break. Natalie Beyer initially floated planning Express Stops for 2025-26 with Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten's second, then revised the motion—seconded by Emily Chávez—to authorize administration to prepare Express Stop plans aimed at ending rotational coverage in January 2025 and bring back detailed operational plans, community notification timelines, and clear Policy 1740/4010 grievance/support procedures at the January 9, 2025 work session. Carda-Auten joined Beyer, Chávez, and Joy Harrell-Goff in supporting the planning-first directive, while Bettina Umstead and Chair Millicent Rogers maintained their opposition to mid-year Express Stops, passing the motion 4-2 with Wendell Tabb absent.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Passed 4-2)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Passed (4-2)

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting
conflicts.issue: Election of Board Vice Chair - Initial Tie Vote (Joy Harrell-Goff vs. Millicent Rogers)
conflicts.summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened nominations for Board Vice Chair at 00:03:55, with Joy Harrell-Goff nominated at 00:04:12 and Millicent Rogers nominated at 00:04:21. In the initial ballot between 00:04:40 and 00:05:00, both candidates received three votes each from the six present members, leaving neither with a majority. Board Attorney Dubes advised the board that because no majority was reached, the board needed to repeat the vote by an explicit show of hands. Members proceeded directly to the sequential show-of-hands re-vote.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 3-3)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (3-3)

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting
conflicts.issue: Election of Board Vice Chair - Re-vote on Nomination of Joy Harrell-Goff
conflicts.summary: Following Attorney Dubes's procedural guidance after the 3-3 tie, Chair Bettina Umstead conducted a show-of-hands re-vote beginning with Joy Harrell-Goff at 00:05:54. Harrell-Goff received two votes in favor while four members held their votes or opposed, falling short of the majority among the six members present. The result at 00:06:24 cleared the way for the immediate vote on Millicent Rogers.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 2-4)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (2-4)

conflicts.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Organizational Meeting | 7/1/24
conflicts.issue: Nomination of Bettina Umstead for Board Vice Chair for 2024-2025
conflicts.summary: Natalie Beyer nominated outgoing Chair Bettina Umstead for Vice Chair, delivering an extended speech arguing that incoming Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis needed Umstead's institutional memory, external relationships, and experience navigating the 2024 pay crisis. Umstead accepted the board's will while highlighting the $27M county budget expansion and pandemic recovery under her tenure, whereas Joy Harrell-Goff spoke in favor of leadership succession and Wendell Tabb explained he would abstain on non-unanimous officer votes. Prior to voting, Attorney Rod Malone advised that board policy requires voting separately on each nominee and treats any unexcused abstention as an affirmative vote. The voice vote on Umstead yielded two Ayes (Beyer and Umstead), four Nays, and Tabb's abstention—recorded officially under policy as 3-4, failing to win a majority.
conflicts.side_a_position: Voted Aye (Failed 3-4)
conflicts.side_b_position: Voted Nay / Opposed
conflicts.resolution: Failed (3-4)

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 7/5/26
meetings.executive_summary: At the July 5, 2026 special called organizational meeting, Durham County Board of Elections Chair Mr. Boone presented official March 3, 2026 election canvass certificates and Judge Hairston Mitchell swore in new board members Natalie Bent Kitaif, Nadeen Bir, Gabrielle (Gabby) Rivero, and Xavier Cason, seating the 2026-present board before any votes occurred. In a contested election for Board Chair, Joy Harrell-Goff defeated incumbent Vice Chair Millicent Rogers by a 5-2 voice vote, and Xavier Cason was unanimously elected Vice Chair (7-0). Following debate over whether to defer all committee assignments until August, the board reached a compromise to appoint Finance, Facilities, and Academics committees plus interim liaisons immediately while deferring Policy Committee, Legislative Steering, and NCSBA delegates to August, and scheduled a special July 20 or 21 meeting for salary schedules.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Recognition of Outgoing Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Vice Chair Millicent Rogers opened the special called reorganization meeting and recognized outgoing board members Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten in the audience.

agenda_items.title: Certification of Election Results and Swearing-In of Newly Elected Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Board of Elections Chair Mr. Boone presented the certified March 3, 2026 election results (Natalie Bent Kitaif 7,602; Nadeen Bir 9,415; Gabrielle (Gabby) Rivero 9,917; Xavier Cason 8,545), and Judge Hairston Mitchell administered the oath of office to all four new members prior to board elections and business.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair and Board Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis presided over the Board Chair nominations. Wendell Tabb nominated Millicent Rogers (failed 2-5 by voice vote) and Nadeen Bir nominated Joy Harrell-Goff, who was elected Chair 5-2; Chair Harrell-Goff then took the gavel and oversaw Xavier Cason's unanimous 7-0 election as Vice Chair.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Rogers Failed 2-5; Harrell-Goff Passed 5-2; Cason Passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated Nadeen Bir's proposal to remove or defer Item H (committee and liaison appointments) until after an August governance retreat versus Millicent Rogers's warning that staff needed standing-committee direction before August meetings. Tabb and Rivero brokered a consensus compromise to appoint core standing committees now and defer Policy, Legislative Steering, and NCSBA delegates to August.

agenda_items.title: 2026-2027 Board of Education Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members amended the proposed 2026-2027 meeting calendar to add a special called meeting on July 20 or July 21 at 5:30 PM to take action on employee salary schedules and then adopted the schedule unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Standing Committee Appointments and Interim Liaisons
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following discussion of member availability and workload, the board approved standing committee rosters for Finance (Rivero, Bir, Rogers), Facilities (Tabb, Bent Kitaif, Cason), and Academics (Bent Kitaif, Tabb, Rivero, plus Rogers), along with interim community liaisons.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The newly seated board voted unanimously to enter closed session for statutory personnel and legal matters.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Chair — Nominee: Millicent Rogers
votes.notes: Voice vote without individual roll call; Superintendent Lewis announced Rogers did not achieve a majority and Harrell-Goff won 5-2 on the ensuing vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Under Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis presiding for the reorganization vote, Wendell Tabb nominated incumbent Vice Chair Millicent Rogers to serve as Board Chair, citing her institutional continuity during a four-member board transition. Nadeen Bir separately nominated incumbent at-large member Joy Harrell-Goff. Taking the nominations in order by voice vote, Rogers received two affirmative voices and five opposed (implied by the subsequent 5-2 Chair tally), failing to secure a majority.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Chair — Nominee: Joy Harrell-Goff
votes.notes: Voice vote without individual roll call; Chair Harrell-Goff assumed the gavel at 00:24:57.
votes.discussion_detail: Nadeen Bir nominated Joy Harrell-Goff to serve as Chair of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education following the swearing-in of the four incoming members. After Millicent Rogers's nomination failed, Superintendent Lewis called the voice vote on Harrell-Goff's nomination, which passed 5-2. Harrell-Goff immediately assumed the presiding chair role to conduct the Vice Chair election and remaining organizational business.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair — Nominee: Xavier Cason
votes.notes: Newly elected Chair Joy Harrell-Goff presided over the Vice Chair election.
votes.discussion_detail: After assuming the chair, Joy Harrell-Goff opened nominations for Board Vice Chair, and newly seated District 4 member Xavier Cason was nominated. No other candidates were put forward for the position. By voice vote, all seven seated board members voted unanimously 7-0 to elect Cason as Vice Chair.

votes.item_title: Approve Special Meeting Agenda (With Consensus Compromise on Committee Appointments)
votes.notes: Compromise reached to appoint Finance, Facilities, Academics, and interim liaisons at this meeting while deferring Policy, Legislative Steering, and NCSBA delegates to August.
votes.discussion_detail: During agenda approval, Nadeen Bir asked whether Item H (committee appointments and liaisons) could be postponed until August after board onboarding and an anticipated governance retreat. Millicent Rogers argued that leaving Finance, Facilities, and Academics committees unstaffed until August would leave district administrators without board guidance ahead of August 11 and August 13 meetings and risk neglecting community partner liaisons. Wendell Tabb and Gabrielle (Gabby) Rivero brokered a middle-ground compromise to proceed with Item H strictly for Finance, Facilities, Academics, and interim liaisons while deferring Policy Committee, Legislative Steering, and NCSBA delegate assignments until August, and the agenda passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Amend 2026-2027 Board of Education Meeting Schedule to Add July 20 or 21 Salary Schedule Meeting
votes.notes: Added a 5:30 PM special called meeting on July 20 or 21, 2026 specifically to address employee salary schedules.
votes.discussion_detail: Reviewing the proposed 2026-2027 annual board calendar, Millicent Rogers noted the urgency of adopting updated employee salary schedules prior to the start of the new school year while the state budget remained unresolved. She moved to amend the schedule to add a special called meeting at 5:30 PM on July 20 or July 21, 2026 dedicated to salary schedules, seconded by Nadeen Bir. The board approved the calendar amendment unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve 2026-2027 Board of Education Meeting Schedule as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after amending the 2026-2027 calendar to include the July special meeting on employee salary schedules, the board voted on the full annual meeting schedule as amended. Members raised no objections to the remaining work session and monthly meeting dates. The motion passed unanimously 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Committee Appointments (Finance, Facilities, Academics) and Interim Liaisons
votes.notes: Finance: Rivero, Bir, Rogers; Facilities: Tabb, Bent Kitaif, Cason; Academics: Bent Kitaif, Tabb, Rivero, plus Rogers.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members discussed personal scheduling constraints and subject-matter interests to populate the three operational standing committees while honoring the consensus to wait until August on Policy, Legislative Steering, and NCSBA delegates. Under the agreed roster, Finance included Gabrielle (Gabby) Rivero, Nadeen Bir, and Millicent Rogers; Facilities included Wendell Tabb, Natalie Bent Kitaif, and Xavier Cason; and Academics included Bent Kitaif, Tabb, Rivero, and Rogers, along with interim community liaison assignments. Wendell Tabb moved approval of the appointments, Xavier Cason seconded, and the slate passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Upon completing all open-session organizational actions, Millicent Rogers moved to enter closed session for the statutory purposes noticed on the special meeting agenda. Wendell Tabb seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously 7-0 by voice vote.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
meetings.executive_summary: In the final regular monthly meeting of the 2024-2026 board cohort, Chair Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten were honored for their service alongside Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's update and contract second amendment approval. Facing unresolved state budget action, CFO Jeremy Teeter briefed the board on operating under an interim budget resolution, and the board voted 7-0 to adopt an hourly substitute teacher pay methodology while deferring rate increases until fall classified pay decisions. The board also approved a district right-sizing and consolidation study RFP (7-0) and the 2026-2031 Beginning Teacher Support Plan (7-0), while rejecting a motion (0-7) to advance Meet and Confer's employee grievance draft (Policy 1750/7220) as written in favor of a unanimous directive for joint legal and HR-DAE redrafting by September.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Recognition of Outgoing Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order, and communications staff recognized Student of the Month Mary Braithwaite before honoring outgoing board members Chair Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten for their years of service.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Anthony Lewis highlighted end-of-year milestones, summer readiness, and gratitude for the outgoing board cohort's leadership.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Second Amendment to Superintendent's Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board amended the agenda 7-0 to add Item 3C (draft RFP for the district right-sizing/consolidation study) and the Second Amendment to Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's contract following his evaluation, then approved the amended agenda and contract amendment 7-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amended 7-0; Agenda Approved 7-0; Contract Amendment Approved 7-0

agenda_items.title: Approval of May 28, 2026 Monthly Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the minutes of the May 28, 2026 regular monthly meeting.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Katie McGonagall, who thanked staff for Little River mold remediation and praised outgoing board members, and Lead Physical Therapist Christy Clum, who warned that the PT department was operating at 50% staffing, resulting in 3,600 fewer IEP-mandated services and lost Medicaid billing.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through AK)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved all consent agenda items A through AK in a single unanimous vote.

agenda_items.title: Budget Update (FY 2026-2027 Interim Resolution Context)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter and Dr. Lewis updated the board on state budget delays and how DPS would operate under an interim budget resolution until final General Assembly appropriations are enacted.

agenda_items.title: Substitute Teacher Compensation Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a substitute compensation study recommending hourly pay and higher rates ($18/$19.40). After Vice Chair Millicent Rogers objected to lifting substitute rates ahead of classified employees and before the state budget is finalized, the board split the recommendation and approved transitioning to an hourly methodology while deferring rate hikes to fall.

agenda_items.title: District Right-Sizing and Consolidation Study RFP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operations staff presented the draft RFP for a comprehensive right-sizing and consolidation study. Board members refined scope language to preserve Growing Together equity commitments, mandate a public community engagement deliverable report, and incorporate small-school and trailer learning environment guidelines before approving the RFP.

agenda_items.title: 2026-2031 Beginning Teacher Support Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR and Beginning Teacher Support staff presented the state-required five-year Beginning Teacher Support Plan covering three-year induction structures and mandatory educator preparation program (EPP) graduate and employer survey compliance.

agenda_items.title: Policy 1750/7220: Grievance Procedures for Employees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board debated the employee grievance procedure draft emerging from Meet and Confer. Joy Harrell-Goff's motion to pass the draft on first reading and advance it to August failed 0-7 after legal counsel and other members cited unresolved operational and legal conflicts, and the board voted 7-0 to direct joint HR, DAE/NCAE, and legal redrafting by the September work session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: First-read motion Failed 0-7; Joint redraft directive Passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Policy Committee Update, Reflections, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jessica Carda-Auten and Dr. Pitman shared first-year Policy Committee lessons learned and transition recommendations for the incoming board, followed by informational grants/gifts items and a 6-0 vote to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Add Item 3C (Right-Sizing RFP) and Second Amendment to Superintendent's Contract
votes.discussion_detail: During agenda review at the start of the business portion of the June 25 meeting, Natalie Beyer moved to amend the agenda to add two time-sensitive items: Item 3C, the draft Request for Proposals for the district right-sizing and consolidation study requested at the June 9 work session, and the Second Amendment to Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's employment contract. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers seconded the addition. With no objections raised, the board passed the agenda amendment unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Following adoption of the additions for the right-sizing RFP and the Superintendent's contract amendment, Emily Chávez moved to approve the full agenda as amended. Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. The full seven-member board approved the amended agenda 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Second Amendment to Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's Contract
votes.notes: Adopted following completion of the Superintendent's annual board evaluation.
votes.discussion_detail: Board leadership presented the Second Amendment to Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's contract following the board's formal evaluation of his performance over the preceding year. Members affirmed their support for his leadership during ongoing budget uncertainty and facility challenges while thanking outgoing board members for guiding the evaluation cycle. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved approval of the contract amendment, Joy Harrell-Goff seconded, and the motion carried unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve May 28, 2026 Regular Monthly Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead called for action on the draft minutes from the May 28, 2026 regular monthly board meeting. Natalie Beyer moved to approve the minutes as presented and Millicent Rogers seconded. No corrections were offered by board members, and the minutes passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Change Substitute Teacher Pay Methodology to Hourly Pay Effective 2026-27 (Deferring Rate Increase to Fall)
votes.notes: Board split the administration proposal so only the hourly pay structure takes effect for 2026-27 while the proposed $18/$19.40 rate increase returns in fall alongside classified pay scales.
votes.discussion_detail: Administration presented a substitute teacher compensation study proposing to switch substitutes from a daily rate to an hourly pay model while raising pay to $18.00 and $19.40 per hour. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers objected to enacting pay raises for substitutes before regular classified employees receive long-awaited scale increases and while state budget funding remained unknown, proposing to split methodology from pay rates. Natalie Beyer moved to approve transitioning to the hourly pay methodology effective for 2026-27 while bringing the rate-increase decision back in the fall with classified salary scales; Joy Harrell-Goff seconded, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve District Right-Sizing and Consolidation Study RFP (With Board Edits)
votes.notes: Included board edits referencing Growing Together alignment, a community engagement deliverable report, and small-school/trailer learning environment guidelines.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff presented the draft Request for Proposals for a third-party district right-sizing and consolidation study as directed at the June 9 work session. Board members scrutinized the scope to ensure bidders evaluate alignment with Growing Together equity goals, produce a dedicated public report summarizing community engagement findings, and factor in learning environment guidelines regarding small schools and mobile trailers. Natalie Beyer moved to approve issuing the RFP incorporating the board's edits, Emily Chávez seconded, and the motion passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve 2026-2031 Beginning Teacher Support Plan
votes.notes: Includes mandatory EPP graduate and employer survey compliance and three-year beginning teacher induction processes.
votes.discussion_detail: District HR and Beginning Teacher Support leadership presented the 2026-2031 five-year Beginning Teacher Support Plan required by state DPI guidelines, detailing mentor ratios, three-year induction support, and mandatory educator preparation program graduate/employer surveys. Board members questioned mentor capacity, support for alternatively licensed educators, and retention tracking across high-need schools. Emily Chávez moved approval of the plan, Jessica Carda-Auten seconded, and the board passed it unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Policy 1750/7220 (Grievance Procedures for Employees) on First Read as Submitted and Advance to August Work Session
votes.notes: Failed unanimously 0-7 after discussion showed even the mover/seconder agreed legal and operational clean-up was necessary before advancing to first read.
votes.discussion_detail: Taking up Policy 1750/7220 on employee grievance procedures from the Meet and Confer process, Joy Harrell-Goff initially moved (seconded by Emily Chávez) to accept the Meet and Confer draft as-is on first reading and advance it to the August work session to honor educator collaboration. However, Board Attorney Malone, Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, Millicent Rogers, and Jessica Carda-Auten pointed out unresolved procedural conflicts, unclear timelines, and inconsistencies with existing legal standards that HR and legal counsel had not yet reconciled with DAE. Convinced that advancing an unvetted draft would create confusion for the incoming board, even the sponsors joined the unanimous 0-7 vote against the motion.

votes.item_title: Direct Administration, Board Counsel, DAE/NCAE, and DAE Counsel to Collaborate on Clean Policy 1750/7220 Draft by September Work Session
votes.notes: Set deadline no later than the September 2026 work session for a reconciled draft.
votes.discussion_detail: After the 0-7 rejection of advancing Policy 1750/7220 unedited, board members sought a constructive timeline that respected Meet and Confer consensus while ensuring legal enforceability. Natalie Beyer moved to direct district administration, board legal counsel, DAE/NCAE representatives, and DAE legal counsel to collaborate on a clean, reconciled draft due back no later than the September 2026 work session. Millicent Rogers seconded, and all seven board members voted Aye (7-0).

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Chair declared motion passed 6-0 at 04:56:47 with one board member away/absent at the late-night adjournment.
votes.discussion_detail: After Jessica Carda-Auten and Dr. Pitman presented the year-end Policy Committee reflection report and staff noted grants, gifts, and donations for information only, Natalie Beyer moved to enter closed session for the statutory items listed on the agenda. Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. The chair called the vote at nearly 11:30 PM, passing 6-0 with one member no longer present at the dais.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
disagreements.issue: Splitting Substitute Teacher Hourly Methodology From Proposed Rate Increase
disagreements.summary: Administration proposed simultaneously moving substitutes to hourly pay and increasing hourly rates, drawing pushback over raising substitute pay while classified staff raises remained stalled by the state budget.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve only the structural shift to hourly pay methodology now and defer substitute rate increases until fall alongside classified salary scales.
side_a_arguments: Raising substitute pay before classified employees receive raises and before state appropriations are finalized sends the wrong priority signal.
Budget certainty is needed before committing recurring compensation increases.
disagreements.side_b_position: Original staff recommendation paired hourly methodology with $18/$19.40 hourly rate increases to strengthen substitute fill rates.
side_b_arguments: Competitive substitute pay addresses classroom coverage shortages alongside moving away from flat daily rates.
disagreements.resolution: The board unanimously voted 7-0 to approve only the hourly pay methodology for 2026-27 and bring rate adjustments back in fall with classified salary scales.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 6/25/26
disagreements.issue: Advancing Meet and Confer Draft of Policy 1750/7220 vs Joint Legal/HR Redrafting
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether to honor Meet and Confer's consensus draft of employee grievance policy 1750/7220 on first read immediately or require joint legal, HR, and union redrafting first.
disagreements.side_a_position: Initially proposed adopting the Meet and Confer draft on first reading and sending it to the August work session for second-read refinements.
side_a_arguments: Educator representatives invested significant Meet and Confer time and deserved to see the product advance rather than stall during board transition.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject first-read passage until HR, board counsel, DAE/NCAE, and DAE counsel resolve operational and legal contradictions.
side_b_arguments: Board counsel and HR had not had sufficient collaborative redrafting sessions with DAE counsel to ensure a legally workable grievance timeline.
Handing an incomplete first-read draft to four incoming board members would create confusion.
disagreements.resolution: The first-read motion failed 0-7 after sponsors joined the consensus, and the board unanimously approved 7-0 a directive for a joint HR, DAE/NCAE, and legal draft due by the September work session.
