meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 9, 2026 monthly work session—opened 6-0 by Vice Chair Millicent Rogers before Chair Bettina Umstead arrived and later facilitated by Joy Harrell-Goff during policy review—the board examined county budget adjustments ($10.9M continuation, $2.65M tax-funded expansion, and $2.65M internal match), capital improvement needs ($965M 10-year systems backlog with no 2026 bond), and major student-safety and discipline policies. Following extensive debate over a third-party right-sizing study, the board directed staff (7-0) to prepare a draft RFP for June 25 rather than authorizing a consultant sight unseen. Across 13 policy votes—including a motion to reconsider—the board adopted Policy 4326 on seclusion and restraint (6-1, Wendell Tabb opposed after the 'briefly' amendment passed 6-1), amended and adopted Elementary and Secondary Codes of Conduct Policies 4301.1/4301.2 (7-0, including a 4-3 vote requiring principal supervisor review for PreK-5 EC suspensions and a 6-1 vote softening 'must' to 'may' on IEP/504 plan clauses), and adopted Policy 4307 (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Minutes (May 14, 2026), and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Chair Bettina Umstead en route, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers presided at opening (6 members present), leading 6-0 approvals of the May 14, 2026 work session minutes, an agenda amendment pulling Item 2S (Policy 4326) from Consent to Policy Item 5A, and the amended agenda.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Durham Advocates for Exceptional Children (DAEC) representatives urging tighter seclusion, restraint, and PreK-5 EC suspension protections; Rob Fields challenging the $18.22/hr living-wage shortfall; and physical/occupational therapists Karen Tartik, Heidi Hitland, and Christy Clum pleading for pay-scale relief amid a 55% PT staffing crisis.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (As Amended)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Excluding Policy 4326, which had been pulled to Item 5A for debate, the board unanimously approved the consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-2027 Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter detailed the county manager's $10.9 million continuation allocation, a $2.65 million tax-funded expansion, $1 million in capital technology, and a $2.65 million internal match to reach an $18.22/hr minimum wage, a $100 safety assistant supplement, and OT/PT scale fixes. Members debated whether to trim coordinator/director raises from 5% to 3% to redirect roughly $263,000 toward lower-paid staff, raised interpreter NC8 pay concerns, and requested year-to-date budget actuals.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and 2022 Bond Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Capital Director Devin Mitchell reported on 2022 bond projects (Murray Massenberg complete at $90.6M, Glenn 85% at $68.9M, DSA 43% at $263.3M), a $965 million 10-year facilities systems need, and the absence of a 2026 bond (shifting focus to LOBS and a 2028 bond). After debate over whether to authorize a right-sizing consultant immediately, the board voted 7-0 directing staff to return with a draft RFP on June 25.

agenda_items.title: Policy 4326: Rules for Use of Seclusion and Restraint in Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Joy Harrell-Goff facilitating the policy section, members spent 35 minutes amending Policy 4326—including a procedural motion to reconsider parent-notice timing in order to insert parallel Section D3 isolation reporting to principals, requiring same-day parent notification, and adding 'briefly' before 'calm or comfort' in A3b over Wendell Tabb's opposition before passing the policy 6-1.

agenda_items.title: Policy 4301.1 (Elementary) and Policy 4301.2 (Secondary) Student Code of Conduct
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated eliminating Level 1B out-of-school suspensions in PreK-5, adding principal supervisor review for suspending PreK-5 EC students (passed 4-3), modifying IEP/504 compliance wording from 'must' to 'may' (passed 6-1), and correcting a Level 1B suspension cap typo from 5 days to 2 days (passed 7-0) before adopting both policies on second reading.

agenda_items.title: Policy 1750/7220 (Employee Grievance Procedure) and Policy 4307 (EC Discipline)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to the late hour, the board voted 7-0 to table Policy 1750/7220 and Policy Committee lessons learned to June 25, then unanimously adopted Policy 4307 (Disciplinary Action for Exceptional Children) and waived second reading (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of open business, the board unanimously entered closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve May 14, 2026 Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead was absent/en route at the opening of the meeting; Vice Chair Millicent Rogers presided.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers called the June 9 work session to order in Chair Bettina Umstead's temporary absence while she was en route. The six members present reviewed the draft minutes from the May 14, 2026 work session. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the minutes, Wendell Tabb seconded, and the motion passed 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Pull Item 2S (Policy 4326) from Consent to Policy Committee Item 5A
votes.notes: Umstead still en route.
votes.discussion_detail: Recognizing pending board edits and community advocacy from DAEC regarding seclusion and restraint rules, Emily Chávez moved to pull Policy 4326 (Item 2S) off the consent agenda and place it under Policy Committee Item 5A for open debate and amendment. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers seconded the amendment. All six present board members voted in favor, passing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: With Policy 4326 relocated to open policy discussion, Natalie Beyer moved to adopt the evening's work session agenda as amended. Wendell Tabb seconded the motion. The six present members approved the amended agenda unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Direct Staff to Return Right-Sizing Study RFP to June 25 Board Meeting
votes.notes: RFP must include an optional plan, minimum scope of work, timeline including board engagement, and budget.
votes.discussion_detail: During the CIP and 2022 bond update, staff sought authorization to engage a third-party consultant to conduct a district right-sizing and consolidation study in light of $965 million in 10-year capital needs and declining enrollment. Several board members balked at granting open-ended authorization without reviewing exact deliverables, community engagement expectations, and Growing Together alignment first. Emily Chávez moved (seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten) to direct staff to bring a draft RFP—specifying minimum scope of work, optional plan elements, budget, and a timeline with board engagement—to the June 25 meeting, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Amend Policy 4326 (Seclusion & Restraint) Sections C4, D4, F4 on Parent Notification Timing
votes.notes: Shortly reconsidered at 03:28:48 because Section D lacked a parallel D3 principal-notification provision.
votes.discussion_detail: With Joy Harrell-Goff facilitating policy revisions, members examined DAEC recommendations to tighten parent notification deadlines following seclusion or restraint incidents. Natalie Beyer moved, seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten, to strike delayed notification language in sections C4, D4, and F4 so families receive same-day notice. One board member voted Nay over a structural mismatch in Section D's internal numbering, resulting in a 6-1 vote that members immediately sought to clean up through reconsideration.

votes.item_title: Reconsider Prior Vote Amending Policy 4326 Sections C4, D4, and F4
votes.notes: Reopened to add Section D3 before finalizing same-day parent notice.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the 6-1 amendment vote, board members noticed that Section D (covering isolation) lacked a provision matching Section C3 requiring staff to report incidents to the principal or designee prior to parent notification. To ensure clean policy drafting, Natalie Beyer moved to reconsider the prior C4/D4/F4 amendment and Chair Bettina Umstead seconded. All seven board members voted Aye (7-0) to reopen the provisions.

votes.item_title: Amend Policy 4326 to Add Section D3 (Isolation Reporting to Principal or Designee)
votes.notes: Harmonized Section D with Section C3.
votes.discussion_detail: With Section D reopened, Policy Committee Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved to insert a new Section D3 requiring school personnel to notify the principal or designee whenever isolation is used, mirroring the reporting safeguard in Section C3. Natalie Beyer seconded the amendment. The board adopted the structural fix unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Amend Policy 4326 Sections C4, D4, and F4 to Require Same-Day Parent Notification
votes.notes: Deleted 'when reasonably possible, but no later than the end of the following workday' across C4, D4, and F4.
votes.discussion_detail: Having resolved the Section D3 internal reporting gap, Jessica Carda-Auten moved to delete the permissive phrase 'when reasonably possible, but no later than the end of the following workday' from C4, D4, and F4 so families receive mandatory same-day notification of seclusion, isolation, or physical restraint. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers seconded the amendment. The full board passed the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Amend Policy 4326 Section A3b to Insert 'Briefly' Before 'Calm or Comfort'
votes.notes: Added temporal guardrail distinguishing permissible brief comforting physical contact from prohibited restraint.
votes.discussion_detail: Emily Chávez moved (seconded by Natalie Beyer) to insert the word 'briefly' before 'calm or comfort' in Section A3b of Policy 4326 so exceptions to prohibited physical restraint cannot be stretched into prolonged holds. Wendell Tabb objected vigorously, arguing that educators and coaches comforting distressed students should not face disciplinary risk over undefined time limits, while Chávez, Carda-Auten, and Beyer countered that the modifier aligns with state law and disability-advocate protections against abuse. The amendment passed 6-1 with Tabb voting Nay.

votes.item_title: Adopt Policy 4326 (Rules for Use of Seclusion and Restraint in Schools) as Amended on Second Read
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb maintained his opposition due to the 'briefly' language in A3b.
votes.discussion_detail: Following completion of the Section D3, same-day notice, and 'briefly' amendments, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved to adopt Policy 4326 on second reading as amended, seconded by Natalie Beyer. Supporters highlighted strengthened annual board data reporting, same-day caregiver notice, and clearer limits on isolation and holds, while Wendell Tabb reiterated his concern over the 'briefly' modifier for caring teachers. The policy passed 6-1 with Tabb in dissent.

votes.item_title: Amend Policy 4301.1 (Elementary Code of Conduct) to Require Principal Supervisor Review Before Suspending PreK-5 Students With Disabilities
votes.notes: Passed 4-3 by voice vote without roll call; Carda-Auten and Chávez advocated expanding PreK-2 oversight safeguards across all PreK-5 EC students.
votes.discussion_detail: During the Student Code of Conduct second reading, Jessica Carda-Auten moved (seconded by Emily Chávez) to require principal supervisor consultation and review prior to issuing any out-of-school suspension for PreK-5 students with disabilities, extending oversight beyond the PreK-2 baseline. Supporters cited persistent racial and disability disproportionality in early elementary suspensions and noted that district assistant superintendents had previously confirmed feasibility, while skeptics voiced operational concerns about turnaround capacity across all elementary grades without dedicated behavior staffing. The amendment narrowly passed 4-3 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Amend Policies 4301.1/4301.2 IEP/504 Clause from 'Must' to 'May' and Remove Trailing Statutory Clause
votes.notes: Changed 'must' to 'may' and deleted 'and ensure compliance with all applicable state and federal laws...' after 'Section 504 plan' following Attorney Murchison's legal advice.
votes.discussion_detail: Board Attorney Murchison advised that retaining absolute 'must' language plus a broad clause requiring compliance with all state and federal laws inside Policy 4301's discipline matrix risked creating redundant local legal exposure beyond Policy 4307 and IDEA/Section 504 safeguards. Jessica Carda-Auten moved, seconded by Natalie Beyer, to change 'must' to 'may' and delete the trailing compliance clause after 'Section 504 plan.' One board member voted Nay over concerns about weakening explicit statutory protections in the handbook, and the amendment carried 6-1.

votes.item_title: Amend Policies 4301.1/4301.2 Page 10 Level 1B Suspension Cap from 5 Days to 2 Days
votes.notes: Corrected page 10 aggravating-factor limit for internal consistency.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members spotted an inconsistency on page 10 of the draft Student Code of Conduct where aggravating factors for Level 1B infractions still allowed up to a five-day suspension despite the matrix cap having been lowered to two days. Jessica Carda-Auten moved to change five days to two days on page 10 for consistency, seconded by Chair Bettina Umstead. The corrective amendment passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Policy 4301.1 (Elementary) and Policy 4301.2 (Secondary) Student Code of Conduct as Amended (Second Read)
votes.notes: Also incorporated prior debate rejecting full elimination of Level 1B OSS in PreK-5 while maintaining supervisor checks.
votes.discussion_detail: After extensive deliberation over restorative practices, PreK-5 Level 1B out-of-school suspensions, and disability protections, Natalie Beyer moved to adopt both Policy 4301.1 (Elementary) and Policy 4301.2 (Secondary) Student Code of Conduct as amended on second reading. Jessica Carda-Auten seconded the motion. The full board approved both updated codes of conduct 7-0.

votes.item_title: Table Policy 1750/7220 (Employee Grievance Procedure) and Policy Committee Lessons Learned to June 25 Meeting
votes.discussion_detail: More than five hours into the work session, board members opted to postpone consideration of Policy 1750/7220 (Grievance Procedures for Employees) and the Policy Committee's year-end Lessons Learned reflection until the June 25 regular meeting. Wendell Tabb moved to table both items to June 25 and Natalie Beyer seconded. The motion passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Policy 4307 (Disciplinary Action for Exceptional Children) as Presented and Waive Second Reading
votes.notes: Aligned with updated Code of Conduct Policies 4301.1/4301.2 ahead of year-round school start.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff and Policy Committee leadership presented Policy 4307 governing disciplinary procedures and statutory safeguards for Exceptional Children so it would align cleanly with the newly adopted Student Code of Conduct ahead of the July year-round opening. Natalie Beyer moved to adopt Policy 4307 as presented and waive the second-reading requirement, seconded by Millicent Rogers. The board voted unanimously 7-0 to adopt Policy 4307 immediately.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Following completion of the policy agenda and follow-up review, Natalie Beyer moved to enter closed session for the statutory purposes stated on the agenda. Emily Chávez seconded. The board passed the motion 7-0 by voice vote and terminated the livestream.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
disagreements.issue: Allocating Coordinator/Director Raises at 3% vs 5% to Reallocate $263k to Lower Wage Grades
disagreements.summary: During the budget update, board members debated whether to cap coordinator and director salary increases at 3% instead of 5% so roughly $263,000 could be shifted to lower-paid classified staff.
disagreements.side_a_position: Stress-test reducing coordinator/director raises from 5% to 3% to free $263,000 for lower-paid workers.
side_a_arguments: Prioritizes limited expansion dollars for front-line and lower-wage staff facing higher cost-of-living burdens.
disagreements.side_b_position: Preserve uniform scale adjustments and avoid worsening salary compression among mid-level administrators.
side_b_arguments: Cutting percentage increases for coordinators creates compression against supervised roles and undermines retention.
disagreements.resolution: Informational budget stress-test; CFO Teeter noted options would be further analyzed alongside final state appropriations.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
disagreements.issue: Immediate Authorization of Right-Sizing Consultant vs Reviewing Draft RFP First
disagreements.summary: Administration asked for early green-light support to hire a third-party right-sizing and consolidation consultant, while board members demanded to review a concrete RFP and board-engagement plan first.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require staff to bring a draft RFP with scope, optional plan, budget, and board engagement timeline before authorizing procurement.
side_a_arguments: Right-sizing and potential school consolidation carry major equity stakes and must explicitly incorporate Growing Together and public engagement.
disagreements.side_b_position: Seek early board backing to accelerate third-party facility utilization planning ahead of future bond cycles.
side_b_arguments: Declining enrollment and a $965M 10-year facilities backlog require timely outside analysis.
disagreements.resolution: Unanimous 7-0 directive instructing staff to bring the draft RFP to the June 25 regular meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
disagreements.issue: Adding 'Briefly' Modifier to Policy 4326 Section A3b on Calming/Comforting Students
disagreements.summary: Board members split 6-1 over adding the word 'briefly' to define permissible physical calming/comforting exceptions in Policy 4326 on seclusion and restraint.
disagreements.side_a_position: Insert 'briefly' before 'calm or comfort' to prevent prolonged physical holds from being misclassified.
side_a_arguments: Aligns with NC statutory boundaries and disability-advocate concerns against disguised restraint.
disagreements.side_b_position: Omit 'briefly' to avoid putting caring educators at vague disciplinary risk while comforting distressed children.
side_b_arguments: The term 'briefly' is unquantified and may chill supportive staff interventions.
disagreements.resolution: Both the amendment and final Policy 4326 adoption passed 6-1 with Wendell Tabb voting Nay.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
disagreements.issue: PreK-5 Level 1B Out-of-School Suspensions and EC Principal Supervisor Review (Policy 4301.1)
disagreements.summary: Members debated prohibiting Level 1B suspensions across PreK-5 and requiring principal supervisor review for all PreK-5 suspensions of students with disabilities.
disagreements.side_a_position: Expand oversight to require principal supervisor review before suspending any PreK-5 student with a disability and curb Level 1B exclusions.
side_a_arguments: Addresses severe disproportionality in elementary suspensions of Black, Hispanic, and EC students.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain administrative discretion for escalating safety disruptions and avoid overextending supervisor review beyond PreK-2 capacity.
side_b_arguments: Principals and superintendent Dr. Lewis emphasized staff readiness limits and the need for safety tools in upper elementary.
disagreements.resolution: The board rejected full PreK-5 1B elimination in discussion but narrowly approved (4-3) requiring principal supervisor review prior to suspending PreK-5 students with disabilities.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 6/9/26
disagreements.issue: Policy 4301 'Must' vs 'May' IEP/504 Compliance Language
disagreements.summary: Following legal counsel advice, the board voted 6-1 to soften 'must' to 'may' and remove a trailing legal compliance sentence in Policy 4301 regarding IEP/504 reviews.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt counsel's edit from 'must' to 'may' and trim redundant statutory compliance language from the handbook matrix.
side_a_arguments: Avoids unintended legal liability and redundancy because Policy 4307 and federal IDEA/504 statutes remain binding.
disagreements.side_b_position: Preserve mandatory 'must' language inside Policy 4301 so school staff see binding disability protections directly in the Code of Conduct.
side_b_arguments: Cross-referencing Policy 4307 is weaker in day-to-day school enforcement than mandatory Code of Conduct language.
disagreements.resolution: Amendment passed 6-1.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 5/28/26
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 28, 2026 monthly board meeting chaired by Bettina Umstead, Lyons Farm Elementary educators filled public comment urging revisions to Policy 4132 after rising kindergartners of veteran teachers were denied hardship transfers due to school overcrowding. Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis addressed J-1 visa limits and legal/contractual bars against district H-1B sponsorship, while CFO Jeremy Teeter analyzed the General Assembly's draft budget framework (projecting a 4.28% local weighted cost below DPS's 5% buffer) and Operation Services presented Priority 5 progress including LINQ V6 ERP integration two years ahead of schedule. The board approved Policy 8600 (Budget Transparency, stemming from Meet and Confer) on first reading 7-0 with grammatical and reporting edits, referring second reading to the June 25 regular meeting rather than waiving work-session action rules.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following monthly student and staff celebrations, Dr. Anthony Lewis highlighted Teacher Appreciation Week, the Sparkies awards, DPS Sustainable Schools Coalition's national win, transit staff Spanish cohorts, and legal/contractual limits preventing DPS from sponsoring H-1B visas immediately following five-year J-1 cultural exchange terms.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, April 23 Minutes, and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved Item 4B (CIP & Bond update) to the June 9 work session (7-0), approved the April 23 minutes with a Lyons Farm spelling fix (7-0), and heard public comment from four Lyons Farm teachers (Megan Lewis, Samantha Delver, Kayla Curran, Jessica Ann) urging Policy 4132 updates to allow employees' kindergarteners at overcrowded workplaces, plus Kelly McAllister on Vision to Learn.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through Z)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members approved Consent Agenda items A through Z unanimously after Emily Chávez noted she would follow up individually regarding the international teacher recruitment item.

agenda_items.title: State Budget Framework Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter briefed the board on the General Assembly's May 12 budget framework—featuring 17.1% early-career vs 5.5% veteran certified raises (8% avg), 3% classified raises, tiered bonuses, and $1.7M potential savings if Master's pay is restored—noting DPS's 5% local budget assumption provided cushion above the 4.28% projected local impact while highlighting a $35.8M private-voucher reinvestment shortfall.

agenda_items.title: Operation Services Strategic Plan Priority 5 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operations leaders Anthony White, Clifton Williams, Paul Majumder, and Fredrick Barnes reported on CEP five-year free meal renewal, transportation hiring (50 hires, 40 active) and Tier 2/3 on-time arrival challenges, 100% emergency drill compliance, student enrollment trends against the 35,000 target (Goal 5C), and LINQ V6 payroll/HRMS/finance migration two years ahead of Goal 5D.

agenda_items.title: Policy Committee Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Policy Committee Chair Jessica Carda-Auten verbally summarized the May 21 and May 26 committee meetings, noting Policy 4326 advanced toward June 9 second reading while Policies 1750/7220 and 3400 were routed to June 9 for first reading.

agenda_items.title: Policy 8600: Budget Transparency (First Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter presented Policy 8600 developed via Meet and Confer and Policy Committee collaboration with DAE. After incorporating Natalie Beyer's edits ('within 30 days' and 'reporting' phrasing) and debating whether to return on June 9 or June 25, the board approved first reading 7-0 and referred second reading to the June 25 regular meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved on first read 7-0 (to June 25 monthly meeting)

agenda_items.title: Information Items and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following informational items on grants, gifts, donations, and overnight/international field trips, the board voted 7-0 to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Move Item 4B (CIP & Bond Update) to June 9 Work Session
votes.notes: Deferred Item 4B at Dr. Lewis's notice prior to agenda approval.
votes.discussion_detail: Opening agenda review, Chair Bettina Umstead noted Dr. Lewis's notification that Item 4B (Capital Improvement Plan and Bond Update) needed to be removed from the evening's docket due to scheduling/staff availability. A board member moved to amend the agenda to move Item 4B to the June 9 work session, receiving an immediate second. All seven members voted Aye by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the removal of Item 4B to June 9, Joy Harrell-Goff moved to adopt the evening's agenda as amended. Wendell Tabb seconded the motion. The full board voted unanimously 7-0 by voice vote to approve the agenda.

votes.item_title: Approve April 23, 2026 Regular Monthly Meeting Minutes (As Amended)
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead flagged a minor typographical error in the spelling of Lyons Farm Elementary within the draft April 23, 2026 regular monthly meeting minutes and asked clerk staff to correct it. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved approval of the minutes as amended, seconded by Natalie Beyer. The board approved the amended minutes unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Policy 8600 (Budget Transparency) on First Read With Edits and Send to June 25 Monthly Meeting
votes.notes: Targets July 1, 2026 fiscal-year effective date; CFO Teeter confirmed June 25 adoption leaves sufficient implementation time.
votes.discussion_detail: CFO Jeremy Teeter introduced Policy 8600 on Budget Transparency—developed from Meet and Confer collaboration with DAE—expanding public quarterly reporting across all district position types. Natalie Beyer proposed clarifying 'within 30 days', converting 'this report' to 'reporting', and repairing track-changes grammar errors, while Emily Chávez initially moved first-read approval returning to the June 9 work session. After Beyer and Chair Bettina Umstead objected to waiving work-session action limits for a policy taking effect July 1 and Teeter confirmed June 25 gave staff adequate time, Chávez modified her motion (seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff) to advance Policy 8600 to the June 25 monthly meeting for second read, passing 7-0.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Following informational notices on grants, gifts, donations, and overnight/international field trips, Natalie Beyer moved to enter closed session for the statutory purposes stated on the agenda. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers seconded. The board passed the motion 7-0 by voice vote and closed the public stream.

disagreements.side_a_position: Bring Policy 8600 back to the June 9 work session (with a policy waiver if needed) to avoid delay.

disagreements.side_b_position: Send Policy 8600 to the June 25 regular monthly meeting without waiving the work-session discussion policy.

Policy 8600 takes effect July 1, and CFO Teeter confirmed June 25 adoption poses no operational problem.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/14/26
meetings.executive_summary: With Chair Bettina Umstead absent, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers presided alongside work-session facilitator Emily Chávez at the May 14, 2026 monthly work session. Public speakers addressed occupational/physical therapist shortages, Burton international teacher visas, Little River mold remediation, Policy 4326 seclusion/restraint, and selling three acres of DSA for affordable housing. The central clash arose over Natalie Beyer and Wendell Tabb placing Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) edits onto the agenda via two-member request: after a 45-minute procedural fight over bypassing the 30-item Policy Committee queue, the board voted down waiving Policy 2231 and then voted 3-2 to refer Policy 7215 to the Policy Committee for next year; the board also passed first-read policies 4240/7312, 5150/7313, 4326, and 4301 (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Approval, and April 9 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers opened the work session (Chair Bettina Umstead absent), and the five members initially present amended the agenda 5-0 to move Item 4A (CIP & bond update) to May 28 due to staff illness; with a sixth member arriving, the board approved the April 9 minutes 6-0.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ten speakers addressed OT/PT staffing losses and missed mandated IEP services (Lenor Champion, Danielle Irvin), Burton Elementary J-1/H-1B teacher visas (Michael Israel), Little River mold delays (Patricia Russick), Burton achievement (Rob Fields), DAEC seclusion/restraint and Code of Conduct recommendations (Dr. Jennifer Gerish via Greg Whitaker), collaboration (Alexandra Valladares), youth toxic stress (Dr. Gabriella Maradiaga Panayotti), and Coalition for Affordable Housing and Transit's proposal to sell DSA's northern three acres to the county (Jim Svara).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 2A through 2N)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers read aloud consent items 2A through 2N (life-safety, elevator, pest control, CTE labs, EC therapy contracts, and first-read policies 6340 and 4270/6145), which passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Waive Policy 2231 in Order to Discuss Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer presented six proposed minor edits to Policy 7215 (including capping meetings at six/year, non-delay of budget, trained neutral facilitator cost-split, and routing through Policy Committee) ahead of May 31 recertification. Jessica Carda-Auten, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Emily Chávez argued bypassing 30 tiered policies violated Policy 2231, while Beyer, Rogers, and Tabb defended two-member agenda authority under Policy 2330; the two-thirds waiver failed, and the board then voted 3-2 to refer Policy 7215 to the Policy Committee.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Waiver Failed; Referral to Policy Committee Passed 3-2

agenda_items.title: Policy 4240/7312: Child Abuse Reports and Investigations (First Read)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pitman reviewed mandatory state-board reporting duties for licensed employee misconduct and student resource notices under Policy 4240/7312, which the board approved on first read 6-0 for May 28 consideration.

agenda_items.title: Policy 5150/7313: Reporting to External Agencies (First Read)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved Policy 5150/7313 on first reading without objection and placed it on the May 28 consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Policy 4326: Rules for Use of Seclusion and Restraint in Schools (First Read)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members discussed DAEC recommendations regarding parent notification timelines, annual data reporting, and restraint bans, reaching consensus to route DAEC's Q&A feedback to Attorney Jason Weber before May 21 Policy Committee and passing first read 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Policy 4301: Student Code of Conduct — Elementary and Secondary (First Read)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chanel Sidbury, Dr. Maddox-Perry, and Dr. Watson presented discipline data showing a 16-17% drop in out-of-school suspensions (29% for EC students), 30 kindergarten suspensions, improper Level 1B coding, and embedded restorative matrices. Members debated PreK-3/K-5 exclusion bans versus safety discretion and staffing constraints before approving first read 6-0 toward the June work session.

agenda_items.title: Summary of Follow-Up Items and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted follow-up items for Policy 4326, Policy 4301, and a consensus request for de-identified school-level discipline data, after which the board voted 6-0 to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Move Item 4A (CIP & Bond Update) to May 28 Meeting
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent; five members seated at start while sixth member joined shortly afterward.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers opened the work session in Chair Bettina Umstead's absence with five board members initially present. Administration requested moving Item 4A, the Capital Improvement Plan and bond update, to the May 28 monthly meeting due to staff illness. The amendment passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Agenda as Amended
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent; 5 members present at time of vote.
votes.discussion_detail: With Item 4A deferred to May 28, the five board members present at the opening of the work session voted on the amended agenda. No further modifications were proposed. The amended agenda passed 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve April 9, 2026 Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead absent for the entire meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: By the approval of the April 9, 2026 work session minutes, a sixth board member had arrived (with Chair Bettina Umstead absent for the evening). Joy Harrell-Goff moved to approve the minutes as presented and Vice Chair Millicent Rogers seconded. All six present board members voted Aye (6-0).

votes.item_title: Waive Policy 2231 in Order to Discuss Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer)
votes.notes: Required a two-thirds vote under Policy 2450 to suspend Policy 2231; presiding chair announced motion did not pass without numerical tally.
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer presented six proposed minor amendments to Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) developed after reviewing conflicts with Policy 2231—including capping sessions at six per year, clarifying budget feedback non-delay, adding a trained cost-shared facilitator, and routing policy proposals to the Policy Committee—before the May 31 recertification window. A contentious 45-minute procedural debate ensued: Jessica Carda-Auten, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Emily Chávez argued that bypassing 30 board-prioritized policies violated Policy 2231, while Beyer, Millicent Rogers, and Wendell Tabb cited Policy 2330's two-member agenda right and the need for full-board clarity. Harrell-Goff ultimately moved to waive Policy 2231 solely to bring the waiver question to a vote under Policy 2450's two-thirds threshold, and the motion failed by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Refer Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) to the Policy Committee
votes.notes: Carda-Auten declined Beyer's friendly amendment to guarantee 15-20 minutes on the May 21 agenda; Harrell-Goff opposed referring now rather than leaving to next board's September tiering. (Chair Bettina Umstead absent; 1 present member not voting/stepped out).
votes.discussion_detail: After the waiver vote failed and Superintendent Dr. Lewis nevertheless confirmed from Meet and Confer survey results that meeting frequency and facilitation needed adjustment, Policy Committee Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved to refer Policy 7215 to the Policy Committee for the upcoming academic year rather than bumping it ahead of active Tier 2 policies on May 21. Natalie Beyer offered a friendly amendment to reserve 15-20 minutes at the May 21 meeting to discuss Dr. Lewis's feedback, which Carda-Auten declined before Beyer seconded the underlying referral to keep the issue alive. Joy Harrell-Goff opposed the referral as premature prior to next board's tiering, and the motion carried 3-2.

votes.item_title: Approve Policy 4240/7312 (Child Abuse Reports and Investigations) on First Read and Send to May 28
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Pitman presented revisions to Policy 4240/7312 clarifying administrators' statutory duty in Section D to report three categories of licensed employee misconduct to the State Board of Education upon termination, suspension without pay, discipline, non-renewal, or resignation, alongside Section H student neglect/abuse resources. Millicent Rogers moved to approve the revisions on first reading and advance the policy to the May 28 board meeting for second reading. Joy Harrell-Goff seconded, and the motion passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Policy 5150/7313 (Reporting to External Agencies) on First Read and Place on May 28 Consent
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Policy Committee review, Jessica Carda-Auten moved to approve Policy 5150/7313 regarding external agency reporting on first reading and place it on the May 28 consent agenda. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. No objections or edits were raised, and the board passed it 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Policy 4326 (Rules for Use of Seclusion and Restraint in Schools) on First Read
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead absent; board reached consensus directing Attorney Jason Weber and staff to review DAEC feedback ahead of May 21 Policy Committee.
votes.discussion_detail: Members spent nearly 25 minutes discussing DAEC advocacy on Policy 4326, including parent notification timing, prohibition of mechanical restraints, and whether Attorney Jason Weber could vet additional DAEC edits within two business days before the May 21 Policy Committee. Carda-Auten noted administration had already addressed most points in a public Q&A document and asked Weber to review remaining items before or during the committee session. Joy Harrell-Goff moved approval of Policy 4326 on first reading, Natalie Beyer seconded, and the motion carried 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Policy 4301 (Elementary and Secondary Student Code of Conduct) on First Read and Advance to June Work Session for Second Read
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead absent; board declined to waive work-session action rule prematurely before staff gathered teacher/counselor/family feedback.
votes.discussion_detail: Assistant Superintendent Chanel Sidbury, Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry, and Dr. Melissa Watson presented Policy 4301 revisions embedding restorative practices, behavior matrices, mandatory intervention documentation, and structured re-entry planning while noting 16-17% suspension reductions and 30 kindergarten suspensions (mostly Black or disabled students, often miscoded). Members clashed over whether to prohibit all PreK-3 or K-5 suspensions for Level 1B disrespect versus preserving limited safety discretion and staff readiness, with staff requesting more time to consult counselors, teachers, and families. Natalie Beyer moved (seconded by Millicent Rogers) to pass first read and return Policy 4301 to the June work session discussion agenda for second reading, passing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: After confirming follow-up items—including a board consensus request for de-identified school-level discipline data—Natalie Beyer moved to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Jessica Carda-Auten seconded. The six present board members voted Aye (6-0) by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/14/26
disagreements.issue: Bypassing Policy Committee Tier Queue (Policy 2231) to Discuss Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer)
disagreements.summary: The board split sharply over whether two board members could use Policy 2330 agenda rules to bring proposed Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) edits directly to the board table without going through Policy 2231's prioritized tiering queue.
disagreements.side_a_position: Permit two board members to place Policy 7215 discussion on the work session agenda and clarify conflicts with Policy 2231 prior to May 31 certification.
side_a_arguments: Policy 2330 grants any two board members the right to place items on an agenda for discussion.
Policies coming out of Meet and Confer face an unresolved procedural conflict with Policy 2231 ahead of the May 31 annual certification deadline.
Full-board discussion is necessary rather than confining debate to Policy Committee members.
disagreements.side_b_position: Enforce Policy 2231 strictly so Policy 7215 cannot jump ahead of 30 tiered policies already voted on by the full board.
side_b_arguments: Policy 2231 was crafted specifically to stop small groups of board members from shopping unprioritized policies outside committee.
Twelve Tier 2 and 18 Tier 3 policies (on seclusion/restraint, K-2 suspensions, AI, lactation, and LGBTQ+ support) wait in the queue.
DAE leadership and administration were not consulted as co-chairs on these redlines.
disagreements.resolution: The two-thirds motion to waive Policy 2231 failed; a subsequent motion by Carda-Auten to refer Policy 7215 to the Policy Committee for the next academic year passed 3-2.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 5/14/26
disagreements.issue: Extent of PreK-5 Suspension Prohibitions and Staffing Support Under Policy 4301
disagreements.summary: Members agreed on expanding restorative practices in Policy 4301 but differed on whether to ban Level 1B/all suspensions up through Grade 3 or Grade 5 immediately given budget and staffing cuts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prohibit Level 1B suspensions (disrespect/non-compliance) for young students, include PreK-3 explicitly, and expand supervisor/EC checks across K-5.
side_a_arguments: Thirty kindergarteners were already suspended this year, disproportionately Black and disabled students.
Exclusionary discipline worsens chronic absenteeism and causes developmental harm.
disagreements.side_b_position: Start with PreK-2 limits, preserve principal/supervisor discretion for serious safety issues, and ensure staff capacity before banning higher grades.
side_b_arguments: Grades 3-5 have New Directions support while K-2 does not, and staffing cuts under an uncertain county/state budget strain school-level capacity.
Restorative practices must be taught proactively rather than imposed without resources late in the school year.
disagreements.resolution: Approved on first read 6-0 directing staff to gather additional counselor, teacher, and family input ahead of June second reading.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/23/26
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 23, 2026 monthly meeting chaired by Bettina Umstead, Dr. Lewis warned of proposed FY27 federal cuts ($2.3B overall and $890M in multilingual funding) alongside a projected $7.2M local state-allotment reduction, while public commenters packed the room over Murray Massenberg art teacher Elvin Herrera's J-1/H-1B visa extension, foreign-exchange student caps, Little River mold/security delays, and Brogden express bus stops. Staff reported that preliminary chronic absenteeism stood at 37.3% (~11,000 students), prompting board demands for root-cause accountability. After spirited debates over opportunity-scholarship wording and ICE/federal-officer school-entry protocols, the board unanimously (7-0) adopted its 'Better than Basics' legislative priorities and second-reading revisions to Policy 5120 (Relationship with Law Enforcement).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order and led celebrations for Students of the Month Jose Aleman and Jennifer Serrano, Battle of the Books champions, Superintendent's Student Advisory Council seniors, E.K. Powe's IB Primary Years Programme authorization, and Spark Pin recipient Juanita Avery. Dr. Lewis highlighted May 1's optional teacher workday, federal FY27 budget threats, and DPS's $7.2M state reduction.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, March 26 Minutes, and Student Representative Introduction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the agenda 7-0 with a friendly amendment updating Legislative Steering Committee materials and marking them for action, approved the March 26 monthly minutes 7-0, and welcomed DSA senior Kayla Cabrera as student representative.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers addressed Little River HVAC/mold and an 18-day security repair delay (Katie McDonough, Patricia Russick), Lyons Farm overcrowding and H-1B visas (Kayla Curran), expanding high school foreign exchange caps/age limits and Say Something training (Shahd, Pauline Myers, Melissa Stansbury, Morgan Whitmore), retaining Murray Massenberg art teacher Elvin Herrera on a visa extension (Katherine Hester Doring, Eric Pridshaw, Pete Crawford), and supporting express bus stops at Brogden (Samira Wellamire).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Budget Amendment #2 and ThoughtExchange Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Representative Marcia Morey acknowledged in attendance, the board unanimously approved the consent agenda containing Budget Amendment #2 and the ThoughtExchange contract.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 2 Update: Attendance and Chronic Absenteeism
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chanel Sidbury and Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry presented attendance data showing 37.3% preliminary chronic absenteeism (~11,000 students, trailing peer districts) despite a 1.3-point YoY gain through month 6, 21 schools meeting benchmarks, day-2 absence outreach, and doubled Elna B. Spaulding Conflict Resolution referrals. Board members pressed for root-cause analyses, linkage to suspensions/economic pressures/November immigration enforcement, and verification of statutory 3/6/10-day notices.

agenda_items.title: Legislative Steering Committee Priorities ('Better than Basics')
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Millicent Rogers and Joy Harrell-Goff presented three streamlined priorities—fully funding K-12 adequacy, supporting every learner (weighted formula/lifting EC, ELL, AIG caps), and demanding accountability across vouchers and charters—designed for coalition-building with rural districts. After debating voucher terminology ('moratorium' vs 'phase out' and 'opportunity scholarships' vs 'vouchers') and charter expansion wording, the board adopted the priorities 7-0 pending edits.

agenda_items.title: Policy 5120: Relationship with Law Enforcement (Second Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pitman, Executive Director of Safety Miklo Bynum, and Anthony White presented second-reading revisions to Policy 5120 on law enforcement and federal immigration enforcement. Members debated whether Section F1 contradicted itself by telling immigration agents to contact the Superintendent and 'report to the school's main office', with Bynum warning against placing principals in RDO confrontations, and refined F1, F2, D7, and F12 on the floor before passing the policy 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Grants, Gifts, and Donations and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board acknowledged informational grants, gifts, and donations and voted 7-0 to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve Agenda (With Friendly Amendment Updating Legislative Steering Materials and Marking for Action)
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer initially moved approval of the agenda as presented, seconded by Vice Chair Millicent Rogers. Before the vote, Rogers apologized for inaccurate figures in the originally posted Legislative Steering Committee packet and requested substituting an updated document and marking the item for action. Beyer accepted the friendly amendment, Rogers confirmed it, and the amended agenda passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve March 26, 2026 Regular Monthly Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead called for action on the minutes of the March 26, 2026 monthly board meeting. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved approval of the minutes and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded. Hearing no corrections or further discussion, the board passed the minutes unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Legislative Steering Committee Priorities Pending Discussed Edits
votes.notes: Three core priorities: Fully Fund Public K-12 Instruction to Reach Adequacy; Support Every Learner; Invest in Educators, Demand Real Accountability, and Protect Public Education.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers and Joy Harrell-Goff presented the Legislative Steering Committee's streamlined three-part 'Better than Basics' agenda intended to build coalition advocacy with rural North Carolina school boards. Members debated whether to refer to vouchers as 'opportunity scholarships' and call for a 'moratorium' versus 'phase out,' clarified weighted funding parity for ELL and AIG students alongside EC caps, and adjusted language on a statewide single-operator charter school study so it would not imply endorsement of charter expansion. Pending those edits, Joy Harrell-Goff moved approval, Natalie Beyer seconded, and the legislative priorities passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Policy 5120 (Relationship with Law Enforcement) on Second Reading With Floor Amendments
votes.notes: Includes Section F15 standard response protocols when immigration officers are on or near school property and November 2025 resolution training requirements.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Pitman walked through second-reading revisions to Policy 5120 vetted by principals, students, the sheriff's office, legal counsel, and new Safety Director Miklo Bynum. Natalie Beyer and Jessica Carda-Auten flagged a contradiction in Section F1 telling immigration officers to both contact central office and 'report to the school's main office'; Bynum and Dr. Lewis cautioned against placing principals in resist-delay-obstruct standoffs if agents arrive with judicial warrants, leading to a compromise in F1 and F2 plus Emily Chávez's clarifications to D7 and F12 permitting principal presence during questioning. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved approval with the evening's floor amendments, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff and Jessica Carda-Auten, passing unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Following informational review of grants, gifts, and donations, Joy Harrell-Goff moved to enter closed session for the statutory purposes stated on the agenda. Natalie Beyer seconded. The board passed the motion unanimously 7-0 and ended the livestream.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/23/26
disagreements.issue: Legislative Priorities Framing on School Vouchers and Charter Expansion
disagreements.summary: Board members debated how forcefully to frame opposition to private school vouchers and charter school expansion while maintaining coalition appeal with rural North Carolina school districts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Use 'school vouchers' instead of 'opportunity scholarships', standardize behind a full moratorium, and avoid wording implying support for charter expansion.
side_a_arguments: 'Opportunity scholarships' sanitizes public subsidies for private schools.
Charter study wording must not sound like DPS endorses expanding single-operator charter chains.
disagreements.side_b_position: Use statutory/NCSBA terminology ('opportunity scholarships', pause/phase-out, accountability & transparency) to maximize coalition reach with rural boards.
side_b_arguments: Focusing on public accountability and adequate K-12 funding attracts non-traditional rural partners.
Phasing out recognizes lower-income families currently relying on scholarships while transitioning back.
disagreements.resolution: Adopted 7-0 keeping NCSBA-consistent 'opportunity scholarship' phrasing for coalition alignment while revising the charter bullet to 'ensure if expansion is necessary, it is done responsibly'.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 4/23/26
disagreements.issue: Policy 5120 Federal Immigration Enforcement Entry & Main-Office Protocol (F1 & F2)
disagreements.summary: Members and district safety leadership debated whether Policy 5120 Section F1 should remove 'report to the school's main office' and instruct principals to ask unannounced immigration officers to wait outside or in the main office.
disagreements.side_a_position: Remove 'report to the school's main office' from F1 so policy clearly expects contact with the Superintendent's office first, and require principals in F2 to ask agents to wait outside or in the main office.
side_a_arguments: Telling agents to contact central office and simultaneously report to a school's main office contradicts itself.
Clear written boundaries protect students and limit campus disruption while central legal counsel verifies judicial warrants.
disagreements.side_b_position: Preserve practical main-office containment without putting unarmed school principals in confrontational standoffs telling federal agents to leave.
side_b_arguments: Executive Director Miklo Bynum and Dr. Lewis warned agents arrive already inside buildings in uniform and directing principals to turn them away risks resist-delay-obstruct liability.
disagreements.resolution: Compromise amendments adopted 7-0: F1 directs officers to contact the Superintendent's office or district administrators before visiting, while F2 directs principals at the site to ask officers to wait outside or in the main office while notifying district leadership.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 4/20/26
meetings.executive_summary: At a brief special called meeting on April 20, 2026 presided over by Vice Chair Millicent Rogers (with Chair Bettina Umstead and Wendell Tabb absent, and Jessica Carda-Auten attending remotely), the board addressed anticipated widespread staff absences ahead of the May 1 statewide public education rally in Raleigh. After hearing that 658+ certified teachers and 15 bus drivers had already submitted leave requests—with projections expected to climb further—the board voted 5-0 by roll call to designate Friday, May 1, 2026 as an optional teacher workday across all three district calendars.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers called the special called meeting to order with four members in person and Jessica Carda-Auten participating remotely (Umstead and Tabb absent), and the board approved the single-item agenda 5-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Designation of May 1, 2026 as an Optional Teacher Workday Across All Academic Calendars
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration reported that more than 658 teachers and 15 bus drivers had already requested leave for May 1, 2026—a statewide Raleigh public education advocacy rally—exceeding safe operational and instructional coverage capacity. The board voted 5-0 by roll call to convert May 1 into an optional teacher workday across traditional, specialty, and year-round calendars.

votes.item_title: Approve Special Called Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead and Wendell Tabb absent; Jessica Carda-Auten participating remotely (requiring roll call vote).
votes.discussion_detail: With Chair Bettina Umstead and Wendell Tabb absent and Jessica Carda-Auten participating remotely, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers convened the special called meeting and conducted a roll call vote on the agenda. Carda-Auten, Joy Harrell-Goff, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Rogers all voted Aye. The agenda passed 5-0.

votes.item_title: Designate May 1, 2026 as an Optional Teacher Workday Across All Three Academic Calendars
votes.notes: Applies to traditional, specialty, and year-round calendars; instructional hours remained compliant without needing makeup days.
votes.discussion_detail: Superintendent Dr. Lewis and HR staff reported that over 658 certified teachers and 15 bus drivers had already entered absence requests for Friday, May 1, 2026 to participate in the statewide public education rally in Raleigh, creating unsustainable instructional and transportation shortages if schools remained open. Staff confirmed that DPS calendars retained sufficient instructional-hour cushion to designate May 1 as an optional teacher workday across traditional, specialty, and year-round schedules without adding makeup days. Emily Chávez moved approval, Joy Harrell-Goff seconded, and the five present board members voted unanimously Aye (5-0) by roll call.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/9/26
meetings.executive_summary: At the April 9, 2026 monthly work session—opened after a solemn moment of silence for two DPS elementary students detained and deported following an asylum check-in—board members approved the agenda and March 12 minutes 7-0, then pulled Consent Item 2A (School Nutrition bid renewals) to Item 7A until missing contract details were uploaded and approved 7-0 later that night. Public speakers urged retaining Murray Massenberg art teacher Elvin Herrera on a visa extension, scrutinizing capital site-size assumptions, selling three acres of DSA for affordable housing, and weighing Brogden versus DSA impacts of express busing. Following a Strategic Plan Priority 3 HR/retention update (highlighting 17.2% teacher attrition and ending grant-funded TA-to-Teacher cohorts) and a heated equity-versus-notice debate on Anthony White's secondary magnet express-stop proposal, the board signaled straw-poll consensus to advance only the 2026-27 pilot at DSA and Brogden DLI while deferring Phase 2 expansion pending fall Q1 data.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and March 12 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board opened with a moment of silence honoring two DPS elementary students detained and deported after an asylum appointment in Charlotte earlier in the week, then unanimously approved the evening agenda and the March 12, 2026 work session minutes (7-0).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Fifteen speakers testified on topics including gratitude for transportation leadership (Keitura Mason); urgent pleas for a J-1/H-1B continuation exception for Murray Massenberg art teacher Elvin Herrera (Natasia Rodriguez Autt, Katherine Hester Doring, Taylor Cook, Jonathan Zeil, Emily Barnacle, Lily Whitten, Mike Trusy, Pete Crawford); opposition to secondary magnet express busing after lottery closure (Chad Hafley); March 30/April 8 closed-session quorum legality questions (Rob Fields); state school-size guidelines (John Hodges-Copple); and selling three acres of DSA to Durham County for affordable housing (Jim Svara).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Item 2B Approved; Item 2A Deferred to Item 7A)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Jessica Carda-Auten flagged that School Nutrition Services bid renewal contracts (Item 2A) were missing from BoardDocs, Natalie Beyer amended her consent motion to approve Item 2B (custodial floor finish) immediately and defer 2A to Item 7A so staff could upload contract terms.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 3 Update: Recruit, Support, and Retain Exemplary Staff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR leaders Michelle Hayes, Terry Phillips, Dr. Idahor, and Operations's Anthony White presented Priority 3 metrics—including 17.2% prior-year teacher attrition (24% recouped), cessation of new NCCU TA-to-Teacher cohorts after MacKenzie Scott funds ended, Child Nutrition's 76% Manager-in-Training rate, Spanish training for 19 transit staff, 290 J-1 and 19 H-1B teachers, and workforce demographics (7% Hispanic teachers vs ~33% student body). Board members pressed for ROI metrics on EC/ESL/Masters differentials and requested a future meeting on international teacher visa renewals.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote (consensus for follow-up reports)

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: School Library Month (April 2026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Curriculum Director Gabby Hall and Media Lead Heidi Perez honored DPS library media coordinators, board members read the April 2026 School Library Month proclamation aloud, and Natalie Beyer sought future data on school library circulation, vacancies, and early college lending collections (noting DECHS lacks a dedicated library).

agenda_items.title: Secondary Magnet Transportation Express Stops Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Anthony White proposed standardizing secondary magnet busing using existing DPS schools as express stops—piloting DSA (cutting 563 stops to 71 and 57 route hours to 20, saving $53.5k+ in fuel and reducing cascading lateness to Riverside and Northern) and Brogden DLI in 2026-27, and expanding to all secondary magnets in 2027-28 while protecting IEP transit and offering hardship appeals. Divided over locking in 2027-28 expansion before Q1 data, members reached non-binding consensus to advance only the 2026-27 pilot and revisit broader expansion in October/November.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Straw poll consensus on 2026-27 pilot

agenda_items.title: Overnight Field Trips (Informational)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Standard informational notice of approved overnight field trips.

agenda_items.title: School Nutrition Services Bid Renewals for 2026-2027 School Year
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Once usage-based contract documents were uploaded to BoardDocs, Child Nutrition Director Jim Keaten explained Sysco (~$5M estimated usage), milk, produce, and Firsthand Foods shifts, after which the board approved the bid renewals as an action item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Summary of Follow-Up Items and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pitman summarized follow-ups on Priority 3 goal metrics, compensation-differential retention/recruitment data, J-1 visa policy review, and Oct/Nov express-stop pilot reporting before the board entered closed session 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Work Session Agenda as Presented
votes.discussion_detail: Following an opening moment of silence acknowledging two DPS elementary students detained and deported during an asylum appointment in Charlotte, the board reviewed the April 9 work session agenda. Natalie Beyer moved to approve the agenda as presented, and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded. Hearing no requested revisions, all seven board members voted Aye (7-0).

votes.item_title: Approve March 12, 2026 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Next, the board considered the draft minutes of the March 12, 2026 work session. Joy Harrell-Goff moved approval of the minutes as written and Natalie Beyer seconded. No corrections were offered, and the minutes passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Proclamation for School Library Month (April 2026)
votes.discussion_detail: Curriculum and Instruction Director Gabby Hall and Media Lead Heidi Perez presented the April 2026 School Library Month proclamation recognizing DPS media coordinators' support for diverse collections and CTE/IB academic databases. Board members read the proclamation aloud sequentially. Natalie Beyer moved approval, seconded by Chair Bettina Umstead, while asking staff to share school-level circulation volumes, librarian vacancy counts, and library plans for Durham Early College of Health Sciences; the proclamation passed 7-0.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Upon reviewing Dr. Pitman's recap of the evening's follow-up directives, Joy Harrell-Goff moved to enter closed session for the statutory purposes stated on the agenda. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. All seven board members voted Aye (7-0) and concluded the livestream.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/9/26
disagreements.issue: International Teacher J-1 to H-1B Visa Renewal Policy and Retention Exemptions
disagreements.summary: Following public outcry over Murray Massenberg art teacher Elvin Herrera, board members questioned administration's refusal to pursue H-1B visa transitions for J-1 international teachers.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question why pandemic-era H-1B exceptions ended without board notice and explore retention pathways for exemplary international teachers.
side_a_arguments: DPS relies on over 300 international educators across dual-language, IB, ESL, and hard-to-staff subjects, and charter schools are hiring them away.
Board members were not consulted when HR shifted back from pandemic-era visa extensions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Standard practice always limited J-1 cultural exchange contracts to 3+2 years with mandatory two-year home residency, and pandemic H-1Bs were strictly temporary exceptions.
side_b_arguments: Participants and partner agencies explicitly contract under J-1 cultural exchange rules rather than permanent H-1B immigration tracks.
No board policy was changed; administration simply resumed standard compliance.
disagreements.resolution: Board majority gave thumbs-up consensus to schedule a deeper future board briefing and discussion on international teacher visa policies.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 4/9/26
disagreements.issue: Secondary Magnet Express Bus Stops: Immediate 2027-28 Commitment vs 2026-27 Pilot Only
disagreements.summary: Board members split over whether to give conditional approval now to roll out express bus stops to all secondary magnets in 2027-28 (to give lottery families notice) or limit direction strictly to the 2026-27 pilot at DSA and Brogden DLI.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve planning for Phase 2 expansion to all secondary magnets in 2027-28 now (subject to later rollback if needed) so families know before magnet lotteries.
side_a_arguments: Notifying prospective 2027-28 lottery applicants in advance is fairer than announcing express stops after seats are accepted.
Rolling back from express stops to door-to-door is operationally easier than surprising families late.
disagreements.side_b_position: Separate out the 2026-27 pilot (DSA and Brogden DLI) and withhold any commitment on other secondary magnets until Q1 data is reviewed by the incoming board.
side_b_arguments: Data from the DSA/Brogden pilot will not exist until fall 2026, when four newly elected members take office.
Express stops carry equity risks that could deter lower-income families from secondary magnets and Growing Together programs.
disagreements.resolution: Consensus reached (thumbs up) to proceed with planning/communication for the 2026-27 DSA and Brogden DLI pilot while bringing comprehensive Q1 operational and equity data back in late October or early November 2026—before Showcase of Schools—so the new board can decide 2027-28 expansion.
