meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/26/26
meetings.executive_summary: With five board members present (Wendell Tabb and Joy Harrell-Goff absent), Chair Bettina Umstead led the March 26, 2026 monthly meeting, passing all seven formal actions by unanimous 5-0 votes. The board adopted a modified NCSBA resolution urging state budget passage (adding local ELL and AIG funding-cap data and 'at a minimum' framing) and adopted the Superintendent's FY 2026-27 Recommended Budget—requesting $25.70M in current-expense increases (anchored by a 12.08% classified pay raise to $19.22/hr) and $7.82M in capital outlay including $2.82M in Chromebook and classroom display leases after reigning in $24.3M internally. Members also approved the extracurricular activities list for the new High School Arts Proficiency Graduation Endorsement (5-0) and received a Community Schools update announcing Student U's 2026-27 expansion to Brogden and Carrington middle schools.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting recognizing Student of the Month Curtis (Jordan HS), Jordan state swim/track champions, Southern High School's 7A boys basketball state champions, February/March Teachers and Employees of the Month, certified school treasurers and CSBO Reuben Barfield, and OPA's 16 state communication awards, followed by student representative Elizabeth Leathers and Dr. Lewis's March district highlights.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, February 26 Minutes, and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The five present members approved the agenda and February 26 monthly minutes (5-0 each). During public comment, parent Lena Nieland urged redirecting the $2.8M edtech proposal toward staff pay, bus drivers, and HVAC while auditing classroom screen time, and PT Christy Clum warned that posted non-competitive classified pay scales left therapist vacancies unfilled and created massive after-hours IEP paperwork.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through C)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the three consent agenda items (A through C) without discussion.

agenda_items.title: Local Board Resolution Urging State Budget Passage
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members read aloud an NCSBA template resolution urging the General Assembly to enact a state budget before the April 21 short session, highlighting frozen salaries for 4,975 DPS employees and the 13% EC funding cap (costing DPS $6.28M locally at 16.6% EC enrollment). Members amended the draft to add ELL (22.8% vs 10.8% cap) and AIG caps plus 'at a minimum' wording before passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Recommended Budget for FY 2026-2027
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter detailed $24.3M in internal cuts/efficiencies (eliminating lapsed-salary reliance and absorbing $7.27M in state enrollment reductions and $6.6M in projected charter growth) alongside a county ask of +$25,700,127 in current expense (including a 12.08% classified pay raise to $19.22/hr matching Durham County, $100/mo safety assistant supplements, and OT/PT scale floor fixes) and $7,823,488 in capital outlay ($5M lump sum + $1.92M Chromebooks + $900k displays). After debating graduated vs flat raises, comp time vs overtime, and $2.8M edtech vs HVAC, the board adopted the budget 5-0.

agenda_items.title: High School Arts Proficiency Graduation Endorsement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Arts coordinator Mr. Turner presented the board-approved list of no-cost extracurricular arts activities required alongside four arts credits (3.0+ unweighted GPA) and 40 extracurricular hours under State Board policy GRAD-007. Seniors could backdate activities to earn the transcript seal immediately; the board approved the list 5-0 while requesting an arts equity audit for early colleges.

agenda_items.title: DPS Community Schools Update (Student U Partnership)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Student U Executive Director Elena Mina, Dr. Luke Carman, coordinators Gloria Suarez, Kasim Kwali, Shantel Cassels, and Principal Dr. Quincy Farmer reviewed year-one Community Schools implementation at Club Blvd, Lakewood, and Fayetteville Street (1,000+ family resource center visits, School Advisory Boards, NCCU mentors) and announced North Carolina Community Schools Coalition funding expanding the model to Brogden and Carrington middle schools in 2026-27 (2,000+ students).

agenda_items.title: Policy Committee Update, Grants/Donations, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jessica Carda-Auten briefly updated the board on Policy 5120 and Policy 4326 progress, informational grants/gifts/donations were noted, and the five present members entered closed session 5-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Regular Monthly Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb and Joy Harrell-Goff absent for the entire meeting.
votes.discussion_detail: With Wendell Tabb and Joy Harrell-Goff absent from the March 26 monthly meeting, Chair Bettina Umstead called for agenda approval from the five members present. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved approval of the agenda as presented and Natalie Beyer seconded. The motion passed unanimously 5-0.

votes.item_title: Approve February 26, 2026 Regular Monthly Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb and Joy Harrell-Goff absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead presented the minutes from the February 26, 2026 regular monthly board meeting. Jessica Carda-Auten moved to approve the minutes as submitted and Natalie Beyer seconded. With no corrections requested, the five present members voted unanimously 5-0 to adopt the minutes.

votes.item_title: Adopt Local Board Resolution Urging State Budget Passage (With Floor Amendments)
votes.notes: Authorized Chair Bettina Umstead and Dr. Lewis to finalize wording with staff and disseminate to legislators and Governor ahead of April 21 short session.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members read aloud the NCSBA template resolution condemning nine months of General Assembly budget inaction that kept 4,975 DPS employees frozen on 2024-25 pay scales amid rising health premiums and forced DPS to spend $6.28M locally above the 13% EC cap. Emily Chávez proposed adding a parallel whereas clause detailing ELL students (22.8% enrolled vs 10.8% state cap) and AIG caps, while Natalie Beyer added 'at a minimum' to the resolved request so House-bill minimums would not cap DPS advocacy. Beyer moved approval as amended, Jessica Carda-Auten seconded, and the resolution passed 5-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Superintendent's Recommended Budget for FY 2026-2027
votes.notes: Authorizes submitting county request for +$25,700,127 in local current expense (12.08% classified raise to $19.22/hr living wage) and $7,823,488 in capital outlay ($5M lump sum + $1.92M Chromebooks + $900k classroom displays); distribution adjustments deferred until June county allocation.
votes.discussion_detail: CFO Jeremy Teeter presented the FY 2026-27 Superintendent's Recommended Budget, detailing $24.3M in internal expenditure reductions and enrollment/charter absorption before requesting $25.70M in additional county current-expense funding (driven by a 12.08% classified raise to match Durham County's $19.22/hr minimum wage, safety assistant supplements, and OT/PT scale adjustments) plus $7.82M in capital outlay including $2.82M for Chromebook and TouchView display leases. Emily Chávez urged later exploring graduated classified raises (smaller percentages for upper administrators) and shifting hourly staff from comp time to overtime pay, while members debated the $2.82M edtech request with student rep Elizabeth Leathers underscoring outdated early-college projectors. Natalie Beyer moved adoption so the request could go across the street to Durham County, Emily Chávez seconded, and the budget passed 5-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Extracurricular Activities List for High School Arts Proficiency Graduation Endorsement
votes.notes: Implements NC State Board policy GRAD-007 allowing seniors to backdate 40 extracurricular arts hours.
votes.discussion_detail: Arts curriculum leader Mr. Turner presented the district's board-required list of no-cost, equitable arts-related extracurricular activities qualifying students toward the new North Carolina Arts Proficiency Graduation Endorsement alongside four arts credits with a 3.0 unweighted GPA. Student representative Elizabeth Leathers applauded the endorsement while urging stronger arts offerings at early colleges, prompting Natalie Beyer and Bettina Umstead to call for an arts equity audit across all high schools. Emily Chávez moved approval of the activity list, Natalie Beyer seconded, and the motion passed 5-0.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb and Joy Harrell-Goff absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the Student U Community Schools expansion briefing and Policy Committee/grants informational updates, Natalie Beyer moved to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Emily Chávez seconded. The five present board members voted Aye (5-0) and adjourned open broadcast.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/26/26
disagreements.issue: Flat 12.08% vs Graduated Classified Pay Scale Raise Distribution
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed philosophically over applying a flat 12.08% raise across all classified steps versus graduating percentages downward for senior central administrators.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore a graduated raise model awarding 12% to lower-paid staff and smaller percentages at the coordinator-and-above tiers.
side_a_arguments: A uniform 12% raise grants roughly $19,000 to a step-zero assistant superintendent versus $4,336 to a transportation safety assistant.
Equity requires lifting workers at the bottom of the wage scale proportionally more.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain uniform 12.08% modeling in the county request to avoid pay compression and protect upward career incentives.
side_b_arguments: Trimming percentages at upper tiers worsens salary compression between supervisors and staff and impacts employees nearing retirement.
Final salary-scale adjustments should wait until Durham County announces actual June funding.
disagreements.resolution: Adopted the full budget request 5-0 while CFO Jeremy Teeter agreed to partner with the board to revisit distribution philosophy once final county appropriations arrive in June.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 3/26/26
disagreements.issue: Capital Technology Lease ($2.82M Chromebooks & Interactive Displays) vs Facilities/Screen-Time Concerns
disagreements.summary: Public commenters and several board members questioned prioritizing $2.82M in leased Chromebooks and BrightLink replacements over HVAC repairs and screen-time limits.
disagreements.side_a_position: Scrutinize $2.8M technology spending relative to HVAC repairs, teacher pay, and childhood screen-time risks.
side_a_arguments: Voters and parents raised research linking heavy classroom screen time to declining literacy/math outcomes and asked whether all 17,173 Chromebooks and 1,786 displays are strictly needed.
disagreements.side_b_position: Fund multi-year leases to replace failing 13-year-old projectors and out-of-warranty Chromebooks to prevent instructional disruption and digital inequity.
side_b_arguments: NC law bars using capital outlay funds for employee salaries.

Chromebook repairs exceed $500,000 annually, 13-year-old BrightLink bulbs fail mid-lesson, and cutting 1:1 devices widens the digital divide for Black and brown students whose families can opt out online.
disagreements.resolution: Budget passed 5-0 including the $2.82M capital technology leases, paired with requests for future reporting on opt-out rates, classroom screen time, and instructional tech planning.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/12/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its March monthly work session under Chair Millicent Rogers, passing revisions to Policy 5120 on law enforcement and immigration visits on first read (referred back to the March 19 Policy Committee), adopting proclamations for Arts in Our Schools Month and a resolution supporting Kids Over Corporations, and approving Consent Agenda Items A-J. During public comment, educators, custodians, and therapists raised urgent concerns over Little River facility mold, 80-to-85-degree classrooms at Southern High School, custodial extra-duty caps, OT/PT/COTA pay, and Spanish interpretation delays. CFO Jeremy Teter presented Phase 2 FY 2026-27 budget simulator options including a county-matched $19.22/hour classified wage floor ($13.29M total cost), OT/PT schedule realignment ($302,596), safety assistant supplements, and a $5M plus $2.8M technology plan for grades 6-12 Chromebooks, sparking a sharp debate over whether to include extra duty pay now or audit school-level payroll inconsistencies first.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Celebrations, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Work Session Chair Millicent Rogers opened the meeting, introduced student representatives, and led a moment of silence honoring DPS educator Kwame Hester and community members. Celebrations recognized student and school achievements across the district.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Approval, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members amended the agenda to add the Resolution of the DPS Board of Education in Support of Kids Over Corporations as Item 4C and subsequently adopted the amended agenda. The Board also reviewed and approved the minutes from the February 9, 2026 Monthly Work Session.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parents, teachers, custodians, and therapists addressed persistent mold, carpet, and wallpaper issues at Little River Elementary and extreme classroom temperatures (80-85 degrees Fahrenheit) at Southern High School. Custodians and specialists described unpaid extra duty hours, rising health insurance costs, OT/PT/COTA pay disparities, and delays or equipment failures in Spanish interpretation.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-J)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board considered Consent Agenda Items A through J without pulling any items for separate debate. During the vote, Wendell Tabb joined the meeting, bringing attendance to six members.

agenda_items.title: Policy 5120: Relationship with Law Enforcement (First Read)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed draft revisions to Policy 5120 addressing campus interactions with local and federal law enforcement, including immigration enforcement. Emily Chávez, Bettina Umstead, and Joy Harrell-Goff sought clarification on whether principals were clearly designated as responsible decision-makers, how judicial warrants are verified, and the scope of exigent circumstances before returning the policy to the March 19 Policy Committee.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Arts in Our Schools Month (March 1-31, 2026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members and a Hillside High School marching band student read the proclamation celebrating visual and performing arts educators, designers, and stage managers across DPS. Members highlighted how arts education strengthens cultural identity, student engagement, and social-emotional well-being; Emily Chávez arrived prior to the vote.

agenda_items.title: Introduction to 2026 North Carolina K-12 ELA Standards
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Superintendent Chanel Sidbury and Curriculum Director Elizabeth Moffett outlined the newly approved 2026 North Carolina English Language Arts Standard Course of Study and an 18-month district implementation timeline. agenda_items.title: Resolution in Support of Kids Over Corporations

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham County Board of County Commissioners met jointly on March 11, 2026, approving the meeting agenda and November 19, 2025 joint minutes unanimously. DPS operations leadership presented a sobering draft Capital Improvement Plan highlighting a $965M+ maintenance and repair backlog and potential school consolidations across 16 small schools, while County officials cautioned against a 2026 GO Bond due to unspent 2022 bond balances (~$200M spent of $460M) and rising costs. CFO Jeremy Teter and County Budget Director Keith Lane then clashed constructively over FY 2026-27 finances, with the County warning of an 'inflection point' ($8.7M natural revenue growth against $13.5M baseline county needs after back-to-back 6% property tax hikes) and DPS board members pressing for county-matched $19.22/hr wages and urgent HVAC/facility funding.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Agenda Review, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened the joint quarterly meeting with DPS Board members and Durham County Commissioners and thanked the Multilingual Resource Center interpreters. Both boards unanimously approved the agenda as presented and the November 19, 2025 joint meeting minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed unanimously (both procedural and minutes motions)

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Planning (CIP) Process and Bond Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS COO Kenneth Barnes and Devon Mitchell outlined a draft CIP addressing a $965M+ maintenance and repair backlog, a 16-school small-enrollment watchlist, potential consolidations (such as Club Blvd and George Watts to the DSA site, Y.E. Smith and Eastway, and Fuller/SDC/Bacon St), and long-range facility needs. County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane stressed shovel-readiness, inflation in aluminum/construction costs, and slower 2022 bond drawdowns (~$200M spent of $460M), signaling reluctance toward a 2026 GO Bond in favor of smaller LOBS increments, while Commissioner Jacobs advocated UNC Development Finance Initiative (DFI) adaptive reuse and teacher housing for Old Northern and DSA.

agenda_items.title: DPS and County FY 2026-27 Budget Presentations and Fiscal Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter highlighted finance department reforms—two timely audits, ERP modernization, fund balance recovery, ending reliance on lapsed salaries, $51M in charter pass-through costs, and the $19.22/hr living wage model—while County Manager Claudia Hager and Keith Lane warned of an 'inflection point' with only $8.7M in natural revenue growth versus $13.5M in county base pressures, flat sales tax (+$770K), back-to-back 6% tax hikes, ~29,000 DPS ADM, and 24% locally funded DPS staff positions. DPS Board members Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten pushed back on county constraints by emphasizing failing HVAC systems and living-wage parity.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Update Deferral and BOCC-BOE MOU Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to the late hour, both boards gave informal consensus affirmation without a roll call vote to defer the Pre-K update to the top of the May joint meeting agenda and assign representatives to update the outdated BOCC-BOE Memorandum of Understanding before May. Chair Umstead adjourned the meeting at 02:50:49.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
disagreements.issue: 2026 General Obligation Bond Feasibility, LOBS Alternatives, and School Site Reuse vs. Consolidation
disagreements.summary: DPS operations staff outlined massive long-term capital needs including school consolidations and aging infrastructure, while County staff favored smaller LOBS borrowing over a 2026 GO Bond and County Commissioners pressed for adaptive reuse/teacher housing on surplus sites.
disagreements.side_a_position: Pursue bold capital investment to tackle a $965M+ M&R backlog and address under-enrolled aging elementary schools via consolidation and new construction.
side_a_arguments: DPS faces a $965M+ maintenance and repair backlog and 16 small schools needing long-term capacity solutions.
Board members emphasized failing HVAC systems and 60-to-75-year-old buildings requiring major modernization or consolidation.
disagreements.side_b_position: Prioritize finishing the 2022 bond projects and using incremental LOBS debt rather than a 2026 GO Bond, while exploring UNC DFI adaptive reuse for surplus sites.
side_b_arguments: Roughly $200M of the $460M 2022 bond has been spent so far, raising shovel-readiness questions alongside inflated construction and aluminum costs.

Commissioner Jacobs urged UNC School of Government/DFI partnerships for educator/affordable housing at Old Northern and the DSA campus rather than demolition; Umstead noted UNC SOG feasibility work is already underway.
disagreements.resolution: Informational joint discussion only; both boards deferred further capital and MOU planning to future budget and May joint discussions.

disagreements.issue: FY 2026-27 County Tax Capacity vs. DPS Classified Wage Parity and Local Staffing Levels
disagreements.summary: County budget officials argued Durham County is at a fiscal inflection point limiting major new DPS increases without unpopular tax hikes, while DPS Board members defended living-wage parity ($19.22/hr), facility repairs, and local positions amid rising charter pass-through costs.
disagreements.side_a_position: County revenues cannot sustain large annual funding deltas without further property tax increases, requiring scrutiny of DPS local position growth (24%) amid declining ADM (~29,000).
side_a_arguments: County faces only $8.7M in natural revenue growth against $13.5M in baseline expenditure increases before any DPS or county staff raises.
Sales tax growth flattened (+$770K), federal ARPA/SNAP dollars are expiring, and residents have absorbed back-to-back 6% property tax rate increases.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain county-matched living wages ($19.22/hr), fix failing school HVAC systems, and recognize that $51M in local funding flows out to charter schools.
side_b_arguments: Board members Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten argued DPS cannot retain classified staff without matching county wage floors and addressing inflation.
DPS has already stabilized its finances, ended lapsed-salary dependency, and absorbed rising charter school tuition shares.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; presentations set the framework for April-June County and DPS budget deliberations.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Budget Hearing | 3/5/26
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its dedicated FY 2026-27 public budget hearing on March 5, 2026, opening with a moment of silence and a 4-0 procedural vote approving the agenda before CFO Jeremy Teter previewed a draft request featuring $16M in additional local current expense and $3.7M in capital outlay. Custodians, physical therapists, media coordinators, and an EC instructional assistant testified during the hearing—briefly paused twice to resolve Spanish interpretation audio issues—urging higher classified pay, elimination of 80-hour biweekly custodian caps and unpaid overtime, inclusion of OT/PT assistants in pay realignments, and stronger EC staffing support. Board members and Superintendent Anthony Lewis closed by acknowledging the tension between Durham County's tight fiscal outlook and the urgent financial pressures facing DPS's lowest-paid employees.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead welcomed attendees and led a moment of silence honoring Trooper Perry and a Durham School of Technology teacher and her husband. Four board members present approved the hearing agenda unanimously before two additional members arrived later.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Draft Budget Request Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter presented an overview of the draft FY 2026-27 budget ask totaling $16M in new current expense funds and $3.7M in capital outlay, highlighting continuation assumptions (5% potential state raise, rising insurance/utilities), classified pay options referenced against Duke's $20/hour benchmark, OT/PT/OTA schedule adjustments, removal of the HR expansion item, and grades 6-12 Chromebook replacement.

agenda_items.title: Public Budget Hearing Comments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Employees and advocates testified on budget priorities, paused by two short recesses (00:27:30-00:37:42) to troubleshoot Spanish interpretation audio. Custodians Maria Lopez, Yamileth Ramirez, and Azucena Chavez Trejo described 80-hour caps, unpaid overtime, understaffing, and low wages; media coordinators Kim Gugino and Carolyn Herbert, PTs Heidi Jo Hetland and Krista Klem, and EC IA Quentin Haden urged expanded compensation, OT/PT assistant inclusion, and stronger support above a 5% increase.

agenda_items.title: Board and Superintendent Closing Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members Natalie Beyer and Emily Chávez (appearing as Ms. Gordon in ASR) thanked speakers and reflected on matching county living-wage policy, addressing salary compression, EC funding caps, and aging 60-year-old HVAC/roofs despite County Manager Hager's sobering fiscal warning. Superintendent Lewis reaffirmed commitment to prioritizing lowest-paid classified workers ahead of the March 12 work session draft and March 26 adoption vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Budget Hearing Agenda as Presented

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/26/26
meetings.executive_summary: At a nearly six-hour monthly meeting on February 26, 2026, the DPS Board of Education heard from 38 public speakers—primarily Lions Farm teachers, students, and parents opposing moving specials to carts and relocating EC Pre-K classes, alongside advocates urging stronger Policy 5120 ICE protections, budget transparency, and OT/PT/assistant raises. The Board accepted the FY 2024-25 audited financial statements unanimously, received a sobering FY 2026-27 fiscal outlook from Durham County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane alongside DPS's draft $16M current expense/$3.7M capital budget presentation, and voted 5-2 to approve a 50% after-school care tuition increase while maintaining existing financial assistance. Late in the evening, the Board voted 6-1 (Umstead dissenting) to reorder the Policy Committee's priority queue and voted 6-0 to advance Policy 5120 with attorney amendments to the March work session.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Student representative Alise Tran of Durham Early College of Health Sciences opened the meeting alongside celebrations of staff and students, including Student U's Mayor's Award and National Board Certified Teachers. Superintendent Anthony Lewis highlighted upcoming March 7 events and delivered formal remarks condemning being addressed by his first name by the DAE president at Meet and Confer, calling for mutual respect and professional norms.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Approval, and January 29, 2026 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At Natalie Beyer's request, the Board amended the agenda to pull Item 2F (Policy Committee retiering) to a new Item 5B for full-board debate, then approved the amended agenda and the January 29, 2026 monthly meeting minutes unanimously.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Thirty-eight speakers—including Lions Farm teachers, parents, and elementary students—opposed moving art, music, and STEM onto carts and relocating the EC Developmental Needs Pre-K program due to overcrowding without stakeholder collaboration. Additional speakers urged adopting Durham Public Schools Strong's private-zones version of Policy 5120, prioritizing DAE Meet and Confer budget transparency and grievance policies, elevating seclusion and restraint policy review, renewing international teacher H-1B visas, and including OT/PT assistants in classified pay increases.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-E)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item F previously removed for separate consideration as Item 5B, the Board approved Consent Agenda Items A through E without debate while Emily Chávez had briefly stepped out of the room.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Audited Financial Statements Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Auditor Paul Carson presented an unmodified opinion on the June 30, 2025 financial statements showing local current expense fund balance rising $3M to $11.4M ($7.9M unassigned), though noting four repeat audit findings tied to prior-year delays, $5.3M in transfers plus loans to Child Nutrition, and $183,891 in salary overpayments. CFO Jeremy Teter and staff highlighted child nutrition turnaround under Jim Keaton, zero cash advances needed this year, and new SOP manuals.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Fiscal Outlook and DPS FY 2026-27 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane outlined severe fiscal headwinds—flat sales tax (+$770K), expiring ARPA/SNAP funds, back-to-back tax hikes, and a $5M baseline county deficit ($8.7M revenue growth vs. $13.5M base needs) before any DPS expansion or county raises. CFO Jeremy Teter followed with DPS's draft $16M current expense and $3.7M capital outlay framework (assuming a 5% state raise, 26% charter share, OT/PT schedule updates, HR reorg, and Chromebooks/BrightLinks), while lifting the current-year hiring freeze.

agenda_items.title: After-School Tuition and Fee Increase Proposal (2026-27)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented two sliding-scale options and survey data (742 responses out of 1,767 families) but recommended Option 1, a 50% flat tuition increase (e.g., $205 to $307.50/month) to restore the enterprise fund balance toward $1.5M and fund $19.22/hr group leader pay. After extensive debate over affordability, uncapped financial assistance, and a failed unseconded 50%-discount motion plus a withdrawn October sliding-scale motion from Emily Chávez, the Board voted 5-2 to approve the 50% increase while maintaining current assistance and asking staff to explore donor/DPS Foundation sponsorship options.

agenda_items.title: Policy Committee Update and Policy Priority Retiering
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief recess, the Board debated the Policy Committee's priority queue (previously pulled from consent as Item 2F), weighing Meet and Confer's Budget Transparency and Grievance policies against Seclusion and Restraint, Child Abuse Reporting, and Student Code of Conduct. The Board voted 6-1 (Bettina Umstead dissenting) to approve a 10-policy priority order placing Seclusion and Restraint first, Child Abuse second, Budget Transparency third, and Student Code of Conduct fourth.

agenda_items.title: Policy 5120 Revisions Referral and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Operations Officer Kenneth Barnes, Dr. Pitman, and Policy Chair Jessica Carda-Auten reviewed Policy 5120 track changes across sections F (federal law enforcement visits), H (resources), and I (training) after sheriff and legal consultations. The Board voted 6-0 to place Policy 5120 on the March work session agenda with recommended attorney amendments, reviewed overnight field trips as informational, and entered closed session 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve Agenda as Amended
votes.notes: Chair initially misattributed mover/seconder order before Joy Harrell-Goff and Natalie Beyer clarified.

votes.item_title: Approve January 29, 2026 Monthly Meeting Minutes

Emily Chávez moved approval of the minutes and Vice Chair Millicent Rogers seconded. No board member offered corrections or additions to the record. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Accept FY 2024-25 Audited Financial Statements
votes.notes: Auditor Paul Carson issued unmodified opinions while noting four repeat compliance/control findings.
votes.discussion_detail: Audit partner Paul Carson presented the June 30, 2025 audited financial statements, reporting an unmodified opinion on financial reliability, a $3M local current expense fund balance increase to $11.4M, and four repeat findings concerning bank reconciliations and pre-PO expenditures primarily from early FY 2024-25, alongside a $4.6M pre-transfer Child Nutrition loss and $183,891 in salary overpayments. CFO Jeremy Teter and Superintendent Lewis noted major operational turnaround in Child Nutrition, hiring of credentialed staff including internal auditor Kernney and accounting lead Evelyn Gyos, and completed standard operating procedures; Vice Chair Millicent Rogers emphasized regular treasurer training so systems survive staff turnover. Rogers moved acceptance of the audited financial statements, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve 50% After-School Care Tuition Increase While Maintaining Current Financial Assistance
votes.notes: Joy Harrell-Goff also seconded; Emily Chávez's prior motion for a 50% discount died for lack of a second [04:43:47], and her subsequent October sliding-scale motion [04:45:35] was withdrawn [04:53:53]. Voice vote did not record individual member votes.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff recommended a 50% flat tuition increase (lifting elementary rates from $205 to $307.50/month) after presenting survey data and sliding-scale models showing administrative verification bottlenecks and revenue risks to the enterprise fund balance, which had fallen to $242,819 against a $1.5M reserve target. Natalie Beyer favored a gentler 40% phased increase and donor-funded scholarships, while Emily Chávez moved a 50% increase paired with a 50% low-income discount that died for lack of a second at 04:43:47. Millicent Rogers then moved to adopt administration's 50% recommendation while maintaining existing financial assistance, seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten and Joy Harrell-Goff, after Carda-Auten urged avoiding caps on eligible discount applicants and promoting assistance visibility. The motion carried 5-2 by voice vote, followed by consensus (after Chávez withdrew a follow-up motion) for annual reviews and exploring DPS Foundation sponsorship options.

votes.item_title: Adopt Revised Policy Committee Priority Tiering Order
votes.notes: Chair Umstead announced she dissented ('6-1') because she wanted Student Code of Conduct placed higher to meet summer handbook printing deadlines.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members debated how to sequence ten pending policies in the Policy Committee queue, balancing DAE Meet and Confer drafts (Budget Transparency and Grievance Policy) against student safety urgency following recent indictments and restraint concerns. Wendell Tabb, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Superintendent Lewis urged elevating Seclusion and Restraint and Child Abuse Reporting to the top, while Bettina Umstead also pushed to move up the Student Code of Conduct ahead of handbook printing deadlines. Emily Chávez moved a ten-policy sequence—1. Seclusion & Restraint, 2. Child Abuse Reports & Investigations, 3. Budget Transparency, 4. Student Code of Conduct, 5. Disciplinary Action for EC, 6. Grievance Policy, 7. Transportation, 8. Teleworking, 9. Inclement Weather Absences, 10. Multiple NCSBA Policies—seconded by Wendell Tabb. The motion carried 6-1, with Bettina Umstead stating on the record that she dissented because Student Code of Conduct should come earlier.

votes.item_title: Place Policy 5120 on March Work Session Agenda with Recommended Attorney Amendments
votes.notes: Emily Chávez stepped out before the vote.
votes.discussion_detail: After Dr. Pitman and Policy Committee Chair Jessica Carda-Auten reviewed track-change updates to Policy 5120 (sections F, H, and I) and confirmed coordination with Sheriff's Office Captain Hinton, board members sought a faster pathway given the late hour and the next committee date falling on March 19. Natalie Beyer suggested incorporating legal counsel Jason Weber's clear recommended edits into the draft before the March 12 work session so the full board could review an updated text immediately. Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved to place Policy 5120 on the March work session agenda for First Read with recommended attorney amendments, and Natalie Beyer seconded. With Emily Chávez momentarily absent, the six remaining members voted unanimously 6-0 in favor.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Emily Chávez stepped out; board did not return to open session.
votes.discussion_detail: Following informational review of overnight and international field trips, Chair Bettina Umstead invited a motion to convene in closed session. Joy Harrell-Goff moved to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, and Natalie Beyer seconded. No debate occurred on the procedural motion. The six board members present voted unanimously 6-0 in favor.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 2/26/26
disagreements.issue: 50% Flat After-School Tuition Increase vs. Lower/Phased Rate and Expanded Low-Income Discounts
disagreements.summary: Board members split 5-2 over adopting administration's recommended 50% flat tuition hike while maintaining current financial assistance versus adopting a gentler 40% increase or pairing the 50% rate with a 50% discount for low-income families.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve administration's 50% tuition increase with existing financial assistance to prevent the enterprise fund from running in the red and restore reserves toward $1.5M.
side_a_arguments: Tuition had been frozen for nearly a decade while group-leader wage targets rose toward $19.22/hr and COVID stabilization grants expired.
Even at 50% ($307.50/month or ~$4/hour), DPS after-school care remains well below local market rates and DSS child-care voucher ceilings.
disagreements.side_b_position: Soften the immediate financial shock on working families via a 40% phased increase or a 50% discount offset by higher-income contributions.
side_b_arguments: A sudden 50% increase hits lower-income families disproportionately amid regional layoffs and inflation.
Emily Chávez sought a 50% discount for eligible families (motion died for lack of a second) while Natalie Beyer urged a 40% rate paired with a donor scholarship fund.
disagreements.resolution: Main motion passed 5-2 by voice vote adopting the 50% increase with current assistance, paired with informal board direction to explore donor/DPS Foundation sponsorship options and annual rate reviews.

disagreements.issue: Policy Committee Priority Order (Code of Conduct vs. Meet & Confer Grievance/Budget Policies)
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed on the sequencing of ten policies in the Policy Committee queue, resulting in a 6-1 split vote over how early to schedule the Student Code of Conduct relative to Budget Transparency and the Grievance Policy.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prioritize Seclusion & Restraint (1st) and Child Abuse Reporting (2nd), followed by Budget Transparency (3rd) and Student Code of Conduct (4th).
side_a_arguments: Budget Transparency is far along from Meet and Confer and timely during active budget season.
Seclusion & Restraint and Child Abuse Reporting require immediate guidance for principals following recent safety incidents.
disagreements.side_b_position: Place Student Code of Conduct ahead of Budget Transparency so restorative discipline matrices can be finalized before summer handbook printing.
side_b_arguments: Code of Conduct revisions will likely take multiple meetings and must be completed before July year-round school handbooks go to print.
disagreements.resolution: Emily Chávez's retiering motion passed 6-1, with Bettina Umstead explicitly noting her lone dissent on the placement of Student Code of Conduct.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 2/9/26
meetings.executive_summary: Conducted in a virtual/hybrid format requiring roll call votes throughout, the DPS Board of Education's February 9, 2026 work session under Chair Natalie Beyer approved the amended agenda, corrected January 15 minutes, Consent Agenda, and a Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month proclamation unanimously. Following presentations on 2026 Summer Programs and a $4.6M/year ($23M five-year) Student Device Model technology proposal, board members sharply questioned device spending and screen-time guardrails and voted unanimously by roll call to table the technology plan to a future work session. CFO Jeremy Teter also delivered an FY 2026-27 budget update highlighting a $7.2M state funding loss, $6.6M in additional charter transfers from ~1,000 students, DPS dropping from #3 to #10 in teacher supplements ($8,904), and a $29.5M cost estimate for DAE's $22/hr plus step proposal.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Student Representative Recognition, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Work Session Chair Natalie Beyer opened the meeting, introduced student representative Lasagna Arietta, and led a Black History Month moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Approval, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because members participated virtually, all votes were conducted by roll call. The Board voted unanimously to add an informational Policy Committee update before Item 4, approved the amended agenda, and approved the January 15, 2026 minutes with a 2025-to-2026 header date typo correction.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters Katie McDonald and Rob Fields raised urgent concerns regarding mold and stapled wallpaper at Little River Elementary, 50-degree classrooms, tribute to Rodney Rogers, Open Meetings Law compliance, and public records requests related to Eno Valley restraint reporting.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda and Policy Committee Informational Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved the Consent Agenda unanimously by roll call vote and received the added informational update from the Policy Committee.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month (February 1-28, 2026)

agenda_items.title: Summer Programs 2026 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ashley Stevens presented plans for 2026 summer programming across elementary, middle, and high school offerings. Board members reached consensus directives requesting budget and per-pupil figures in April, preliminary enrollment demographics and staffing in June, and completion/outcome metrics in September.

agenda_items.title: Technology Update: Student Device Model Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT Director Paul Majumbi and Assistant Superintendent Chanel Sidbury presented a five-year, $4.6M/year ($23M) Student Device Model keeping K-2 on limited classroom 1:1, 3-8 on school-day plus optional take-home, and 9-12 on full take-home Chromebooks. votes.notes: Cited Policy 2235 restrictions on final action at work sessions and unresolved fiscal/screen-time questions on the $4.6M/year proposal.
votes.discussion_detail: IT Director Paul Majumbi and Chanel Sidbury presented a five-year, $4.6M/year ($23M) Student Device Model maintaining 1:1 Chromebooks across grade bands with tiered take-home access. disagreements.issue: $4.6M/Year Student Device Model, Screen-Time Guardrails, and Work Session Action Authority

disagreements.side_a_position: Delay approval pending instructional evidence, screen-time limits, cost reductions, and compliance with Policy 2235.
side_a_arguments: Sustaining 1:1 devices at $4.6M/year consumes scarce capital and local funds without clear proof of academic return on investment.

side_b_arguments: Modern curriculum, state testing, and classroom instruction depend on reliable devices without aging hardware failures.
disagreements.resolution: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved (seconded by Emily Chávez) to table the Student Device Model and refer it to a future work session and subsequent regular board meeting; passed unanimously on roll call.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 1/29/26
meetings.executive_summary: At its January 29, 2026 monthly meeting, the DPS Board of Education opened with a moment of silence honoring Minneapolis residents killed by immigration enforcement and issued a joint Board-Superintendent statement responding to recent indictments of three DPS employees while pledging full cooperation with prosecutors. The Board unanimously approved the amended agenda (adding a National Mentoring Month proclamation honoring Deworn Langley and Atreus Goode), November 20 minutes, Consent Agenda Items A-C, and the Mentoring Month proclamation. On a 4-3 split vote after contentious debate, the Board directed staff to return by February 26 with sliding-scale after-school tuition models comparable in revenue to Option 1 (50%), acknowledging that doing so would push summer camp registration from February 16 into March, before hearing a Climate Action and Sustainability update.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened with a moment of silence mourning Minneapolis deaths involving immigration enforcement and community fear, followed by school/staff celebrations (including Magnet Schools of America merit awards and winter graduates) and Superintendent Lewis's update. Both Dr. Lewis and Chair Umstead read formal statements addressing the indictment of three DPS administrators, affirming full cooperation with the District Attorney's office and reinforced safety training.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Approval, and November 20, 2025 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers requested adding a National Mentoring Month proclamation as Item 4 before budget priorities, and the Board approved the amended agenda and November 20, 2025 monthly meeting minutes unanimously.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers addressed EC restraint and family isolation at Hillandale and Eno Valley (Stephanie Walton), H-1B visa sponsorship termination (Kayla Curran), the proposed 'private zones' immigration policy 5120 (Fern Hickey, Ellen Holmes, Jen Painter), termination of the SiteLogic energy contract and climate action urgency (Matias Matthew, Miriam Masamba), affordable housing on the Durham School of the Arts parcel (Jim Svara, Mimi Kessler), and classified salary schedule stagnation (Christy Klem).

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-C) and Policy Committee Informational Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved Consent Agenda Items A-C covering an Easley Elementary utility easement, a DHA Pearson LP construction easement at Hillside High, and a 2026 CTE computer purchase, and noted an informational Policy Committee update.

agenda_items.title: Proclamation: National Mentoring Month (January 2026)

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Budget Priorities Tour Feedback

Several board members objected to rushing a large flat hike on low-income families without community feedback or exploring whether higher-income households could pay more on a sliding scale, though staff warned DPS lacks household income data for non-waiver families and might need income-tier quotas. The modified directive passed on a 4-3 split voice vote, with Chair Bettina Umstead warning staff to communicate early so the Board is not cornered again at the February 26 meeting.

disagreements.side_a_position: Require sliding-scale tuition models by February 26 before raising rates so higher-income families can offset lower-income increases.
side_a_arguments: A flat 35%-50% jump burdens low-income Black and Hispanic families disproportionately during economic instability.

disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid delaying summer camp and after-school registration timelines or imposing sliding-scale modeling without reliable family income data.

disagreements.resolution: Emily Chávez's modified motion directing sliding-scale models by February 26 passed 4-3 on a voice vote (returning on Feb 26, where the Board ultimately adopted the 50% flat rate 5-2).

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/11/25
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Board Member Joy Harrell-Goff with all seven board members participating, the December 11, 2025 Durham Public Schools Board of Education work session featured unanimous action extending Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's contract by one year, adopting revised Law Enforcement Relationship Policy 5120 after waiving a second reading, advancing Naloxone Policy 5023 on first reading, and terminating several vendor contracts—including SiteLogic after heated board debate over budget cuts and sustainability tracking. The board also reviewed Strategic Plan Priority 1 academic progress, received a finance update addressing a $4.7 million local charter school funding shortfall, discussed FY 2026-27 budget priorities led by classified and certified employee compensation, and reviewed the Legislative Steering Committee selection process.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, Agenda Modifications, and Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Work Session Chair Joy Harrell-Goff opened the meeting, introduced interpreters and student representative, and led a moment of silence. The board modified the agenda to remove Consent Item A (2026-27 and 2027-28 calendars) to the January work session for community feedback and added Item 3A (Personnel: superintendent contract extension) before approving the amended agenda and the November 6, 2025 work session minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved 7-0 (agenda amendment, amended agenda, and minutes)

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers included Sunrise Movement and Sustainable Schools Coalition representatives advocating for a district climate action plan and criticizing the SiteLogic energy contract's ROI and un-updated energy dashboard. Additional speakers raised concerns about overcrowding at Lyons Farm Elementary, district neutrality on ICE talking points, and mold remediation at Little River.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items B through F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Consent Item A (instructional calendars) removed to January during agenda review, the board took up Consent Agenda items B through F. No items were pulled for separate discussion prior to adoption.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent Contract Extension and Compensation Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's 2024-25 evaluation, Board Chair Bettina Umstead praised Dr. Lewis's steady, transparent leadership during his first year in Durham Public Schools. The board voted to extend his contract by one year and provide a one-time $2,500 annuity contribution plus 40 hours of compensatory time.

agenda_items.title: Policy 5120: Relationship with Law Enforcement (Warrant, FERPA, and ICE Protections)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Policy Committee Chair Jessica Carda-Auten and committee members presented revisions to Policy 5120 restoring 2017 Policy 4321 student due process protections, judicial warrant verification, FERPA subpoena requirements, and immediate escalation of ICE inquiries to the superintendent and board. After amending 'should, whenever feasible' to 'shall, except in cases of emergency,' broadening MOU posting requirements, and referring SRO policy separation to the January 22 Policy Committee, the board waived a second reading and adopted the policy.

agenda_items.title: Policy 5023: Emergency Use of Naloxone (First Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated first-reading language for Policy 5023 governing opioid overdose reversal medication across DPS facilities. Members amended the draft to apply to all DPS buildings rather than only schools, require at least two Naloxone devices and at least three trained DPS staff members excluding SROs and school nurses, remove restrictive 'only' wording on administration liability, and advance the draft to the January work session consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 1 Academic Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Academic Services presented progress indicators under Strategic Plan Priority 1, covering literacy, mathematics, English learner growth, and instructional support initiatives across DPS campuses. Board members asked follow-up questions about equitable intervention alignment and monitoring.

agenda_items.title: Finance Update and Contract Terminations (B&B Triangle Enterprises, BJNL Painting, SiteLogic)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter delivered a finance update detailing budget pressures, including a $4.7 million charter school pass-through shortfall, and brought forward vendor contracts for termination. A sharp policy disagreement emerged over whether to keep SiteLogic's energy management contract until a January ROI review or cut it immediately given budget constraints and an un-updated dashboard since April 2023; Natalie Beyer ultimately amended her motion to terminate all three contracts including SiteLogic while directing a January sustainability report.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved termination of all three contracts as amended 7-0

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's FY 2026-27 Budget Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Lewis and Mr. Teter outlined early FY 2026-27 budget priorities centering on classified salary schedule reform, certified educator compensation, operational stabilization, and forthcoming engagement with Durham County and the DAE Meet and Confer process.

agenda_items.title: Legislative Steering Committee Selection Process, Follow-up Summary, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the member selection process for the ad hoc Legislative Steering Committee and heard the staff follow-up summary, including scheduling a separate February budget public hearing by January. The board then voted to enter closed session without returning to livestream.

votes.discussion_detail: Following passage of the agenda modification, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved to adopt the December 11 work session agenda as amended, and Natalie Beyer seconded. No additional changes or objections were raised by board members. The presiding chair, Joy Harrell-Goff, called for the voice vote, and the amended agenda passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approve November 6, 2025 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Emily Chávez moved to approve the minutes from the November 6, 2025 monthly work session, with Natalie Beyer seconding the motion. No board member offered corrections or edits to the draft minutes. Presiding Chair Joy Harrell-Goff called the voice vote, and all seven members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Extend Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's Contract by One Year with $2,500 Annuity Contribution and 40 Hours Compensatory Time
votes.notes: Following 2024-25 superintendent evaluation.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the board's completion of Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's 2024-25 performance evaluation, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved to extend his employment contract by one year and award a one-time $2,500 annuity contribution plus 40 hours of compensatory time. Board Chair Bettina Umstead seconded the motion and commended Dr. Lewis for steady, collaborative, and transparent leadership during a challenging transition year. All seven board members supported the extension, passing the motion 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Waive Second Reading of Policy 5120 (Relationship with Law Enforcement)
votes.notes: Procedural waiver to allow immediate final adoption at the work session due to urgency around student and immigrant family protections.
votes.discussion_detail: Because community members, teachers, and board members emphasized the urgent need to put explicit law enforcement and immigration enforcement safeguards into board policy ahead of winter break, Natalie Beyer moved to waive the board's customary second-reading requirement for Policy 5120. Emily Chávez seconded the procedural waiver. Board members agreed that the committee and public had already thoroughly vetted the revisions, and the waiver passed 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Revised Policy 5120 (Relationship with Law Enforcement) as Amended
votes.notes: Restores 2017 Policy 4321 warrant verification, logging, FERPA/court-order limits, and ICE request escalation to Superintendent and Board.
votes.discussion_detail: Policy Committee Chair Jessica Carda-Auten and committee members Natalie Beyer and Emily Chávez presented major revisions to Policy 5120 restoring 2017 Policy 4321 protections, requiring judicial warrant checks, FERPA compliance, and immediate escalation of immigration enforcement requests to the superintendent and board. During floor debate, board members strengthened discretionary 'should, whenever feasible' notification language to mandatory 'shall, except in cases of emergency' and expanded public posting rules to cover any law enforcement MOU. Members debated whether SRO provisions should be split into a separate policy and agreed to refer that follow-up work to the January 22 Policy Committee so the core student protections could take effect immediately. Natalie Beyer moved final adoption as amended, Jessica Carda-Auten seconded, and the motion carried 7-0.

votes.item_title: Terminate Contracts with B&B Triangle Enterprises, BJNL Painting, and SiteLogic and Direct January Sustainability Report

disagreements.issue: Immediate Termination vs. Delayed ROI Review of SiteLogic Energy Management Contract
disagreements.summary: Board members split over whether to terminate SiteLogic's energy management contract immediately alongside two underperforming vendor contracts or pause until January to evaluate sustainability ROI and historical data.
disagreements.side_a_position: Defer terminating SiteLogic until staff brings an ROI and sustainability analysis in January.
side_a_arguments: Wanted administration to present cost-benefit data and clarity on prior energy savings and district sustainability commitments before cutting the vendor.
disagreements.side_b_position: Terminate the SiteLogic contract immediately while bringing a broader sustainability and climate action plan review in January.
side_b_arguments: The district faces a $4.7 million charter school shortfall and urgent budget constraints requiring immediate expenditure cuts.
Student advocates and board members noted SiteLogic's public energy dashboard had not been updated since April 2023, undermining confidence in active contract value.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved when Natalie Beyer amended her motion to terminate SiteLogic immediately alongside B&B Triangle Enterprises and BJNL Painting while directing a January sustainability report, passing 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/11/25
disagreements.issue: Scope of Mandatory Notification and SRO Separation in Law Enforcement Policy 5120
disagreements.summary: Board members debated how strictly to word parental/district notification mandates during law enforcement actions and whether School Resource Officer (SRO) provisions should remain in Policy 5120 or be separated.
disagreements.side_a_position: Preserve flexible 'should, whenever feasible' phrasing or examine all statutory edge cases before tightening language.
side_a_arguments: Legal and committee drafters sought careful alignment with state law and practical feasibility during active school emergencies.
disagreements.side_b_position: Mandate stronger enforceable 'shall, except in cases of emergency' protections, broaden public MOU posting, and pursue a standalone SRO policy.
side_b_arguments: Heightened federal immigration enforcement requires unambiguous, binding protections for students and families rather than discretionary language.
Separating SRO-specific governance from general law enforcement / ICE protocols prevents confusion and strengthens accountability.
disagreements.resolution: Consensus reached by amending Policy 5120 to 'shall, except in cases of emergency,' broadening MOU posting rules, adopting Policy 5120 immediately 7-0, and referring a standalone SRO policy to the January 22 Policy Committee.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 12/11/25
disagreements.issue: Naloxone Policy 5023 Facility Coverage, Full-Time Staff Requirement, and Good Samaritan Liability
disagreements.summary: Members debated operational details of Policy 5023 regarding which facilities must stock Naloxone, whether trained staff minimums must specify full-time employees, and phrasing that could restrict emergency responders.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require full-time staff certification at sites to guarantee daytime coverage and retain explicit trained-personnel framing.
side_a_arguments: Full-time staff requirement ensures trained staff are reliably on site rather than part-time or itinerant personnel.
disagreements.side_b_position: Cover all DPS buildings (not just schools), keep staffing requirements flexible for principals excluding nurses/SROs, and remove 'only' trained language.
side_b_arguments: Principals need flexibility in selecting three trained staff per building without rigid full-time mandates.
Removing 'only' prevents chilling anyone from administering life-saving Naloxone in an emergency.
disagreements.resolution: Board reached 7-0 first-reading consensus expanding to all DPS buildings, requiring >=2 devices and >=3 trained staff (excluding nurses/SROs) without a rigid full-time clause, and removing 'only.'

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting |
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham County Board of County Commissioners convened for their joint quarterly meeting (held Wednesday, November 19 and published November 20, 2025), co-chaired by BOE Chair Bettina Umstead and BOCC Chair Nida Allam. Both boards addressed recent immigration enforcement fears and school visitor protocols, reviewed DPS's $965 million Facility Condition Assessment and early 2026 school bond planning alongside County Manager Claudia Hager's sobering FY 2025-26 revenue update ($11 million sales tax shortfall and $2B+ 10-year county CIP), and examined DPS's state accountability gains (88.9% meeting/exceeding growth, ranking #1 among NC's 12 largest districts). The joint bodies approved the agenda, the August 12 joint meeting minutes, and an amended 2026 joint calendar adding a Q1 budget meeting before May 12, followed by public comment advocating affordable housing on a 3-acre parcel at the current Durham School of the Arts site.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks on Immigration Enforcement, Agenda Approval, and August 12 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOE Chair Bettina Umstead and BOCC Chair Nida Allam opened the joint quarterly meeting with remarks addressing heightened Customs and Border Protection / ICE activity in Durham and emphasizing visitor protocols keeping students safe. The joint boards unanimously approved the meeting agenda and the August 12, 2025 joint meeting minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda approved unanimously; August 12 minutes approved unanimously

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Process and 2026 Bond Outlook
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS leadership and planning staff presented findings from the district's $965 million Facility Condition Assessment—translating to roughly $2 billion in total long-term facility needs—alongside work by the CIP Task Force on 13 elementary schools enrolling under 450 students and 5 potential consolidation trade-up candidates. Commissioners and school board members questioned facility capacity, underutilized school footprints, and timing ahead of a targeted 2026 bond referendum.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Operating Budget and 10-Year CIP Fiscal Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Manager Claudia Hager outlined tight county fiscal conditions, reporting an $11 million FY 2024-25 sales tax shortfall, a $5.9 million per month SNAP gap, county hiring freezes, and more than $2 billion in competing 10-year county capital needs. Hager stressed early coordination between DPS and county finance staff before finalizing the 2026 bond sizing and operating expansion requests.

agenda_items.title: DPS 2024-25 Academic Accountability Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Al Royster and Dr. King presented 2024-25 academic results showing 56.6% of DPS schools earned A, B, or C grades, low-performing schools dropped from 20 to 17, overall GLP reached 48.4%, and 88.9% of schools met or exceeded growth—#1 among NC's 12 largest districts and well ahead of Durham charter schools (71.4%). BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee criticized the state's 80% achievement / 20% growth school performance grade formula for penalizing high-growth schools.

agenda_items.title: 2026 Joint Quarterly Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Joint board members reviewed proposed 2026 quarterly meeting dates and agreed to add an extra Q1 joint BOCC-BOE budget meeting prior to May 12 to align county and school board budget cycles alongside joint City/County/DPS sessions.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Durham School of the Arts North Parcel Reuse
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Jim Svara urged the Board of Education and County Commissioners to explore developing affordable housing on a 3-acre north lot on the existing Durham School of the Arts campus adjacent to the Rail Trail once DSA relocates.

votes.item_title: Approve Joint Quarterly Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Joint BOCC-BOE voice vote; BOCC Chair Nida Allam seconded BOE Vice Chair Millicent Rogers's motion.
votes.discussion_detail: Following joint opening remarks from BOE Chair Bettina Umstead and BOCC Chair Nida Allam regarding community immigration concerns and school safety protocols, BOE Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved to approve the joint quarterly meeting agenda as presented. BOCC Chair Nida Allam seconded the motion. No joint board members requested modifications, and the motion carried unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve August 12, 2025 Joint Quarterly Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint BOCC-BOE voice vote; BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee moved and BOE member Natalie Beyer seconded.
votes.discussion_detail: BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee moved to adopt the minutes of the August 12, 2025 joint quarterly meeting between the Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners, and BOE member Natalie Beyer seconded. No edits or corrections were raised by members of either board. The joint bodies approved the minutes unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve 2026 Joint Meeting Calendar as Amended to Add Q1 Budget Meeting Before May 12
votes.notes: Joint BOCC-BOE voice vote ensuring early joint budget coordination before May 12.
votes.discussion_detail: When reviewing the proposed 2026 joint quarterly meeting schedule, BOCC and BOE members agreed on the need to meet jointly earlier in the spring budget cycle rather than waiting until May 12. BOCC Vice Chair Dr. Mike Lee moved—with BOCC Chair Nida Allam seconding—to approve the 2026 joint calendar as amended to add a Q1 BOCC-BOE budget meeting before May 12 alongside planned City/County/DPS joint sessions. Both boards approved the amended schedule unanimously by voice vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting |
disagreements.issue: Sizing the 2026 School Bond and Potential Small-School Consolidation Amid County Capital Constraints
disagreements.summary: While DPS presented ~$965M in immediate FCA needs (~$2B long-term) and highlighted 13 under-enrolled elementary schools (<450 students), county leadership emphasized severe county revenue constraints ($11M sales tax shortfall, county hiring freezes, and >$2B competing 10-year CIP requests) requiring tough trade-offs on bond sizing and school footprint consolidation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Address comprehensive district facility equity, deferred maintenance (~$965M FCA), and modernizations across all campuses through a major 2026 bond while carefully studying 5 consolidation trade-up candidates through the CIP Task Force.
side_a_arguments: Every DPS campus deserves modernized learning environments after years of deferred maintenance.
Community trust requires transparent objective CIP Task Force evaluation before closing or consolidating small neighborhood elementary schools.
disagreements.side_b_position: Align DPS capital requests strictly with Durham County debt capacity, sales tax revenue pressures, and realistic project phasing, while pursuing consolidation efficiencies where elementary schools remain under 450 students.
side_b_arguments: Durham County faces an $11M sales tax shortfall, federal safety-net pressures, and over $2B in countywide capital demands requiring strict debt limits.
Operating 13 elementary schools below 450 students creates ongoing capital and operating inefficiencies unless consolidation or co-location options are weighed.
disagreements.resolution: No formal bond vote was taken; both boards agreed to add an extra Q1 2026 joint budget session before May 12 to coordinate capital and operating requests early.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/20/25
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead with six members present (Jessica Carda-Auten absent; Emily Chávez joining virtually), the November 20, 2025 monthly board meeting centered on student protections amid local ICE enforcement fears—where attendance had dipped to 70%—and final adoption of Student Wireless Communication Device Policy 4318. The board unanimously passed (6-0) an amended Resolution Affirming Commitment to Student Safety and Privacy Regardless of Immigration Status after debating whether notices 'shall' or 'may' be posted in schools, and adopted Policy 4318 (6-0) after modifying the middle school ban to allow phone use at lunch alongside smart-glasses prohibitions. Members also received CFO Jeremy Teter's finance and classified salary study updates (showing a $4.7M charter shortfall, 33 collapsed classrooms, and three salary scenarios ranging from $23.5M to $119.7M) and deferred the 2026-27 and 2027-28 instructional calendars to December 11 for public input.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence on ICE Raids, Celebrations, and Superintendent Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened with a joint statement with Durham's Mayor and BOCC Chair condemning immigration enforcement raids that contributed to districtwide attendance dropping to 70%. The board held monthly student, teacher, employee, and Spark Pin celebrations and heard Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's update on multilingual family engagement and campus operations.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Modifications/Approval and October 21, 2025 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Jessica Carda-Auten absent, the six present board members amended the agenda to add the Immigration Resolution as Item 3, move Policy 3620 to Consent 2E, add Policy 4207 rescission to Consent 2F, and present the Finance Update before the Classified Salary Study. They then approved the October 21, 2025 meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters included Sunrise DSA students advocating green school initiatives, parents and advocates speaking on cell phone safety and Club Boulevard Elementary's petition on school discipline and policing, and speakers addressing budget transparency and academic proficiency.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved Consent Agenda items A through F, including Policy 3620 and Policy 4207 rescission added during agenda review.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Affirming Commitment to Student Safety and Privacy Regardless of Immigration Status
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emily Chávez introduced and moved an emergency resolution reaffirming FERPA privacy, judicial warrant requirements, and staff protocols amid ICE activity in Durham. Following debate over whether printed notices 'shall' or 'may' be posted in schools, members amended the text to 'may be posted,' underlined 'only,' required review by board legal counsel, and specified judicial officials' signed warrants.

agenda_items.title: Policy 4318: Student Use of Cell Phones and Other Personal Wireless Communication Devices (2nd Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board held second reading on state-mandated Policy 4318. After debating whether middle schoolers should face a full bell-to-bell ban or retain lunch access like high schoolers, members amended the Policy Committee's draft to permit middle school lunch access, ban smart glasses unless IEP/504/IHP-approved, include high school class-change bans, and add Dr. Lewis's emergency access and anti-secret-recording clauses.

agenda_items.title: Finance Update ($4.7M Charter Shortfall) and Classified Salary Study Scenarios
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter presented a sobering finance report noting a $4.7 million local charter school shortfall alongside $51 million in total charter pass-through costs and 33 collapsed classrooms to stabilize FY 2025-26. He then presented three classified salary study scenarios costing $23.5M (county floor), $34.5M (city floor), and $119.7M (MIT living wage floor), noting a 1% across-the-board raise costs $1.1M.

agenda_items.title: 2026-27 and 2027-28 Traditional and Year-Round Instructional Calendars
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because draft 2026-27 and 2027-28 traditional and year-round calendars were posted late to BoardDocs, board members deferred action to the December 11, 2025 work session so families and staff could review and submit feedback first.

agenda_items.title: Information-Only Grants/Policy Items and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board briefly acknowledged information-only grant and policy update reports without questions and voted to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve November 20, 2025 Monthly Meeting Agenda as Amended
votes.notes: Jessica Carda-Auten absent; Emily Chávez attended virtually.
votes.discussion_detail: With Board Member Jessica Carda-Auten absent and Emily Chávez attending virtually, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved to approve the November 20 agenda with several modifications, seconded by Natalie Beyer. The amendments added the emergency Immigration Safety and Privacy Resolution as Item 3, moved Policy 3620 to Consent Item 2E, added Policy 4207 rescission to Consent Item 2F, and reordered the Finance Update before the Classified Salary Study presentation. All six participating board members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Approve October 21, 2025 Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Jessica Carda-Auten explicitly noted absent at 00:51:02.
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer moved to approve the October 21, 2025 meeting minutes, and Vice Chair Millicent Rogers seconded. No edits were proposed, and Chair Bettina Umstead noted Jessica Carda-Auten's absence for the record. The six present board members approved the minutes 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adopt Resolution Affirming Commitment to Student Safety and Privacy Regardless of Immigration Status as Amended
votes.notes: Jessica Carda-Auten absent. Compromised on 'may be posted' after debate over whether physical postings could invite targeting or overburden staff.
votes.discussion_detail: Amid acute community anxiety following local ICE/CBP enforcement activity that pushed DPS attendance down to 70%, Emily Chávez moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded a resolution affirming student safety and privacy protections regardless of immigration status. Board members tightened legal precision by underlining 'only' under FERPA rules, specifying judicial warrants signed by a judicial official, and requiring legal counsel review. A substantive disagreement arose over whether schools 'shall' or 'may' physically post the resolution, with Chávez and Harrell-Goff urging mandatory posting for family reassurance while Beyer, Rogers, Tabb, and Chair Umstead warned against overburdening staff or making campuses visible targets. Chávez accepted 'may be posted' to preserve unanimity, and the amended resolution passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Adopt Policy 4318 (Student Use of Cell Phones and Other Personal Wireless Communication Devices) on Second Reading as Amended
votes.notes: Jessica Carda-Auten absent. Required by state legislation for January 1, 2026 implementation.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved and Natalie Beyer seconded second-reading adoption of state-mandated Policy 4318 governing student wireless devices. The board extensively refined the Policy Committee's draft, prohibiting smart glasses except for IEP/504/IHP medical accommodations, equating smartwatches with phones, prohibiting high school phone use during class transitions, adding Dr. Lewis's emergency communication exception, and substituting clearer anti-secret-recording language. On the central policy divide—whether middle schoolers should face a bell-to-bell ban—Rogers, Beyer, Umstead, and Tabb favored permitting middle school lunch access for consistency with high schools and smoother mid-year rollout, overcoming Emily Chávez's preference for a full bell-to-bell ban. With all edits incorporated, the board adopted Policy 4318 by a 6-0 voice vote.

votes.item_title: Defer 2026-27 and 2027-28 Traditional and Year-Round Instructional Calendars to December 11 Work Session
votes.notes: Deferred for community feedback because draft calendars were posted late; Jessica Carda-Auten absent.
votes.discussion_detail: When Item 5 (2026-27 and 2027-28 Traditional and Year-Round Instructional Calendars) came up for consideration, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers noted that the proposed calendars had been posted late, limiting community review ahead of the meeting. Rogers moved to defer action on the calendars until the December 11 work session to give families and staff adequate time to review and weigh in, and Natalie Beyer seconded. Board members agreed without dissent, voting 6-0 to table the item to December.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Jessica Carda-Auten absent.
votes.discussion_detail: After reviewing brief informational reports, Natalie Beyer moved to enter closed session for the purposes listed on the agenda, and Wendell Tabb seconded. The remaining six present board members voted Aye 6-0 via voice vote.
