disagreements.issue: Mandatory ('Shall') vs. Permissive ('May') Physical Posting of Immigration Resolution in Schools
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed over whether the Immigration Safety and Privacy Resolution should mandate ('shall be posted') or permit ('may be posted') physical display in all school buildings.
disagreements.side_a_position: Mandate physical posting ('shall be posted') at schools so families and staff see visible institutional solidarity.
side_a_arguments: Visible signage reassures immigrant families and ensures school staff and visitors know district protections clearly.
disagreements.side_b_position: Use permissive language ('may be posted') rather than a rigid posting mandate.
side_b_arguments: Mandatory physical posters could invite vandalism, draw hostile attention, or create compliance burdens for principals when digital communication is safer and more effective.
disagreements.resolution: Emily Chávez agreed to amend the language to 'may be posted,' and the resolution passed unanimously 6-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/20/25
disagreements.issue: Middle School Cell Phone Rules: Bell-to-Bell Ban vs. Lunchtime Access in Policy 4318
disagreements.summary: Following the Policy Committee's draft favoring a strict bell-to-bell ban for elementary and middle schools, a majority of the full board amended Policy 4318 to allow middle school students phone access during lunch.
disagreements.side_a_position: Maintain a full bell-to-bell wireless device prohibition for middle school students (consistent with Policy Committee recommendation).
side_a_arguments: Research and educator feedback indicate lunchtime phone use fuels cyberbullying, social conflict, and distraction back into afternoon classes.
disagreements.side_b_position: Allow middle school students to access phones during lunch alongside high schoolers.
side_b_arguments: Aligning middle and high school rules avoids an abrupt mid-year enforcement shock on January 1 and allows families a smoother transition.
Consistent secondary-level rules give principals clearer operational expectations during non-instructional lunch periods.
disagreements.resolution: Policy 4318 was amended to permit middle school phone access during lunch while prohibiting class-change use and smart glasses, passing 6-0.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/6/25
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Board Member Joy Harrell-Goff, the November 6, 2025 work session approved the first reading of state-mandated Student Wireless Communication Device Policy 4318, established an ad hoc 15-to-16-member Legislative Steering Committee, and approved a $675,000 Chromebook repair contract with CDW Government LLC after pulling it from consent for closer scrutiny. Members debated smartwatches, smart glasses, language-justice outreach, and bell-to-bell vs. lunch access for middle schoolers in Policy 4318, as well as whether to bind DPS to a full-year Chromebook repair contract ahead of its upcoming 1:1 refresh plan. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Chair Joy Harrell-Goff called the work session to order with six members initially present (Wendell Tabb joining shortly after 00:12:04). The board amended the agenda to pull Consent Item 2B (Chromebook repair contract) to Item 4C for discussion and remove Consent Item 2G (Policy 3620) to the November monthly meeting, then approved the amended agenda and October 7, 13, and 20 meeting minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Approved 6-0 (agenda amendment, amended agenda, and minutes)

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members of the public addressed student safety, digital device policies, special education staffing, and community input ahead of upcoming policy and operational decisions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through E after Item Pulls)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following removal of the Chromebook repair contract (to 4C) and Policy 3620 (to the November monthly meeting), the board approved remaining consent items covering the 2025-26 budget resolution, a GoDurham Freeman Road bus stop easement at Southern High School, a DSA Enbridge Gas easement, October grants/gifts/donations, and second-reading adoption of Policy 3210.

agenda_items.title: Policy 4318: Student Wireless Communication Devices (First Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Policy Committee presented first-reading draft Policy 4318 ahead of the state's January 1 mandate. Board members debated middle school bell-to-bell bans versus lunch access, coverage of smartwatches and smart glasses (including IEP/504 exemptions), and multilingual family outreach, before approving first reading and referring the draft back to Monday's Policy Committee.

agenda_items.title: Low-Performing School Improvement Plans and Enrollment Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Academic Services reviewed improvement plans for the district's 17 low-performing schools—prompting board requests for Spanish-language accessibility—alongside current enrollment trends and questions about how after-school program availability and marketing affect student retention.

agenda_items.title: Chromebook Repair Service Contract (CDW Government LLC, NTE $675,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board deferred Item 4C temporarily to new Item 5B while staff uploaded a clean corrected contract document. disagreements.issue: Policy 4318 Middle School Phone Access, Smart Devices, and Language Access
disagreements.summary: Board members split during first reading over whether middle school students should face an all-day bell-to-bell cell phone ban or be allowed device access at lunch, as well as how to regulate smartwatches and smart glasses.
disagreements.side_a_position: Apply a full bell-to-bell ban for middle schoolers and explicitly restrict smartwatches/smart glasses to prevent classroom and hallway disruption.
side_a_arguments: Educators and parents expressed concern that lunch-period access drives hallway conflicts, social media drama, and enforcement confusion.
disagreements.side_b_position: Permit middle school lunchtime access for continuity with high schools while carefully verifying medical/IEP accommodations for smart glasses and multilingual outreach.
side_b_arguments: Allowing lunch access provides consistency across secondary grades during the mid-year transition.
Policies must not penalize students needing smart glasses for IEP/504 accessibility or families needing Spanish communication.
disagreements.resolution: Approved first reading 7-0 and referred all board questions to the November 10 Policy Committee for revision before second reading.

disagreements.issue: Duration and Scope of $675,000 CDW Chromebook Repair Contract Ahead of 1:1 Refresh Plan

disagreements.side_b_position: Approve the CDW repair contract up to $675,000 now as a not-to-exceed ceiling so broken devices are promptly restored for instruction and testing.

meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Board Member Jessica Carda-Auten (with Millicent Rogers virtual from the start and Emily Chávez joining virtually midway), the October 7, 2025 work session approved October proclamations for Disability History and Awareness Month and National Bullying Prevention Month (6-0) and authorized a $1,262,140 purchase of 2,000 Chromebooks with protective cases from CDW-G (7-0) to restore 1:1 student device capacity. CFO Jeremy Teter also presented three draft classified salary schedule options and flagged an annualization calculation flaw (48 vs. 52 weeks) on existing pay tables, while Safety & Security presented emergency protocols, SRO restorative training, and HEART team coordination.

disagreements.issue: Day-User Chromebook Restrictions for Grades 6-12 and Technology Fee Equity

Sixth-grade families and low-income students are unfairly penalized for district inventory gaps and uneven school-level fee enforcement.
disagreements.resolution: Board approved the 2,000-device purchase 7-0 while logging follow-up directives requiring staff to detail how any day-user policy protects equity, digital textbooks, and home access before bringing a comprehensive 1:1 plan back by March.

meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Vice Chair Millicent Rogers with Chair Bettina Umstead absent throughout (and Wendell Tabb joining virtually prior to the consent agenda), the September 11, 2025 work session featured a 5-1 split vote approving the transition of district and 51 school checking accounts from Truist to JP Morgan Chase while retaining up to six school accounts at Durham-based Mechanics and Farmers Bank. The board also heard extensive public comments urging immediate passage of Law Enforcement Policy 5120 and private-zone protections amid ICE fears, Sunrise DSA climate proposals, and Little River mold complaints. Academic Services presented 2024-25 ESSA accountability gains—highlighted by 88.9% of schools meeting or exceeding growth (#1 among NC's 12 largest districts vs. 71.4% of Durham charters)—while board members requested a per-pupil spending analysis and intervention plans for the district's two F-graded schools.

agenda_items.title: Opening, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and August 14 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Work Session Chair Millicent Rogers welcomed City of Medicine Academy student representative Briana Barona and led a September 11 and anti-gun-violence moment of silence. With Chair Bettina Umstead and Wendell Tabb not yet online, the five present members unanimously approved the agenda and the August 14, 2025 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Educators, parents, and students—including Holly Harden, Fawn Hickey, River Wadsworth, a Hillside freshman, and a translated parent letter—called for strengthening Policy 5120 and adopting ACLU/NC Justice Center private-zone protocols amid declining multilingual enrollment and fear of ICE. Additional speakers included Little River teacher Katie McDonald on mold air-quality testing, Sunrise DSA students on climate resolutions, a CC Spalding parent on family responsibility zones, and physical therapist Christy Clem on 38% PT staffing vacancies.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda

agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter recommended migrating central funds and 51 school checking accounts from Truist to JP Morgan Chase—projecting $600,000+ in annual interest income, waived fees, and remote check scanners—while honoring six schools currently banking with Mechanics and Farmers Bank. Wendell Tabb questioned whether limiting M&F to 'up to six' accounts barred other principals from choosing M&F later, leading to a 5-1 roll call vote.

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Finance Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Teter updated the board on incremental DPI state funding releases ($240.8M received toward $245.6M prior-year levels), restart school and international-teacher conversions, and the $3 million local cost estimate needed to provide classified employees at least a 2% raise absent state budget action.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: 2024-25 ESSA Accountability Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Al Royster and Ashley Stevens reported that 56.6% of DPS schools earned A-C grades, low-performing schools dropped from 20 to 17, overall GLP reached 48.2%, and 88.9% of schools met or exceeded EVOS growth—ranking #1 among North Carolina's 12 largest districts and 9th statewide. Board members probed a 5.6-point Hispanic graduation drop, science test renorming, AP exam funding, per-pupil spending disparities, and wraparound support for two F-graded schools.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session

disagreements.side_a_position: Keep the motion strictly framed as 'up to six' Mechanics and Farmers school accounts while migrating the remaining 51 schools and central funds to JP Morgan Chase.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/14/25
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Board Member Natalie Beyer with Vice Chair Millicent Rogers absent throughout (six members participating max, with Emily Chávez virtual), the August 14, 2025 work session tackled major governance, financial, and capital actions. Following external auditor Paul Carson's presentation of the overdue FY 2023-24 audit—revealing an unmodified financial opinion alongside seven audit findings, an $8.8M local fund balance drop, a $5M School Food Service loss, and a $4.4M accounts payable spike—CFO Jeremy Teter detailed systemic fixes, secured approval of an accelerated FY 2026-27 budget calendar (6-0 after adding 'initial funding request' language), launched the internal Classified Salary Study timeline (5-0), and won approval for House Bill 125 mini-budget local supplements including $500/year for certified staff and nurses and $200/month for bus drivers (6-0). The board also approved a new $6,491,837 capital staffing contract with 35 North (6-0), appointed Wendell Tabb, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Natalie Beyer to the 10-year Capital Improvement Plan Task Force (5-0), and formally accepted the 2023-24 audited financial statements (5-0).

agenda_items.title: Opening, Agenda Modifications/Approval, and June 10 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Work Session Chair Natalie Beyer opened the meeting (with Millicent Rogers absent throughout) and led a moment of silence. The board amended the agenda to move the Glenn Elementary renovation update to new Item 3A (5-0 before Emily Chávez joined online) and, once Chávez connected, approved the amended agenda (6-0) and June 10 minutes (6-0).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda amendment 5-0; Amended agenda and minutes 6-0

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Physical therapist Christy Clem warned of a 33% occupational therapist vacancy crisis and 30-year salary compression compared to psychologists and speech therapists, urging relief in the upcoming classified salary study. Parent Victoria Peterson questioned special education funding and called for higher pay for staff supporting high-needs EC students.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A through H, Including Policy Committee Appointments)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved Consent Agenda items A through H via roll call, including formal appointment of three board members to the newly established Policy Committee.

agenda_items.title: Glenn Elementary Renovation Update and Back-to-School Readiness Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: 35 North president Scott McIntyre and COO Ken Barnes reported that teachers could return to Glenn Elementary Monday ahead of final certificate of occupancy, with contingency classrooms covered until Wing A finishes 2-3 weeks later and no change orders exceeding $90,000. Dr. Lewis then previewed the 'Reset, Refocus, Reignite' theme, the Durham Early College of Health Sciences opening, Infinite Campus rollout, bus lounges/route improvements, and 273 vacancies.

agenda_items.title: 2023-24 External Audit Presentation and Staff Corrective Response
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Auditor Paul Carson (Anderson Smith & White) delivered an unmodified opinion on the delayed June 30, 2024 financial statements alongside seven findings (unreconciled accounts, missing POs, budget overruns, late LGC filing, workers' comp restatement, and federal/state cash findings), a $4.4M accounts payable jump, and a $5M food service loss. CFO Jeremy Teter presented corrective controls including current bank reconciliations, hard PO enforcement, SOP manuals, and hiring an internal auditor, and the board later voted 5-0 to accept the 2023-24 audited statements.

agenda_items.title: FY 2026-27 Budget Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Teter proposed an accelerated 2026-27 budget timeline targeting a December 11 draft budget, early-January Meet and Confer consultation, and late-February board adoption ahead of the county's March 1 deadline. After Natalie Beyer voiced concern about locking in figures prior to state budget clarity, the board amended the calendar wording to authorize an 'initial funding request' and approved it 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Classified Salary Study Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Teter outlined an internal classified salary study launching with an August 18–September 2 staff survey, executive summary on September 25, draft schedules on October 9, and October 23 action to feed into FY 2026-27 budget expansion requests. Board members aligned on goals of living wages, decompression, clarity, and eliminating legacy differentials.

agenda_items.title: State Mini-Budget (HB 125) Impact and Local Supplements Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Teter briefed the board on North Carolina's HB 125 mini-budget (no across-the-board raises, step freezes at steps 15-23, rising employee health insurance bands) and won 6-0 authorization to implement local supplements: +$500/year for certified staff and nurses, $200/month for regular-route bus drivers (Sept–June), and single monthly paychecks for dually employed bus drivers, while committing to return September 11 on local classified raise options.

agenda_items.title: New 35 North Capital Staffing Plan Contract ($6,491,837)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration sought approval of a new $6,491,837 contract with 35 North to manage Glenn, DSA, and remaining 2022 bond projects as its interim contract expired in September. Natalie Beyer clarified the précis should reflect a new contract rather than an amendment, and Emily Chávez asked that the exact dollar figure be stated on the record before passing 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Task Force Composition and Board Appointments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: School Planning Director Devin Mitchell presented the 10-year CIP Task Force framework covering $965M in facility needs across 8 buckets ahead of a 2026 bond referendum. Board members requested adding EC and athletics representation, flexible meeting times, and three board seats instead of two, voting 5-0 to appoint Wendell Tabb, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Natalie Beyer.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Summary and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pittman summarized board follow-up items (emailing the spring simulator consensus breakdown, updating the 35 North précis to 'new contract,' and posting approved CIP Task Force minutes on BoardDocs), after which the board voted 6-0 to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve Classified Salary Study Timeline
votes.notes: Seconded simultaneously by Joy Harrell-Goff and Emily Chávez; Millicent Rogers absent and Wendell Tabb temporarily stepped out (5-0 tally).
votes.discussion_detail: Mr. Teter outlined the internal Classified Salary Study schedule beginning with an August 18–September 2 staff survey (with mobile and shared-device access for trades, bus, and cafeteria staff), a September 25 survey summary, October 9 draft schedules, and October 23 integration into FY 2026-27 expansion requests. Board members aligned on core goals including addressing compression, achieving living wages, simplifying opaque pay tables, and phasing out legacy differentials. Chair Bettina Umstead moved approval of the timeline, seconded simultaneously by Joy Harrell-Goff and Emily Chávez, passing 5-0 via roll call while Wendell Tabb was briefly away from the dais.

votes.item_title: Approve Local Salary Supplements Under HB 125 Mini-Budget ($500/Yr Certified & Nurses, $200/Mo Bus Drivers, Monthly Pay for Dual-Role Drivers)
votes.notes: Millicent Rogers absent; Mr. Teter pledged to return September 11 with local options for classified staff absent state budget raises.
votes.discussion_detail: Because North Carolina's HB 125 mini-budget omitted across-the-board raises and froze steps 15-23, Mr. Teter sought immediate local authorization from the board's spring budget consensus while promising a September 11 analysis of local options for classified employees. Emily Chávez moved (seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff) to increase local supplements for state-certified staff and school nurses by $500 per year ($50/month), launch a $200/month supplement for regular-route bus drivers (September through June), and consolidate pay into a single monthly check for dually employed bus drivers to simplify tax withholdings. On roll call at 03:03:22, all six participating board members voted Aye 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve New Contract with 35 North for 2022 Bond and Building Program Staffing Plan ($6,491,837)
votes.notes: Millicent Rogers absent; replaces interim April contract expiring in September.
votes.discussion_detail: With 35 North's interim project-management contract expiring in September, staff requested continuity for Glenn Elementary, Durham School of the Arts, and remaining 2022 bond projects. Joy Harrell-Goff moved and Wendell Tabb seconded approval, initially referencing the précis label 'amendment.' General Counsel Ken Soo/Malone and Natalie Beyer clarified this was a new contract rather than an amendment and directed an updated précis, while Emily Chávez asked that the exact $6,491,837 contract value be read into the motion. With Harrell-Goff and Tabb accepting both clarifications, the motion passed 6-0 at 03:09:50.

votes.item_title: Approve Appointments of Wendell Tabb, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Natalie Beyer to Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Task Force
votes.notes: Millicent Rogers absent and Wendell Tabb stepped out briefly before vote (5-0 tally).
votes.discussion_detail: School Planning Director Devin Mitchell presented the 12-to-16-member CIP Task Force tasked with evaluating all campuses across eight facility buckets and producing school-by-school 10-year priority plans ahead of a 2026 bond. Board members urged adding Exceptional Children and athletics representation, flexible meeting hours, and three board appointees instead of two so at least two members could attend every meeting. Chair Bettina Umstead moved to appoint Wendell Tabb, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Natalie Beyer to the CIP Task Force, Jessica Carda-Auten seconded, and the motion passed 5-0 while Tabb was momentarily out of the room.

votes.item_title: Accept 2023-24 Audited Financial Statements
votes.notes: Formal vote taken near end of meeting after auditor presentation; Millicent Rogers absent and Wendell Tabb briefly out (5-0 tally).
votes.discussion_detail: Realizing the board had not taken a formal acceptance vote immediately following Anderson Smith & White's audit presentation earlier in the evening, Presiding Chair Natalie Beyer called for action on the June 30, 2024 audited financial statements. Chair Bettina Umstead moved to accept the 2023-24 audited financial statements, and Jessica Carda-Auten seconded. On roll call, the five members present (with Rogers absent and Tabb briefly away) voted Aye 5-0.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb returned for final vote; Millicent Rogers absent throughout.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Dr. Pittman's summary of follow-up items, Joy Harrell-Goff moved to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, and Jessica Carda-Auten seconded. With Wendell Tabb returned to the meeting, all six participating board members voted Aye 6-0 on roll call.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 8/14/25
disagreements.issue: Accelerated February Budget Deadline vs. Waiting for State and County Budget Clarity
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether adopting the FY 2026-27 district budget ask by the end of February—more than two months before the May 15 statutory deadline—risked locking DPS into underfunded requests before the General Assembly acts or competing county expansion requests emerge.
disagreements.side_a_position: Hold flexibility beyond February and explicitly label any February submission an 'initial' or 'projected' funding request.
side_a_arguments: State budget delays leave key teacher and classified cost variables unresolved in February.
Locking in a number too early could leave DPS short relative to Sheriff, Durham Tech, or other competing county requests.
disagreements.side_b_position: Adopt an aggressive early timeline targeting late-February approval and add a standalone budget public hearing date.
side_b_arguments: County commissioners previously finalized budget presentations before receiving DPS numbers; hitting March 1 ensures DPS priorities are on the county manager's table from day one.
Planning early preserves room to revise if state or fiscal circumstances change.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved through a friendly amendment replacing final adoption language with 'authorize initial funding request to county commissioners,' passing 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 8, 2025 annual organizational meeting, the six present members of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education elected new board leadership for the 2025-2026 term. After outgoing chair Millicent Rogers's re-nomination failed 2-4, the board unanimously elected Bettina Umstead 6-0 as Board Chair, and subsequently elected Millicent Rogers 4-2 as Vice Chair following an initial 3-3 tie with Joy Harrell-Goff. The board also unanimously approved the 2025-2026 meeting schedule—deferring a request to make Juneteenth an observed board-calendar holiday until the 2026-2027 cycle—and approved the 2025-2026 out-of-county tuition rate.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Election of Board Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Chair Millicent Rogers opened the organizational meeting and Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis presided over the annual election of the Board Chair with six members present. Two nominations were advanced: Millicent Rogers and Bettina Umstead. Following a 2-4 defeat on Rogers's nomination, Bettina Umstead was unanimously elected Chair and assumed the gavel.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Rogers nomination failed 2-4; Umstead elected Chair 6-0

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Newly elected Chair Bettina Umstead opened nominations for Vice Chair, receiving nominations for Joy Harrell-Goff and Millicent Rogers. The initial voice/standing poll produced a 3-3 split without a majority, prompting Board Attorney Dubes to advise holding an open show-of-hands re-vote. On the re-vote, Harrell-Goff received two votes and Rogers won the Vice Chair seat 4-2.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Initial vote tied 3-3; re-vote failed 2-4 for Harrell-Goff, passed 4-2 for Rogers

agenda_items.title: 2025-2026 Board of Education Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the proposed 2025-2026 meeting calendar and discussed aligning board schedules with district holidays. Joy Harrell-Goff asked to include Juneteenth on the calendar, and members agreed to revisit incorporating Juneteenth into the 2026-2027 schedule next cycle while keeping the 2025-2026 calendar intact.

agenda_items.title: Out-of-County Tuition Rate (2025-2026)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the annual consent item setting the 2025-2026 tuition rate for out-of-county students attending Durham Public Schools. No substantive objections or revisions were raised prior to the vote.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Chair - Nomination of Millicent Rogers
votes.notes: Six board members present. Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis presided over the Chair election. Rogers nomination failed 2-4 before the board proceeded to vote on Umstead's nomination; exact individual breakdown of the second aye vote and fourth nay beyond the six present members was conducted by voice/hands without a formal roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Outgoing Chair Millicent Rogers opened the organizational session at 00:00:39 and turned the floor over to Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis at 00:01:02 to conduct the election of the Board Chair for 2025-2026. Both Millicent Rogers (00:01:56) and Bettina Umstead (00:02:28) were placed in nomination by colleagues. Dr. Lewis called for a vote on the first nomination, Millicent Rogers, at 00:02:38. The nomination received two votes in favor and four opposed, falling short of the majority needed to re-elect Rogers as Chair.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Chair - Nomination of Bettina Umstead
votes.notes: Vote announced as 6-0 unanimous among the six members present (one member absent; individual roll call was not read aloud).
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the 2-4 failure of Millicent Rogers's nomination, Dr. Anthony Lewis put forward the second nomination, Bettina Umstead, for Board Chair at 00:03:10. All six board members present voted in favor, with zero opposed, making the selection unanimous at 00:03:22. Millicent Rogers congratulated Umstead and transferred the gavel at 00:03:31. Chair Umstead then presided over the remainder of the organizational meeting.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair - Initial Tie Vote (Joy Harrell-Goff vs. Millicent Rogers)
votes.notes: Six members present; initial poll produced a 3-3 split between Joy Harrell-Goff (3 votes) and Millicent Rogers (3 votes), failing to achieve a majority and prompting a procedural show-of-hands re-vote.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead opened nominations for Board Vice Chair at 00:03:55, with Joy Harrell-Goff nominated at 00:04:12 and Millicent Rogers nominated at 00:04:21. In the initial ballot between 00:04:40 and 00:05:00, both candidates received three votes each from the six present members, leaving neither with a majority. Board Attorney Dubes advised the board that because no majority was reached, the board needed to repeat the vote by an explicit show of hands. Members proceeded directly to the sequential show-of-hands re-vote.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair - Re-vote on Nomination of Joy Harrell-Goff
votes.notes: Show-of-hands re-vote among six present members after the 3-3 tie; full individual roll call was not read aloud.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Attorney Dubes's procedural guidance after the 3-3 tie, Chair Bettina Umstead conducted a show-of-hands re-vote beginning with Joy Harrell-Goff at 00:05:54. Harrell-Goff received two votes in favor while four members held their votes or opposed, falling short of the majority among the six members present. The result at 00:06:24 cleared the way for the immediate vote on Millicent Rogers.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Vice Chair - Re-vote on Nomination of Millicent Rogers
votes.notes: Show-of-hands re-vote among six present members; individual member names were not read aloud on the record beyond the 4-2 tally.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after the 2-4 defeat of Joy Harrell-Goff's re-vote, Chair Bettina Umstead called for a show of hands on Millicent Rogers for Vice Chair at 00:06:35. Four of the six present board members voted in favor and two opposed, electing Rogers as Vice Chair at 00:06:52. Rogers accepted the Vice Chair role for the 2025-2026 term alongside new Chair Umstead. The board then moved directly to operational calendar and tuition items.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2025-2026 Board of Education Meeting Schedule
votes.notes: Six members present. Board agreed to revisit adding Juneteenth recognition to the 2026-2027 calendar next year.
votes.discussion_detail: At 00:11:53, Vice Chair Millicent Rogers moved and Wendell Tabb seconded approval of the proposed 2025-2026 Board of Education meeting schedule. During discussion, Joy Harrell-Goff requested that the board add Juneteenth to its official board calendar holidays. Other board members and staff noted that the upcoming 2025-2026 calendar had already been coordinated and agreed to bring Juneteenth back for consideration during the 2026-2027 calendar cycle. Chair Umstead called the voice vote at 00:14:36, and the schedule passed unanimously 6-0.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: During its June 26, 2025 monthly meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education adopted a resolution opposing North Carolina Senate Bill 227's DEI restrictions, renewed its School Resource Officer MOU with the Durham County Sheriff's Office (6-0), and approved final readings of Policy 7502 (Salary Administration) and Policies 3520, 4326 (restraint and seclusion, paired with referral back to the Policy Committee), and 7800. The board also approved retroactive 2024-2025 Master's pay for school social workers including McKinney-Vento liaisons and an $80/month nurse supplement, adopted the 2025-2026 interim budget resolution and 2024-2025 Budget Amendment #2, and raised the Glenn Elementary construction change-order authority to $300,000. Significant policy disagreements emerged over whether to pass Policy 4326 immediately while amending it later, whether to fund a $200/month bus monitor supplement immediately or await state budget clarity, and SRO uniform practices.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board adjusted its agenda by pulling Consent Item B (Policy 4326) into Academic Services for discussion, tabling Policy 2305/Communication Guidelines (Item F) to the August 14 work session/retreat, and adding Item 3B (Resolution Against Senate Bill 227). All seven members approved the amended agenda.

agenda_items.title: May 22, 2025 Meeting Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed the May 22, 2025 meeting minutes, adding a spelling correction and inserting the individual 6-1 breakdown of the closed-session personnel vote into the public record. The corrected minutes passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Rethink Ed, Grounds, Nutrition, Policy 2231, Afterschool Pilot, Budget Amendment #2, Interim Budget Resolution)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Policy 4326 pulled for separate debate and Communication Guidelines tabled, the board took up the remaining consent agenda covering instructional contracts, grounds maintenance, school nutrition bids, Policy 2231 (Policy Committee), an eight-school afterschool pilot, 2024-2025 Budget Amendment #2, and the 2025-2026 Interim Budget Resolution.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Sheriff's Office School Resource Officer (SRO) MOU
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Sheriff Clarence Birkhead presented school safety updates covering threat assessments, mental health co-response partnerships, and SRO staffing. Board members Natalie Beyer and Joy Harrell-Goff questioned SRO uniform and plain-clothes practices, while Sheriff Birkhead defended visible uniforms as a safety standard. The board subsequently renewed the SRO MOU 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Opposing North Carolina Senate Bill 227
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bettina Umstead introduced a resolution opposing Senate Bill 227's restrictions on diversity, equity, and inclusion in public education, emphasizing that DPS would continue protecting marginalized students and accurate history. Jessica Carda-Auten offered friendly amendments strengthening alignment with DPS policies and anti-discrimination language, and the board adopted the resolution unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Code of Character, Conduct & Support (Policy 4301) Informational Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration presented updates on Policy 4301 (Code of Character, Conduct, and Support) outlining restorative practices, behavioral tiers, and support alignment ahead of the 2025-2026 school year. Board members asked clarifying questions about implementation consistency and family communication without taking a formal vote.

agenda_items.title: Second Reading of Policies 3520, 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion), and 7800
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following extensive debate over pulled Policy 4326, members disagreed on whether to delay adoption until demographic data reporting and seclusion safeguards were added or to pass baseline state-aligned training language now and immediately refer the policy back to the Policy Committee. Jessica Carda-Auten moved an amendment referring Policy 4326 to the Policy Committee for revisions, and all three policies passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pay Amendments for School Social Workers and School Nurses
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration proposed retroactive 2024-2025 Master's pay for school social workers—explicitly confirming inclusion of two McKinney-Vento homeless liaison social workers (up to $80,000 total)—and an $80/month supplement for school nurses (up to $9,000). Emily Chávez moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the clarified motion, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Policy 7502 Salary Administration (Final Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the final reading of Policy 7502 governing district salary administration, extra-duty compensation, and payroll controls. After brief clarifying questions, the board adopted the policy unanimously.

agenda_items.title: 2025-2026 Budget Prioritization Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter updated the board on budget priorities under the county's $10.35 million expansion allocation, sparking debate over whether to immediately authorize a $200/month bus monitor supplement (~$140,000) or hold flexible reserves pending the state budget and a comprehensive classified pay study. No formal budget amendment vote was taken at this meeting.

agenda_items.title: Glenn Elementary Change Order Authority Increase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operations staff requested temporarily increasing superintendent change-order authority on the Glenn Elementary construction project from $90,000 to $300,000 through August 25, 2025 to avoid summer schedule delays prior to school opening. Members approved the temporary authority unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: At the close of open business, the board voted unanimously to enter closed session for confidential legal, personnel, and statutory matters.

votes.item_title: Agenda Review and Approval (Pulling Policy 4326, Tabling Item F, Adding SB 227 Resolution)
votes.notes: All seven board members present and voting Aye.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Millicent Rogers opened agenda review at 00:33:53, where board members discussed adjusting the night's order of business to allow substantive deliberation on several high-interest items. Members requested pulling Policy 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion) from the consent agenda into the Academic Services block, deferring Communication Guidelines (Item F) to the August 14 work session, and adding Bettina Umstead's proposed resolution opposing North Carolina Senate Bill 227 as Item 3B. Natalie Beyer moved and Wendell Tabb seconded approval of the amended agenda. At 00:35:15, the board approved the revised agenda 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 22, 2025 Meeting Minutes (with Corrections)
votes.notes: Included individual transparency addition for the May 22 closed-session 6-1 vote.
votes.discussion_detail: At 00:35:35, the board reviewed the draft minutes of the May 22, 2025 monthly meeting. Natalie Beyer moved and Jessica Carda-Auten seconded approval with two revisions: correcting a spelling error and adding the individual 6-1 member vote breakdown for a personnel action taken in closed session on May 22. Board members supported recording the detailed tally to ensure transparency in the official record. The corrected minutes passed 7-0 by voice vote at 00:37:05.

votes.item_title: Durham County Sheriff's Office School Resource Officer (SRO) Memorandum of Understanding
votes.notes: Chair announced 'passes 6' (6-0), indicating one member briefly stepped away or did not cast an audible vote; no nays were recorded.
votes.discussion_detail: Prior to the vote, Sheriff Clarence Birkhead presented an annual school safety update highlighting SRO training, threat assessment teams, and mental health co-response collaboration. During Q&A, Natalie Beyer and Joy Harrell-Goff asked whether SROs could consider plain-clothes or softer uniform options to reduce student intimidation, which Sheriff Birkhead declined on the grounds that identifiable uniforms ensure rapid emergency recognition and officer safety. At 01:59:59, Joy Harrell-Goff moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the annual SRO MOU. The chair declared the motion passed with 6 votes in favor and none opposed at 02:00:18.

votes.item_title: Resolution Opposing North Carolina Senate Bill 227 (DEI Restrictions)
votes.notes: Drafted by Bettina Umstead and added as Item 3B during agenda review.
votes.discussion_detail: At 02:00:43, Bettina Umstead introduced a board resolution opposing North Carolina Senate Bill 227, explaining that the bill's restrictions on diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives threaten inclusive curriculum, staff training, and supportive spaces for DPS's diverse student body. Jessica Carda-Auten offered friendly revisions aligning the resolution's citations with DPS's non-discrimination and equity policies, which Umstead accepted. Joy Harrell-Goff moved and Emily Chávez seconded adoption of the amended resolution, with members voicing strong support for standing firm on equity despite state legislative pressures. The resolution passed unanimously 7-0 at 02:07:32.

votes.item_title: Second Reading Approval of Policies 3520, 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion), and 7800 (with Referral Amendment)
votes.notes: Passed 7-0 as amended so baseline state-aligned training language took effect immediately while Policy Committee works on revisions.
votes.discussion_detail: After pulling Policy 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion) from consent, board members engaged in an extended debate starting around 03:34:55 over whether the draft adequately constrained seclusion and mandated transparent demographic reporting. Joy Harrell-Goff and Natalie Beyer initially favored approving the baseline update alongside Policies 3520 and 7800 so staff training rules remained current, whereas Jessica Carda-Auten, Emily Chávez, and Bettina Umstead pressed for stricter safeguards and disaggregated data reporting. To bridge the divide, Carda-Auten proposed amending the motion at 03:41:24 and 03:46:18 to adopt the baseline policies now while formally referring Policy 4326 to the newly created Policy Committee for substantive revision. The amended motion passed 7-0 at 03:47:31.

votes.item_title: Pay Amendments for School Social Workers (Retroactive Master's Pay) and School Nurses ($80/Month Supplement)
votes.notes: Included retroactive 2024-2025 Master's pay for eligible school social workers including 2 McKinney-Vento liaisons (up to $80,000) and an $80/month nurse supplement (up to $9,000); restated at 04:26:57 with Harrell-Goff seconding after initial Carda-Auten second.
votes.discussion_detail: Administration brought forward compensation adjustments at 04:02:43 to grant retroactive 2024-2025 Master's pay for school social workers (up to $80,000) and an $80 monthly supplement for school nurses (up to $9,000). During lengthy discussion, Emily Chávez and Jessica Carda-Auten sought explicit assurance that two McKinney-Vento homeless liaison social workers were covered and raised concerns about other Master's-prepared student support specialists left off the proposal. After finance and HR staff confirmed McKinney-Vento liaisons were included within the $80,000 cap, the motion was restated at 04:26:57 with Emily Chávez moving and Joy Harrell-Goff seconding. At 04:32:04, the board approved both pay amendments 7-0.

votes.item_title: Policy 7502 Salary Administration (Final Reading)
votes.notes: Final reading following May 8 first reading and subsequent administrative refinements.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the social worker and nurse pay vote, the board turned at 04:32:13 to the final reading of Policy 7502 governing Salary Administration across Durham Public Schools. HR and finance staff confirmed updates clarifying salary placement, extra-duty compensation during non-contract time, and documentation standards following board feedback at earlier sessions. Emily Chávez moved adoption and Natalie Beyer seconded. The policy passed unanimously 7-0 by voice vote at 04:38:07.

votes.item_title: Glenn Elementary Construction Change Order Authority Increase ($90,000 to $300,000)
votes.notes: Temporary authority increase effective through August 25, 2025 to keep summer completion on track.
votes.discussion_detail: Operations staff requested at 05:17:32 that the board temporarily increase administrative change-order authority for the Glenn Elementary project from $90,000 to $300,000 through August 25, 2025. Staff explained that rapid summer construction approvals were essential to avoid delaying the school's readiness for students in August, and pledged to report all change orders back to the board. Emily Chávez moved and Natalie Beyer seconded the request. At 05:22:01, the board voted 7-0 in favor.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Entered closed session at the conclusion of open business.
votes.discussion_detail: At 05:22:46, with all open-session agenda items completed, Natalie Beyer moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded entering closed session for statutory personnel and legal matters. No further discussion occurred. The voice vote at 05:23:06 passed unanimously 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
disagreements.issue: Policy 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion) Timing and Safeguards
disagreements.summary: Board members split over whether to adopt the revised Policy 4326 immediately or hold it for stronger limits on seclusion and demographic data reporting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require stronger seclusion limits, parent-notification timelines, and disaggregated data reporting before finalizing policy language.
side_a_arguments: Seclusion and restraint disproportionately affect students with disabilities and Black and brown students, requiring explicit demographic data reporting.
Delaying finalization or immediately committing to Policy Committee revisions protects vulnerable students.
disagreements.side_b_position: Pass the baseline policy update now to align with state training rules without holding up Policies 3520 and 7800.
side_b_arguments: Baseline policy language is needed promptly so district training and compliance remain current for the upcoming school year.
Further refinements can be processed systematically through the Policy Committee.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved via Carda-Auten's compromise amendment passing the baseline policy 7-0 while simultaneously referring Policy 4326 back to the Policy Committee for revisions.

disagreements.issue: Immediate $200/Month Bus Monitor Supplement vs. Awaiting State Budget and Classified Pay Study
disagreements.summary: During the budget prioritization update, members disagreed over whether to commit ~$140,000 immediately for a $200/month bus monitor weather/retention supplement or preserve flexible funds until state action and a broader classified salary study.
disagreements.side_a_position: Fund the $200/month bus monitor supplement now alongside the bus driver supplement.
side_a_arguments: Bus monitors work alongside bus drivers on the same routes and face the same weather-related pay interruptions and retention challenges.
Waiting months leaves low-paid classified transportation staff behind.
disagreements.side_b_position: Hold remaining flexible funds pending state legislative budget numbers and a comprehensive classified pay study.
side_b_arguments: Committing recurring local expansion dollars piecemeal before seeing the state budget risks exacerbating mid-year shortfalls or salary compression.
A systematic classified compensation review ensures equitable alignment across job groups.
disagreements.resolution: Informational budget discussion only; no final allocation vote was taken at the June 26 meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
disagreements.issue: School Resource Officer (SRO) Uniforms vs. Plain-Clothes Options
disagreements.summary: Board members questioned Sheriff Clarence Birkhead on whether SROs could wear softer or plain-clothes attire on campus, while the Sheriff insisted on standard recognizable uniforms.
disagreements.side_a_position: Explore plain-clothes or less-militarized attire for campus SROs.
side_a_arguments: Standard tactical/police uniforms can feel intimidating or traumatic to students and undermine non-punitive school climate goals.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain standard identifiable law-enforcement uniforms for campus SROs.
side_b_arguments: Clear uniform visibility ensures students, staff, and responding emergency personnel can immediately identify sworn officers during a crisis.
disagreements.resolution: Sheriff Birkhead retained uniform policy; the board subsequently voted 6-0 to renew the SRO MOU.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Bettina Umstead with all seven members present, the June 10, 2025 work session featured approval of an annual student technology fee ($15 elementary, $30 middle/high with waivers), the 2025-2028 Academically and Intellectually Gifted (AIG) Plan, and first readings of Policies 7800, 3520, 4326, and 2231 (Policy Committee). The board deferred action on two facilities/financial items (5A and 5B) to June 26 by a 7-0 vote, but rejected Natalie Beyer's motion to also move the Legal Services RFP decision (5C) off the table by a 1-6 vote before hearing presentations from competing firms Poyner Spruill and Tharrington Smith. Intense debates emerged over Legal Services RFP rubric transparency, Policy 2231 committee timelines and meeting cadence (with 5-2 and 3-4 straw polls), and PreK/K 1:1 Chromebook screen-time policies.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval & May 8, 2025 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over approval of the June 10 work session agenda and the May 8, 2025 work session minutes. Both procedural items passed 7-0 without revision.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment (Riverside Latin Program)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six parents, students, and alumni spoke in support of preserving the Latin program at Riverside High School, urging the board and administration to protect staffing and course offerings for world languages.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 5 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: District leaders presented an update on Strategic Plan Priority 5 metrics covering operational effectiveness, governance accountability, and resource alignment. Board members asked clarifying questions regarding dashboard benchmarks.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-H)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved Consent Agenda items A through H in a single motion moved by Natalie Beyer and seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten without pulling any consent items.

agenda_items.title: Annual Student Technology Fee ($15 ES / $30 MS & HS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT staff presented the annual student device technology fee ($15 for elementary students and $30 for middle and high school students with hardship waivers), while board members Emily Chávez and Bettina Umstead questioned PreK and kindergarten 1:1 Chromebook use. The fee schedule passed 7-0.

agenda_items.title: DPS 2025-2028 AIG Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Advanced Academics Director Laura Parrott presented the state-required three-year 2025-2028 Academically and Intellectually Gifted (AIG) plan expanding equitable identification and auto-enrollment practices. Members praised the program and approved the plan unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Scheduling Motions & Legal Services RFP Presentations (Poyner Spruill vs. Tharrington Smith)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 7-0 to defer Items 5A and 5B to June 26, but rejected Natalie Beyer's motion (1-6) to defer Item 5C (Legal Services) as well. Following heated debate over RFP scoring transparency and incumbent evaluations, both Poyner Spruill and Tharrington Smith presented to the board, which formed a three-member working group rather than voting on a final contract.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Deferral of 5A/5B passed 7-0; deferral of 5C failed 1-6; Legal Services contract deferred to working group

agenda_items.title: First Reading of Policies 7800, 3520, and 4326
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented first-reading updates to Policies 7800, 3520, and 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion) for advancement toward second reading at the June 26 monthly meeting.

agenda_items.title: Policy 2231 (Policy Committee) First Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated how the new Policy Committee should operate, splitting 5-2 in a straw poll in favor of an August 31 policy submission deadline over July 15, and rejecting (3 votes) monthly meeting cadence and rolling submission models in straw polls before passing first reading 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Policy 2231 first reading, the board voted unanimously to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Agenda Review and Approval
votes.notes: All seven board members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Bettina Umstead called for approval of the June 10, 2025 monthly work session agenda at 00:10:08. Joy Harrell-Goff moved approval and Wendell Tabb seconded. No amendments were proposed at that point in the meeting. The voice vote at 00:10:25 passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Approval of May 8, 2025 Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Approved as presented.
votes.discussion_detail: At 00:10:33, the board reviewed the draft minutes from the May 8, 2025 work session. Natalie Beyer moved approval and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. No corrections or edits were requested by any member. At 00:10:52, the minutes passed 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Annual Student Technology Fee ($15 Elementary / $30 Middle & High School)
votes.notes: Includes fee waivers for families with financial hardship; follows discussion on PreK/K 1:1 Chromebook deployment.
votes.discussion_detail: District technology leadership presented the annual student technology fee proposal of $15 for elementary students and $30 for middle and high school students, noting availability of financial hardship waivers. During discussion, Emily Chávez and Chair Bettina Umstead questioned Dr. King on whether PreK and kindergarten students truly needed 1:1 Chromebooks given screen-time concerns in early grades, while staff defended device readiness and assessment compatibility. At 02:35:16, Emily Chávez moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the annual technology fee. The voice vote at 02:35:34 passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: DPS 2025-2028 Academically and Intellectually Gifted (AIG) Plan
votes.notes: Three-year NCDPI-required district AIG plan.

votes.item_title: Procedural Motion: Defer Item 5C (Legal Services RFP) to June 24/26
votes.notes: Chair announced six opposed after Beyer moved to postpone Item 5C; Harrell-Goff seconded for discussion but voted with the majority to keep the presentations on the night's agenda.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after deferring Items 5A and 5B, Natalie Beyer moved at 03:12:20 to also postpone Item 5C (Legal Services RFP selection) to June 24 or June 26, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff. votes.notes: Advanced from first reading toward June 26 second reading.
votes.discussion_detail: Staff presented first-reading updates to Policies 7800, 3520, and 4326 (Restraint and Seclusion) ahead of scheduled second reading on June 26. Joy Harrell-Goff moved approval of first reading at 04:11:04 and Natalie Beyer seconded. No member opposed advancing the drafts for further review between meetings. The first-reading motion passed unanimously 7-0 at 04:11:18.

votes.item_title: Policy 2231 (Policy Committee) First Reading
votes.notes: Followed three non-binding straw polls shaping the committee charter.
votes.discussion_detail: Board members spent over an hour shaping draft Policy 2231 establishing a formal Policy Committee, dividing in straw polls over how frequently the committee would meet and how members could submit policy requests. Five members favored an August 31 submission deadline over July 15 (5-2 straw poll), while proposals for monthly meetings and rolling submissions each garnered only three votes in straw polls. Following those parameters, Emily Chávez moved first-reading approval at 05:23:33 and Wendell Tabb seconded. At 05:25:54, the board approved Policy 2231 on first reading 7-0.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Entered closed session at end of work session.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
disagreements.issue: Legal Services RFP Selection Process, Rubric Transparency, and Deferral (Item 5C)
disagreements.summary: Board members clashed over whether to defer Legal Services RFP presentations (failing 1-6) and over transparency of the scoring rubric used to narrow finalists to Poyner Spruill and Tharrington Smith.
disagreements.side_a_position: Demand full RFP scoring rubrics, fee transparency, and careful evaluation before deciding on legal counsel.
side_a_arguments: Board members had not received complete RFP evaluation matrices and pricing comparisons ahead of the presentations.
Contracting board legal counsel is a core board governance responsibility requiring transparent comparative data.
disagreements.side_b_position: Proceed with hearing both finalist firms as scheduled rather than deferring Item 5C.
side_b_arguments: Both law firms had already been invited and were present in the room to present to the board.
Hearing presentations does not force an immediate final contract vote.
disagreements.resolution: Deferral motion failed 1-6; both Poyner Spruill and Tharrington Smith presented starting at 04:11:53, and no contract vote was taken—instead the board formed a three-member working group to review options.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
disagreements.issue: Policy 2231 Policy Committee Submission Deadlines and Meeting Cadence
disagreements.summary: Members divided in multiple straw polls (5-2 and 3-4) over Policy Committee cadence, rolling vs. fixed deadlines, and whether the policy request deadline should be July 15 or August 31.
disagreements.side_a_position: Set an August 31 submission deadline and structured periodic review cycles rather than continuous rolling submissions or monthly meetings.
side_a_arguments: An August 31 deadline gives newly organized board leadership and staff realistic summer bandwidth.
Fixed review windows prevent overwhelming district staff and legal counsel with continuous ad-hoc policy drafts.
disagreements.side_b_position: Prefer earlier July 15 deadlines, monthly committee meetings, or rolling submissions.
side_b_arguments: More frequent monthly meetings and rolling submissions allow timely board responsiveness to urgent equity and operational policy issues.
disagreements.resolution: Majority favored August 31 in a 5-2 straw poll while monthly cadence and rolling submissions failed with 3 votes each; Policy 2231 then advanced on first reading 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
disagreements.issue: PreK and Kindergarten 1:1 Chromebook Deployment vs. Screen-Time Concerns
disagreements.summary: During the technology fee discussion, Emily Chávez and Chair Bettina Umstead challenged district administration on whether PreK and kindergarten students should receive 1:1 Chromebooks.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question 1:1 Chromebooks for PreK and kindergarten learners on developmental and cost grounds.
side_a_arguments: Excessive screen exposure in PreK and kindergarten classrooms is developmentally questionable when shared classroom sets could suffice.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain districtwide 1:1 device provisioning across elementary grades.
side_b_arguments: Consistent 1:1 devices support diagnostic assessments, digital literacy integration, and standardized fleet management across schools.
disagreements.resolution: Board approved the annual technology fee 7-0 while flagging early-grade device utilization for ongoing administrative review.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven members present and 30 public speakers addressing the School for Creative Studies high school phase-out, social worker and interventionist Master's pay, bus monitors, and Exceptional Children funding, the DPS Board of Education focused its May 22, 2025 meeting on amending Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer). After taking an emergency recess so newly circulated May 22 and May 4 drafts could be uploaded to BoardDocs and seeing Natalie Beyer's motion to table to June 10 fail for lack of a second, the board voted 4-3 to adopt a modified Meet and Confer policy lowering the ERO recognition threshold to 11% with optional third-party verification. The board also reviewed a nearly $966 million 10-year Facility Conditions Assessment need and prioritized FY25-26 budget allocations under the County Manager's $10.35 million expansion figure.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment (30 Speakers)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Thirty community members, educators, students, and parents testified regarding the proposed phase-out of high school grades at the School for Creative Studies, retroactive Master's pay for school social workers and interventionists, bus monitor compensation, and Exceptional Children funding.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval & April 24, 2025 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved its May 22 agenda after reordering Item 5A ahead of Item 4A, and unanimously approved the April 24, 2025 monthly meeting minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A-N)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved Consent Agenda items A through N by unanimous voice vote without pulling items.

agenda_items.title: Procedural Recess & Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer Committee) Modifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members paused for a unanimous recess to upload both the May 22 and May 4 drafts of Policy 7215 to BoardDocs. Following sharp debate over notice, NC Public Records confidentiality, and the 11% employee organization threshold, a 4-3 majority adopted the amended May 22 draft.

agenda_items.title: Facility Conditions Assessment (FCA) and Local Educational Guidelines (LEGs) Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Capital planning staff and consultants presented the districtwide Facility Conditions Assessment and Local Educational Guidelines, identifying roughly $966 million in 10-year capital needs across aging school buildings.

agenda_items.title: FY25-26 Budget Prioritization Activity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teter facilitated a board prioritization exercise adjusting DPS's FY25-26 spending plan to the County Manager's recommended $10.35 million operating expansion, leaving roughly $3.16 million in flexible expansion capacity after continuation obligations.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session at the end of the meeting (where subsequent June 26 minutes recorded a 6-1 personnel vote).

votes.item_title: Agenda Review and Approval (Reordering 5A ahead of 4A)
votes.notes: All seven board members present.
votes.discussion_detail: At 01:04:58, the board reviewed the May 22 monthly meeting agenda and agreed to reorder Item 5A ahead of Item 4A. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the adjusted agenda and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded. No members opposed the reordering. The motion passed 7-0 by voice vote at 01:07:05.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 24, 2025 Monthly Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Approved as presented.
votes.discussion_detail: Following agenda approval, the board considered the draft minutes of the April 24, 2025 monthly meeting at 01:07:15. Natalie Beyer moved approval and Emily Chávez seconded. No edits or objections were offered. At 01:07:35, the minutes passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Procedural Recess to Upload Policy 7215 Drafts (May 22 and May 4 Versions)
votes.notes: Temporary recess to ensure public and board access to both versions before debating Policy 7215.
votes.discussion_detail: As the board prepared to debate Policy 7215 at 01:54:50, members raised concerns that a revised May 22 draft had been distributed shortly before the meeting and was not yet posted alongside the May 4 draft in BoardDocs. Wendell Tabb moved a recess, seconded by Jessica Carda-Auten, and Natalie Beyer offered a friendly amendment ensuring both the May 22 and May 4 drafts were uploaded for public transparency. Members agreed unanimously to pause proceedings so staff could post the documents. The recess passed 7-0 at 02:01:53.

votes.item_title: Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer Committee) Modifications - Amended May 22 Draft
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer moved to table the policy to June 10 at 03:16:07, which failed for lack of a second. Passed 4-3 with Chair Millicent Rogers joining Chávez, Harrell-Goff, and Carda-Auten.
votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening around 02:30:17 and formally refining the motion at 03:33:55, Emily Chávez moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded adopting the May 22 draft of Policy 7215 establishing an 11% membership threshold for Employee Representative Organization (ERO) participation, defining EROs, and permitting HR or third-party verification. Natalie Beyer, Bettina Umstead, and Wendell Tabb objected strongly to acting on an eleventh-hour rewrite without legal vetting on North Carolina Public Records Act confidentiality for membership lists and tried to table the vote to June 10 (failing for lack of a second at 03:16:07). During floor negotiation, sponsors agreed to strike 'all', strike the Section C Appendix, and mandate mutual agreement on any third-party certifier. In the roll call between 03:59:13 and 04:01:36, Chávez, Harrell-Goff, Carda-Auten, and Chair Millicent Rogers voted Aye while Tabb, Beyer, and Umstead voted Nay, passing the modified policy 4-3.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: June 26 minutes subsequently recorded that a 6-1 personnel vote took place during this closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: At 05:19:17, after concluding the budget prioritization discussion, Natalie Beyer moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded entering closed session for personnel and legal matters. No discussion was held in open session. The voice vote at 05:19:44 passed unanimously 7-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting
disagreements.issue: Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer) 11% Threshold, Third-Party Verification, and Late-Draft Process
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-3 over adopting last-minute May 22 modifications to Policy 7215 lowering the ERO recognition threshold to 11% and allowing third-party verification.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt the amended May 22 draft immediately with an 11% threshold, mutual-agreement third-party verification, and streamlined ERO language.
side_a_arguments: The 11% threshold and third-party verification respond directly to months of employee advocacy and protect worker privacy while keeping the policy moving before summer.
Striking 'all' and the Section C Appendix and requiring mutual agreement on a third-party certifier address administrative feasibility concerns.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer or reject the May 22 rewrite pending formal legal review and standard public-notice procedures.
side_b_arguments: Circulating major policy changes the day of the meeting circumvents transparent board process and public notice.
Third-party membership verification and ERO record handling raise unresolved North Carolina Public Records Act risks.
disagreements.resolution: Beyer's motion to table to June 10 failed for lack of a second; the amended May 22 Policy 7215 draft passed 4-3.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education & Durham County Board of Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
meetings.presiding_chair: Nida Allam (BOCC Chair presiding Joint Meeting)
meetings.executive_summary: At their May 14, 2025 joint quarterly meeting, Durham Public Schools Board members and the Durham County Board of Commissioners unanimously approved the joint agenda and February 18, 2025 minutes before examining long-term capital needs and FY25-26 budget gaps. DPS capital staff presented a Facility Conditions Assessment identifying $900M-$965M in immediate/10-year repair needs and a ~$2 billion comprehensive CIP envelope, while DPS CFO Jeremy Teter contrasted DPS's $15.9M operating expansion request against County Manager Claudia Hager's recommended $10.35M operating increase and $6M capital outlay (+$10M CIP reserve), leaving a $5.6M operating gap and $2M annual capital gap. Leaders also agreed to update their 2017/2021 joint MOU and received an update on the newly signed May 9 Durham PreK MOA.

agenda_items.title: Joint Agenda Approval and February 18, 2025 Joint Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: BOCC Chair Nida Allam called the joint quarterly session to order, and both boards unanimously approved the meeting agenda and the February 18, 2025 joint meeting minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda approved unanimously; Feb 18 minutes approved unanimously

agenda_items.title: Facility Conditions Assessment (FCA) and Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Preview
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Devon Mitchell presented DPS's Facility Conditions Assessment across 6.4 million square feet of buildings averaging 59 years old, projecting ~$900M-$965M in FCA needs and ~$2B in total 10-year CIP requirements including growth, Local Educational Guidelines, Bethesda/Lyons Farm capacity, and closed-school reuse. Commissioners and board members pressed staff on +20% tariff/construction escalation and net-zero design costs.

agenda_items.title: DPS FY25-26 Budget Request Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis and CFO Jeremy Teter outlined DPS's 31,188-student enrollment, $30M+ in prior shortfall corrections, 27 central office RIFs, and $222M+ local request, highlighting a $5.6M operating gap, $2M capital gap, and $4M Medicaid reimbursement risk under the county's recommended budget.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Manager FY25-26 Recommended Budget Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County Manager Claudia Hager explained how the 60% countywide property revaluation lowered the revenue-neutral rate to 51.92 cents, with a proposed 3.5-cent tax increase amid slowing sales tax growth, funding a $224M total DPS county allocation ($10.35M operating expansion, $6M capital, and $10M CIP reserve) ahead of June 9 adoption.

agenda_items.title: Assessment of DPS/BOCC Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board and commission leaders reviewed the 2017 MOU and 2021 draft update governing joint capital planning and fiscal coordination, reaching consensus for leadership and staff from both bodies to prepare an updated draft for the next joint meeting.

agenda_items.title: DPS PreK / Durham PreK Update & Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pittman announced a newly signed PreK MOA and data-sharing agreement effective May 9 between DPS and county PreK partners. Public commenter Javanah Lewis (EPIC & DCABP) urged both boards to fund $6.1M in Black community education priorities before adjournment at 03:05:39.

votes.item_title: Joint Quarterly Meeting Agenda Review and Approval
votes.notes: Joint vote of present DPS Board of Education members and Durham County Board of Commissioners.
votes.discussion_detail: At 00:09:09, BOCC Chair Nida Allam called for a motion to approve the May 14, 2025 joint quarterly meeting agenda. disagreements.side_a_position: Fast-track or adopt a structured community engagement policy featuring board school visits, listening protocols, and community QR feedback tools.

votes.item_title: Amendment to Policy 7215: Raise ERO Threshold from 6% to 20%
votes.notes: Proposed raising the Employee Representative Organization threshold in Policy 7215 from 6% to 20% to prevent excessive committee fragmentation while maintaining meaningful worker representation.
votes.discussion_detail: At 04:21:48, Jessica Carda-Auten moved and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded an amendment to replace the proposed 6% membership threshold for Employee Representative Organizations (EROs) with 20%. Supporters argued a 20% threshold avoided splintering worker representation across tiny groups while giving recognized organizations credible standing with the superintendent, whereas opponents backed the administration's 6% floor to preserve broad inclusion and avoid an exclusive threshold seen as biased toward DAE. Following the unanimous cloture vote, Wendell Tabb called the roll between 05:04:28 and 05:04:55. Harrell-Goff, Chávez, and Carda-Auten voted Aye, while Beyer, Umstead, Rogers, and Tabb voted Nay, defeating the amendment 3-4.

votes.item_title: Main Motion: Waive Second Reading & Adopt Policy 7215 (Meet and Confer Committee, 6% Threshold)
votes.notes: In the roll call transcript (05:06:48-05:07:47), Chávez, Harrell-Goff, and Tabb were captured voting No and Umstead and Beyer voting Yes, while Rogers (seconder) and Carda-Auten's final roll-call voices were not captured by ASR before the chair moved to follow-up items; subsequent May 22 board proceedings confirmed the 6% Policy 7215 passed 4-3 on April 10.
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer moved at 03:59:36 (restated at 05:05:26) and Millicent Rogers seconded waiving second reading and adopting Policy 7215 with a 6% ERO threshold, amended Section E1 naming the largest ERO as committee vice chair, mutually exclusive percentage bands in the seat table, and deletion of 'other employees' in Section C3. Supporters argued passing a workable policy immediately ended 14 months of delay and complied with board legal counsel's equal-access guidance, while Chávez, Harrell-Goff, and Tabb objected that a 6% threshold and committee structure undermined DAE's collective-voice proposal and urged mediation or a 20% compromise. On the roll call starting at 05:06:48, Chávez, Harrell-Goff, and Tabb voted No while Umstead and Beyer voted Aye alongside seconder Rogers and Carda-Auten (whose roll-call audio dropped in ASR before the next item), adopting the 6% policy 4-3 (later revisited and modified May 22).

Temporary Chair Wendell Tabb conducted a roll call at 05:13:03-05:13:18. All seven board members voted Aye.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Work Session
disagreements.issue: Policy 7215 Meet and Confer ERO Threshold (6% vs. 20%), Committee Structure, and Waiving Second Reading
disagreements.summary: The board split 3-4 on Jessica Carda-Auten's amendment for a 20% ERO threshold and then 4-3 to waive second reading and adopt the administration-backed 6% Policy 7215 draft.
disagreements.side_a_position: Require a 20% ERO threshold or pursue further mediation with DAE rather than adopting a 6% threshold in one meeting.
side_a_arguments: A 6% threshold dilutes representative worker organizations and creates an unbalanced Meet and Confer committee.
Waiving second reading cuts off community and worker feedback on a policy 14 months in the making.
disagreements.side_b_position: Waive second reading and adopt the 6% ERO threshold policy immediately with technical guardrails (Section E1 vice chair and exclusive seat table).
side_b_arguments: Legal counsel advised that lower thresholds avoid improper exclusivity under North Carolina law and ensure broad employee access.
Adopting a baseline policy now lets Meet and Confer begin functioning immediately, with future amendments always possible.
disagreements.resolution: Carda-Auten's 20% threshold amendment failed 3-4 (Tabb joined Rogers, Beyer, Umstead in Nay); on the main motion Tabb voted Nay while Beyer, Umstead, Rogers, and Carda-Auten carried the 6% policy 4-3 (later modified to 11% on May 22).

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Budget Hearing | 3/20/25
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its first FY 2025-26 budget hearing on March 20, 2025, featuring an unexpected briefing from CFO Jeremy Teeter on the Dollars & Decisions ThoughtExchange community survey before receiving public testimony. Survey feedback from 1,531 participants highlighted staff compensation, staffing levels, transportation reliability, school safety, and fiscal transparency as top community priorities. Two public speakers urged the board to resolve classified pay compression and bus driver shortages while criticizing the lack of a published proposed budget ahead of the hearing, after which the board voted to enter closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome, and Agenda Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board Chair Millicent Rogers called the budget hearing to order with six members present and acknowledged interpreters. Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved to amend the agenda to insert a brief budget feedback presentation from CFO Jeremy Teeter prior to the public hearing.

agenda_items.title: CFO Presentation on Dollars & Decisions Budget Feedback
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter presented results from the Dollars & Decisions ThoughtExchange engagement tool, which recorded 1,531 participants, 1,244 thoughts, and 28,229 ratings, including 171 non-native English participants across Spanish, Arabic, French, and Vietnamese. Top-rated community themes emphasized competitive staff pay and classified compensation, adequate school staffing, transportation stability, school safety, and transparent budget management.

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Public Budget Hearing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham Association of Educators President Micah Tweetmeyer urged the board to address classified pay compression, the ongoing transportation crisis, restoration of master's degree pay, and formal meet-and-confer engagement. DPS parent Lauren Sartin criticized holding a budget hearing before a proposed budget was released to the public and urged eliminating non-mandated testing, unnecessary professional development, one-to-one devices in grades K-2, and major facility contracts.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session Motion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following the conclusion of public testimony, Chair Millicent Rogers requested a motion to move into closed session for the purposes stated on the published agenda. No additional public business occurred before the livestream concluded.

votes.notes: Six board members present; added CFO Jeremy Teeter's ThoughtExchange presentation prior to the public hearing.
