Teeter then briefed the board and public on participation metrics and top-ranked budget priorities from 1,531 respondents.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Board transitioned to closed session following the two-speaker budget hearing.
votes.discussion_detail: After hearing three-minute testimonies from Durham Association of Educators President Micah Tweetmeyer and DPS parent Lauren Sartin during the FY 2025-26 public budget hearing, Chair Millicent Rogers thanked the speakers and noted the board would review written and spoken feedback alongside CFO Jeremy Teeter's ThoughtExchange data. Bettina Umstead moved that the board enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, and Natalie Beyer seconded. No board member raised objections or requested additional discussion on the motion. The board voted 6-0 by voice vote to enter closed session at 00:40:36.

meetings.executive_summary: Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten presided over the March 14, 2025 Durham Delegates legislative breakfast meeting with state lawmakers Rep. Ray Jeffers, Sen. Sophia Chitlik, Rep. Zack Hawkins, and Rep. Marcia Morey. Board members, Superintendent Anthony Lewis, CFO Jeremy Teeter, and Dr. Nicholas King presented the district's 2025 legislative priorities, highlighting local general-fund drains from the state's 13% Exceptional Children funding cap ($5.5M) and 10% English Language Learner cap ($6M), classified/bus-driver pay competitiveness, DMV commercial road-test delays, and State Health Plan premium instability. Legislators committed to coordinating with DPS leadership on targeted state bills, $4 billion statewide school bond prospects, and opening the new Durham Early College of Health Sciences in August 2025.

Board members, DPS cabinet officials, Durham Public Schools Foundation CEO Erica Wilkins, and four members of Durham's General Assembly delegation introduced themselves.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jessica Carda-Auten, Emily Chávez, Natalie Beyer, and Superintendent Anthony Lewis outlined the district's legislative priorities, focusing on lifting the 13% EC funding cap (costing DPS $5.5M locally) and 10% ELL cap (costing $6M locally, equivalent to roughly 150 teaching positions). They also urged raising starting classified/bus driver wages above $17.50/hour, supporting educator housing, expanding mental health staffing ratios, and preserving public school funding amid voucher expansion.

CFO Jeremy Teeter raised alarm over State Health Plan reporting changes and potential premium hikes under the new State Treasurer, while Joy Harrell-Goff and Emily Chávez stressed student anxiety regarding federal immigration enforcement and support for a $4 billion state school bond.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nicholas King briefed lawmakers on the August 2025 opening of the Durham Early College of Health Sciences at the former Holton facility in partnership with Duke Health and Durham Tech, backed by a $29 million Bloomberg Philanthropies grant. meetings.executive_summary: At the March 13, 2025 work session, all seven board members and newly seated student representative Kaylin Myers heard emotional public testimony regarding student suicides, anti-bullying enforcement, classified pay compression, and climate action before approving a pulled Consent Agenda and an Arts in Our Schools Month proclamation. disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/13/25
disagreements.issue: Policy 7502 (Salary Administration & Employee Compensation) — Binding Experience Raises, Pay Schedule Merging, and Supplement Equity
disagreements.summary: During the 53-minute second reading of Policy 7502, board members disagreed over whether policy text stating 'intent of the board' creates an unsustainable fiscal promise on annual experience steps, how Crutchfield and HIL pay scales should be reconciled, and how to ensure parity between Arts and Extra-Duty supplements.
disagreements.side_a_position: Embed explicit policy commitments protecting annual experience-step progression, preventing arbitrary min/max placement penalties, and guaranteeing equitable treatment of Arts and extra-duty supplements.
side_a_arguments: Employees and union advocates (DAE/Christy Clen) have repeatedly cited classified pay compression and past pay-schedule discrepancies.
Without clear 'intent of the board' and supplement-parity language, workers risk losing expected step recognition during schedule transitions.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep Policy 7502 flexible enough not to legally bind future budgets beyond uncertain county and state appropriations while schedules are still being reconciled.
side_b_arguments: Enshrining annual step guarantees inside board policy risks creating unfunded mandates if state or county revenues fall short.
Technical placement rules and supplement structures require careful HR and legal review across both legacy and new compensation frameworks.
disagreements.resolution: No vote taken on second reading; staff and legal counsel were directed to revise Policy 7502 language and return it for further board review.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 3/13/25
disagreements.issue: Equity Impacts of Fee-Based Summer Camps Following ESSER Expiration
disagreements.summary: After pulling Summer Programs from the Consent Agenda, board members questioned shifting three enrichment camps to a fee-based model as ESSER pandemic funds ended, raising access barriers for low-income families.
disagreements.side_a_position: Questioned charging tuition fees for three summer camps and demanded accountability metrics to ensure low-income students are not excluded from summer enrichment.
side_a_arguments: Fee-based programs risk creating a two-tier summer experience when federal ESSER funding expires.
Families without discretionary income rely on DPS summer camps for safe enrichment and academic continuity.
disagreements.side_b_position: Administration and fiscal-minded members noted the district still preserves targeted free academic camps while using fees only to sustain optional enrichment camps without pandemic funding.
side_b_arguments: Ending ESSER grants leaves no dedicated recurring general-fund dollars to subsidize every optional camp.
Targeted academic recovery camps remain free for qualifying students with highest need.
disagreements.resolution: Board directed administration to conduct and report a post-summer demographic, scholarship, and student outcome audit.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/9/25
meetings.executive_summary: In a six-hour January 9, 2025 work session presided over by Designate Natalie Beyer with all seven members present, the board recessed briefly to announce a January 10 snow closure, pulled a STOP Grant contract off Consent for later review, and adopted an updated Consent Agenda (7-0). Although administration withdrew mid-year Magnet Express Stops based on negative feedback from over 500 ThoughtExchange survey respondents and committed to ending rotational busing on January 17, board members sharply debated launching Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs) mid-year—with Wendell Tabb, Joy Harrell-Goff, Emily Chávez, and Jessica Carda-Auten raising safety, neighborhood crime, and driver-input concerns against Millicent Rogers, Bettina Umstead, and Natalie Beyer's insistence on honoring the December 19 commitment. The board also unanimously adopted Policy 7921 (Classified Personnel Reduction), approved the 2025-26 Budget Timeline after withdrawing an amended community-forum motion, joined twice-yearly City-County-Board meetings, and reconvened after closed session at 06:01:42 to pass the personnel report 7-0 and end post-closed-session livestreaming.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda & Minutes Approval, Public Comment, and Snow Closure Recess
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding Designate Natalie Beyer called the meeting to order, and the board adopted the agenda and November 7, 2024 minutes (noting a Zoom correction). Thirteen public speakers addressed solar/climate action plans and criticized Express Stops and FRZs before a brief recess for weather consultation, after which Superintendent Lewis announced DPS schools would close January 10 for snow.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (STOP Grant Removal and Amended Consent Approval)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bettina Umstead moved to defer the STOP Grant update and Lincoln Center contract to January 23 pending answers from Dr. King. The board then unanimously approved the remaining Consent Agenda: Restart reauthorization, contracts over $90,000, Clancy & Theys and Glenn Elementary IT/fiber change orders, and a Duke Energy temporary easement for the new Durham School of the Arts.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Update: Express Stops Withdrawal, FRZs, and Driver Retention Debate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Lewis and Dr. Webb reviewed over 500 ThoughtExchange responses and recommended deferring Express Stops until 2025-26 while ending rotational busing on January 17 using previously approved FRZs and a new Policy 6322 hardship exception form. Board members split sharply during nearly two hours of debate over mid-year safety, hazard exclusions (crime/abandoned buildings), bus-driver qualitative input, and whether reversing December's FRZ approval would undermine trust.

agenda_items.title: Legislative Agenda Planning & Joint City-County-Board of Education Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emily Chávez, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Bettina Umstead volunteered to draft the 2025 legislative brief and organize the delegation breakfast. The board then voted 7-0 to join twice-yearly Joint City-County-DPS meetings (Feb 11 and Aug 12), naming Bettina Umstead as the third voting representative and Wendell Tabb as alternate.

agenda_items.title: Policy 7921 (Classified Personnel Reduction) — Second Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Giovanni presented an overhaul of Policy 7921 drafted with attorney Jonathan Blumberg to align classified reduction-in-force procedures with certified staff. After Vice Chair Carda-Auten asked to specify statutory health-insurance continuation notice in writing, the board approved Policy 7921 7-0 with direction to bring back that technical addition on consent.

agenda_items.title: FY 2025-26 Budget Calendar & Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter outlined the state-dependent budget timeline, proposing an early February 20 public budget hearing ahead of the superintendent's March 27 recommendation and April 24 county request authorization. agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Summary, Closed Session, and Post-Closed-Session Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After summarizing follow-up directives (meeting with the DAE transportation delegation, presenting a driver retention plan, adding a community budget meeting, and revising Policy 7921), the board entered closed session at 03:52:52. Reconvening at 06:01:42, the board passed the January 9, 2025 Personnel Report 7-0 and reached consensus to cease livestreaming post-closed-session personnel votes starting in two weeks.

votes.item_title: Approve January 9, 2025 Work Session Agenda
votes.notes: All seven seated members present.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/9/25
disagreements.issue: Mid-Year Implementation of Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs), Safety Criteria, and Bus Driver Retention
disagreements.summary: Although staff withdrew mid-year Express Stops to end rotational busing on January 17, the board divided sharply over whether to proceed immediately with December 19-approved FRZs given safety, equity, attendance-data, and bus-driver concerns.
disagreements.side_a_position: Questioned or regretted launching FRZs mid-year in January, arguing neighborhood hazards, bus-driver insights, attendance comparisons, and accessible Policy 6322 hardship exceptions were insufficiently developed.
side_a_arguments: Wendell Tabb and Jessica Carda-Auten warned that excluding neighborhood crime, loitering, abandoned buildings, and loose dogs from hazard criteria leaves students unsafe on routes adults would not walk.

Joy Harrell-Goff stated her position flipped since December after meeting with veteran bus drivers, arguing switching from rotational coverage to mid-year FRZs trades one harmful Band-Aid for another without qualitative driver input.

Emily Chávez demanded direct engagement with the DAE transportation delegation, an inventory of community carpool/nonprofit resources at each school, and an immediate meeting focused on driver retention.
disagreements.side_b_position: Urged moving forward on January 17 with the December 19 decision to end exhausting rotational busing while relying on principal collaboration and the case-by-case Policy 6322 hardship appeal process.
side_b_arguments: Reversing course days before January 17 would undermine trust with overworked transportation staff and leave thousands of families who have already made arrangements scrambling.
Bus drivers have been working two to three extra routes past 6:00 PM under rotational coverage; ending rotational routes provides immediate relief while data on FRZs can be monitored and adjusted.
disagreements.resolution: No motion was introduced to rescind December's FRZ approval, allowing staff to end rotational busing and launch FRZs on January 17 while directing administration to meet with the DAE driver delegation and bring a driver retention plan to the January 23 meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 1/9/25
disagreements.issue: Mandating Timing and Off-Site Format for a Budget 101 Community Forum in the 2025-26 Budget Calendar
disagreements.summary: Board members differed over whether to amend the formal 2025-26 budget calendar motion to lock in a pre-hearing Budget 101 community meeting at high school venues or pass the statutory deadline schedule cleanly.
disagreements.side_a_position: Pushed to embed an accessible Budget 101 community education meeting outside the Fuller Building—before Feb 20 (Chávez/Carda-Auten) or between Feb 20 and Mar 27 (Harrell-Goff)—so residents understand federal/state/local revenues before testifying.
side_a_arguments: Traditional hearings at Fuller Building draw low turnout because families lack accessible background on how school budgets work and cannot easily attend downtown board nights.
Providing infographics and plain-language budget briefings at Southern or Jordan High Schools prior to public hearings leads to more equitable community input.
disagreements.side_b_position: Argued the calendar vote only sets formal Policy 8100 benchmark deadlines and does not require voting on logistics or dates for supplemental community sessions.
side_b_arguments: Adding binding event logistics into the statutory budget calendar motion risked locking staff into unvetted dates and venues.
Supplemental community briefings can be directed operationally without amending the formal deadline calendar.
disagreements.resolution: Rogers withdrew her amended motion at 03:50:04, and the board passed a clean motion approving the benchmark budget timeline (7-0) while recording a formal staff follow-up directive to schedule a community budget meeting.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 1/6/25
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten with a four-member quorum (Carda-Auten, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Joy Harrell-Goff), the January 6, 2025 special called meeting examined administration's rollout plan for Family Responsibility Zones (21 elementary schools, adjusted at five sites after principal feedback) and Secondary Magnet Express Stops (serving DSA, Rogers-Herr, and Creative Studies). Staff shared preliminary ThoughtExchange survey results from 417 participants revealing intense parent opposition citing equity harms to working families, dark early-morning wait times (7:15-7:45 AM), lack of adult supervision at Express Stops, and mid-year disruption. During nearly two hours of questioning (interrupted by a 15-minute IT recess), Emily Chávez, Joy Harrell-Goff, and Jessica Carda-Auten clashed with staff and Natalie Beyer over Policy 6322 hardship exception authority and whether Express Stops and FRZs could be implemented equitably mid-year without formal action.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten convened the special called meeting with four members present (Carda-Auten, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Joy Harrell-Goff). The board approved the single-topic agenda 4-0 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Plan Implementation Briefing and Preliminary ThoughtExchange Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Webb, Matthew Palmer (remote), and Annie Fulwood presented implementation details for Family Responsibility Zones across 21 elementary schools (0.25-0.5 miles expanding up to 1 mile, with five sites adjusted after principal input), Secondary Magnet Express Stops at DSA, Rogers-Herr, and Creative Studies during a 7:15-7:45 AM window, route optimization covering 19,500 riders, and initial ThoughtExchange feedback from 417 respondents highlighting equity, safety, and working-parent burdens.

agenda_items.title: Board Q&A on Policy 6322 Hardship Exceptions, Express Stops, and Walkability
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members questioned staff at length (including a technical recess from 01:01:43 to 01:16:28) regarding who approves hardship bus requests under Policy 6322, supervision and darkness at Express Stops, elementary walk-zone hazards, and how DPS compares with Wake, Mecklenburg, and Guilford districts before adjourning at 02:09:45 with no vote taken.

votes.notes: Four-member quorum present (Jessica Carda-Auten, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, Joy Harrell-Goff); three board seats absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten called the January 6, 2025 special called transportation work session to order at 00:03:11 with four board members present—Carda-Auten, Natalie Beyer, Emily Chávez, and Joy Harrell-Goff—constituting a legal quorum. Natalie Beyer moved to approve the agenda as presented, and Emily Chávez seconded. No changes were proposed to the single-item transportation agenda. All four members present voted Aye by voice vote at 00:04:07 before turning immediately to Dr. Webb's operational briefing.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 1/6/25
disagreements.issue: Policy 6322 FRZ Hardship Exception Standards and Mid-Year Secondary Magnet Express Stops
disagreements.summary: During the special called review, board members split between demanding stricter equity safeguards, accessible hardship waivers, and delays on Express Stops versus empowering staff to deploy standard peer-district transit tools immediately to end rotational busing.
disagreements.side_a_position: Pressed for clear, accessible Policy 6322 hardship exemptions and raised severe equity and safety objections to unsupervised early-morning Express Stops and mid-year walk zones.
side_a_arguments: Emily Chávez and Joy Harrell-Goff warned that 7:15-7:45 AM Express Stops without guaranteed supervision or walkable infrastructure create safety risks in winter darkness and disproportionately burden single and low-income working parents.

Jessica Carda-Auten, Chávez, and Harrell-Goff insisted families facing extreme transportation hardship need a transparent, navigable administrative approval path rather than punitive barriers—even as Dr. Nicholas King cautioned against placing principals in the position of overriding board policy.
disagreements.side_b_position: Supported giving staff operational latitude to implement Express Stops and 1-mile FRZs consistent with large North Carolina peer districts.
side_b_arguments: Natalie Beyer noted that Wake, Charlotte-Mecklenburg, and Guilford school systems already utilize 1.5-mile walk zones and magnet Express Stops to manage driver shortages.
Continuing rotational bus cancellations harms families unpredictably, so staff need board backing to execute structural routing reforms.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; intense board and ThoughtExchange pushback led administration to return on January 9 with a revised plan deferring Express Stops to 2025-26 and drafting a formal Policy 6322 hardship exception form.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
meetings.executive_summary: The Board of Education navigated a contentious nearly seven-hour meeting dominated by the ongoing school bus driver shortage, a 43-speaker public comment period from bus drivers, DAE members, and parents, and Phase 2 transportation proposals. The board voted 6-1 to adopt modified Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs) affecting roughly 864 riders within one mile of elementary schools, rejected an immediate mid-year rollout of Express Bus Stops in a 3-3 tie (with Wendell Tabb absent), and then voted 4-2 to authorize planning for Express Stops to end rotational bus coverage in January 2025. The board also declined governance training RFP proposals, approved Policy 7921 on first reading, authorized purchasing 1,500 Chromebooks ($700,000), and approved the December personnel report and a special education placement agreement.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers called the meeting to order with Emily Chávez participating virtually and led a moment of silence. Staff and board members recognized Student of the Month Shaimie Castro Romero (DPLC Holton), Distinguished Alum Soni Gas Osaji, November Employee of the Month Dr. Sanders Beckwith (Hillside IB), December Teacher of the Month Naima Brooks (Hillandale), and Spark Pin recipient Freddie Rogers (retiring after 60 years of NC service and 24 years with DPS).

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis recognized retiring Deputy Superintendent Dr. Alvera Lesane, celebrated 5,000 food bags from the Bull City Food Drive and a $363,187 Duke Energy rebate, and praised bus drivers. He outlined his Meet and Confer philosophy—supporting dialogue with DAE while advocating inclusion of non-union classified employees—and noted ongoing FY24 audit priorities alongside the NC General Assembly's $463.5 million private school voucher override.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of November 21, 2024 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed and approved the December 19 meeting agenda and the November 21, 2024 meeting minutes by roll call vote with no modifications.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Forty-three speakers addressed the board under a one-minute time limit covering Hope Valley walk-zone safety, Northern High School athletic fields, and Montessori classroom conditions. Bus drivers presented a five-point petition urging retention of supervisors behind the wheel, route efficiency, bonus incentives, transparent extra-duty rotation, and school bathroom access while opposing four-day rotations, while social workers, therapists, and DAE/labor leaders pressed for Master's pay parity and adherence to the board's September Meet and Confer directive.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board adopted the December 19 consent agenda without discussion or pulled items.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Update and Phase 2 Recommendations (FRZs and Express Stops)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: COO Dr. Larry Webb, Matthew Palmer, and Transportation Director Joe Harris reported that rotational coverage covered 100% of routes December 2-13 (averaging 21 daily driver absences against a 25-driver threshold), with 143 drivers on payroll and 160 candidates in the CDL pipeline. Staff proposed Phase 2 measures—modified <=1-mile Family Responsibility Zones (~864 riders, saving ~20 routes) and Express Bus Stops for School for Creative Studies, Rogers-Herr, and DSA (saving ~8 routes)—prompting extensive debate over safety, crossing guards, lost instructional time, and Policy 1740/4010 grievance clarity.
agenda_items.vote_summary: FRZs approved 6-1; immediate Express Stops failed 3-3; Express Stop planning for Jan 2025 approved 4-2

agenda_items.title: RFP for Board Governance Training and Agenda Amendment (Item 5B)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a recess and Wendell Tabb's departure, the board voted to decline all vendor proposals received under the board governance training RFP. Members also amended the agenda to defer Academic Services Item 5B (Strategic Plan Priority 3 Update) to the January 9, 2025 work session.

agenda_items.title: Policy 7921: Classified Personnel Reduction (First Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Legal Officer Dr. Tanya Giovanni presented Policy 7921 on first reading, noting administration withdrew its request to waive a second reading so the policy could return on January 9, 2025. Board members noted track changes were missing from BoardDocs and asked staff to provide clear redlines before final adoption.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Chromebook Sustainability and Replacement Purchase
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT Director Paul Mbimi reported that DPS manages over 31,300 active Chromebooks with roughly 2,000 missing/unaccounted devices (~$2.3 million cumulative loss) and 7,530 repairs in 2023-24. He proposed purchasing 1,500 replacement devices via PRC 015 (~$700,000) and exploring future strategies including Tech Champion stipends ($50,000 in 2025-26), in-school device models, and optional technology fee frameworks.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Personnel Report, and Special Education Placement Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session at 05:42:55 with six members present. Returning to open session at 06:56:55 with five members present (Wendell Tabb and Emily Chávez absent), the board approved the December 19 personnel report, added an exceptional children item to the agenda, and approved a placement agreement with the American School for the Deaf before adjourning at 06:58:29.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session 6-0; Personnel Report 5-0; Agenda addition & EC placement 5-0

votes.item_title: Approval of December 19, 2024 Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Emily Chávez participated remotely.
votes.discussion_detail: Following Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's update, Chair Millicent Rogers called for a motion to adopt the December 19, 2024 meeting agenda. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the agenda as presented, and Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten seconded the motion. Because Emily Chávez was participating virtually, all formal open-session votes during this portion of the meeting were conducted via roll call. With no amendments or discussion proposed at that point, all seven seated board members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 21, 2024 Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: The board reviewed the draft minutes from the November 21, 2024 monthly board meeting. Natalie Beyer moved to approve the minutes as submitted, and Emily Chávez seconded the motion. No edits or corrections were requested by board members. On a roll call vote conducted by Chair Millicent Rogers, all seven board members voted in favor.

votes.item_title: Adopt Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs) Transportation Plan
votes.notes: Establishes modified <=1-mile walk/family responsibility zones around eligible elementary schools affecting approximately 864 riders and freeing roughly 20 bus routes.
votes.discussion_detail: Transportation leaders Dr. Larry Webb, Matthew Palmer, and Joe Harris presented Phase 2 options to eliminate rotational bus cancellations, proposing modified Family Responsibility Zones (<=1 mile at 21 elementary schools, excluding hazard crossings) affecting ~864 riders and saving ~20 routes. Public commenters and several board members raised concerns about winter weather, crossing guards, pedestrian safety at Hope Valley and other campuses, driver bathroom access, and family hardship opt-out mechanisms under Policy 1740/4010. Staff noted hardship accommodations and walking/carpool support plans, while arguing FRZs were necessary to stabilize daily service and address a chronic driver shortage. Bettina Umstead voted Nay due to concerns over mid-year disruption, safety, and insufficient family support infrastructure, while the other six board members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Implement Express Bus Stops for School for Creative Studies, Durham School of the Arts, and Rogers-Herr
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb absent for vote; tie vote failed.
votes.discussion_detail: Transportation staff proposed converting bus service at School for Creative Studies (SCS), Durham School of the Arts (DSA), and Rogers-Herr Middle School to regional Express Stops to save approximately eight bus routes needed to end rotational coverage. Natalie Beyer, seconded by Emily Chávez, moved to implement Express Stops immediately for those three magnet/specialty campuses rather than waiting until 2025-26. Opponents including Bettina Umstead, Jessica Carda-Auten, and Chair Millicent Rogers expressed concern about imposing major routing changes mid-year without detailed hub site logistics, student weather shelter, family outreach, and clear hardship appeals. With Wendell Tabb having stepped out/left the meeting, the roll call ended in a 3-3 tie, causing the motion to fail.

votes.item_title: Authorize Administration to Plan Express Stop Service to End Rotational Coverage in January 2025 and Return January 9 with Details
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb absent for vote.
votes.discussion_detail: After the 3-3 tie on immediate Express Stop implementation, board members debated how to give families relief from rotational bus cancellations without forcing an unvetted rollout before winter break. Natalie Beyer initially floated planning Express Stops for 2025-26 with Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten's second, then revised the motion—seconded by Emily Chávez—to authorize administration to prepare Express Stop plans aimed at ending rotational coverage in January 2025 and bring back detailed operational plans, community notification timelines, and clear Policy 1740/4010 grievance/support procedures at the January 9, 2025 work session. Carda-Auten joined Beyer, Chávez, and Joy Harrell-Goff in supporting the planning-first directive, while Bettina Umstead and Chair Millicent Rogers maintained their opposition to mid-year Express Stops, passing the motion 4-2 with Wendell Tabb absent.

votes.item_title: Decline Vendor Proposals for Board Governance Training RFP
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb absent for remainder of meeting after transportation votes.
votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening after a recess, the board considered proposals received in response to an RFP for board governance training. Natalie Beyer moved that the board decline to move forward with any of the governance training vendor proposals at this time, and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. No board member objected or argued in favor of contracting with the submitting vendors. With Wendell Tabb absent, the six remaining members voted unanimously 6-0 on roll call to reject the proposals.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Defer Academic Services Item 5B to January 9, 2025
votes.notes: Deferred Strategic Plan Priority 3 Update due to meeting length.
votes.discussion_detail: Given that the meeting had already passed the five-hour mark following the lengthy transportation debate, Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved to amend the agenda to remove Academic Services Item 5B (Strategic Plan Priority 3 Update) and place it on the January 9, 2025 work session agenda. Emily Chávez seconded the motion. Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis and staff expressed no objection to postponing the update. On roll call with Wendell Tabb absent, all six members present voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Approve Policy 7921 (Classified Personnel Reduction) on First Reading
votes.notes: Administration withdrew request to waive second reading; scheduled for second reading on January 9, 2025 with tracked changes posted.
votes.discussion_detail: Chief Legal Officer Dr. Tanya Giovanni presented revisions to Policy 7921 governing reductions in force for classified personnel, noting that administration was withdrawing its request to waive a second reading so the policy could undergo full two-reading review. Board members pointed out that the track-changes version was missing from the BoardDocs packet and asked staff to ensure marked edits were posted prior to final consideration. Natalie Beyer moved to approve Policy 7921 on first reading and return it for second reading on January 9, 2025, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff. The motion passed 6-0 on roll call with Wendell Tabb absent.

votes.item_title: Authorize Purchase of Approximately 1,500 Replacement Chromebooks via PRC 015
votes.notes: Funded at approximately $700,000 through state PRC 015 technology funds; future device sustainability options (Tech Champion stipends, in-school models, device fees) deferred for later review.
votes.discussion_detail: IT Director Paul Mbimi outlined severe student device attrition—reporting over 31,300 active Chromebooks alongside ~2,000 missing devices representing $2.3 million in cumulative losses and 7,530 repairs during 2023-24—and requested authorization to buy roughly 1,500 replacement Chromebooks using $700,000 in state PRC 015 funding. Board members questioned device accountability protocols, equity concerns surrounding potential parent technology fees, and whether school-based cart models or higher Tech Champion stipends ($50,000 projected for 2025-26) could reduce loss rates. Members stressed that approving the immediate purchase did not endorse adopting technology fees yet. Emily Chávez moved approval of the ~1,500 Chromebook purchase via PRC 015, Natalie Beyer seconded, and the motion passed 6-0 on roll call with Wendell Tabb absent.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb absent.
votes.discussion_detail: At 05:42:55, Bettina Umstead moved to enter closed session for the statutory purposes stated on the meeting agenda, and Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. No discussion occurred prior to the vote. With Wendell Tabb absent, the six remaining members voted unanimously 6-0 on roll call to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve Personnel Report Dated December 19, 2024
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb and Emily Chávez absent following closed session.
votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning to open session at 06:56:55 with five members present (Wendell Tabb and Emily Chávez absent), Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis requested board action on the December 19, 2024 personnel report. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the personnel report, and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. With no open-session discussion, the remaining five board members approved the report 5-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Add Special Education Placement Agreement
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb and Emily Chávez absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the personnel report, Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved to amend the open-session agenda to add an out-of-district special education placement agreement discussed in closed session. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. Without objection, the five board members present voted 5-0 by voice vote to add the item.

votes.item_title: Approve Special Education Placement Agreement with American School for the Deaf
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb and Emily Chávez absent; meeting adjourned at 06:58:29.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the agenda addition, Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved approval of the special education placement agreement with the American School for the Deaf. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. The five members present approved the placement agreement 5-0 by voice vote, after which Chair Millicent Rogers adjourned the meeting at 06:58:29.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
disagreements.issue: Adoption of Family Responsibility Zones (FRZs) Around Elementary Schools
disagreements.summary: Board members split 6-1 over implementing modified <=1-mile Family Responsibility Zones affecting roughly 864 riders in January 2025 to free up ~20 bus routes and end rotational cancellations.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt FRZs now with hazard exclusions and family support protocols to stabilize systemwide bus service.
side_a_arguments: Frees roughly 20 routes to eliminate unpredictable rotational bus cancellations.
Walk zones exclude roads >=35 mph without enhanced crossings and retain EC/McKinney-Vento service.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not implement FRZs mid-year due to child safety, winter weather, and family hardship concerns.
side_b_arguments: Parents raised urgent concerns about crossing guards, winter coats, and unwalkable routes near schools like Hope Valley.
Policy 1740/4010 hardship exemptions and family-support logistics were not yet clear enough before implementation.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 6-1 to adopt FRZs.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
disagreements.issue: Immediate Rollout vs. Operational Planning for Magnet/Specialty Express Bus Stops
disagreements.summary: The board deadlocked 3-3 on implementing Express Stops immediately for School for Creative Studies, DSA, and Rogers-Herr before voting 4-2 to authorize planning for January 2025 implementation pending a January 9 operational review.
disagreements.side_a_position: Move immediately or prepare directly for January 2025 Express Stops to end rotational bus coverage.
side_a_arguments: Express Stops save ~8 routes primarily serving secondary magnet students who are older than elementary FRZ riders.
Ending four-day rotational cancellations is urgent for working families and drivers alike.
disagreements.side_b_position: Reject mid-year implementation of Express Stops without advance notice, hub logistics, and transparent appeals.
side_b_arguments: Implementing Express Stops mid-year with minimal notice disrupts families who selected magnet schools relying on bus access.
Hub locations, supervision, weather shelter, and Policy 1740/4010 grievance details had not been finalized.
disagreements.resolution: Immediate implementation failed 3-3; Jessica Carda-Auten joined the majority in a 4-2 vote authorizing Express Stop planning to end rotational coverage in January 2025 with detailed plans due January 9.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 12/19/24
disagreements.issue: Scope of Meet and Confer Policy and Inclusion of Non-Union Staff
disagreements.summary: Public commenters from DAE and supporting labor unions clashed with Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's update advocating non-union worker representation alongside DAE in Meet and Confer drafts.
disagreements.side_a_position: Include mechanisms for non-union classified and staff voices alongside DAE in administration's Meet and Confer draft.
side_a_arguments: Roughly 30-40% of workers or non-union employees still deserve structured representation in workplace discussions.
Administration must ensure compliance with North Carolina law while fostering inclusive communication.
disagreements.side_b_position: Honor the board's September 26 directive establishing Meet and Confer with an ERO meeting the 50% threshold (DAE).
side_b_arguments: Labor leaders argued administration's counter-draft undermined democratic worker representation and the board's 4-3 September vote.
Employees repeatedly cited broken trust between cabinet leadership and frontline classified/certified staff.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken on Meet and Confer on December 19.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/21/24
meetings.executive_summary: Conducted inside the Fuller Building amid a rolling power outage that darkened lights, disabled HVAC, and temporarily knocked out Spanish interpretation, the board initially removed non-urgent items from its agenda before voting 6-1 to restore the Local Master's Pay budget impact item after interpretation returned and social workers testified. Transportation leadership presented Phase 1 rotational coverage beginning December 2 (holding back 25 routes/day so most families receive four days of service per week while maintaining 100% EC coverage). On Master's pay, after rejecting a 2-5 motion to table an immediate expansion mandate, the board voted 7-0 to amend and 6-1 to pass a compromise directing the Superintendent to bring a funded plan on December 2 covering certified teachers and instructional staff—including school social workers, specialists, coaches, and coordinators—retroactively for 2024-25.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Amendment During Power Outage & Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because a rolling power outage at the Fuller Building cut building HVAC, lighting, and interpretation services at the start of the meeting, the board voted to remove non-urgent items (including Consent Item D, DPS Foundation Report, Academic Services 4A-C, and Operation Services 5/Master's pay) for rescheduling to December 2, and approved the October 24, 2024 minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Sunrise Durham climate youth, Lakewood/Brogden/Creekside families decrying chronic bus cancellations (citing 53 cancellations and 24 delays on Bus 235) and opposing walk zones, ~8 school social workers and DAE members demanding Master's pay parity after receiving conflicting HR eligibility emails, David Price supporting naming a facility for Bill Bell, and Highland Electric Fleets warning on EV bus grant rules. Spanish interpretation was restored at 00:12:46.

agenda_items.title: Reconsideration of Local Master's Pay Agenda Item & Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Once interpretation was restored and social workers spoke during public comment, the board voted 6-1 to reconsider removing the Master's pay budget update and 7-0 to restore it after Transportation. Members also adopted Consent Agenda Items A, B, C, E, and F unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Phase 1 Rotational Coverage Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: COO Dr. Larry Webb, Matthew Palmer, Tammy Phillips, and Sheena Cooper introduced Phase 1 rotational coverage from December 2 through December 20, holding back 25 routes daily so general-education routes receive four days of service and one pre-announced alternating uncovered day while keeping Exceptional Children buses at 100% coverage. Student services outlined a new bus-cancellation absence code, and the board gave informal consensus to track school- and demographic-disaggregated lost instructional time.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Consensus direction on instructional time tracking

agenda_items.title: Local Master's Pay Budget Impact and Expansion Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Jeremy Teeter and HR reported that 358 classroom teachers qualified for Master's pay ($2.517M actual vs. $1.259M budgeted—a $1.258M shortfall covered by withholding 15% of local department budgets), and adding non-teaching certified roles such as social workers and coaches would cost at least $272,000 more while the FY24 audit remained incomplete. Following sharp debate, a tabling motion failed 2-5, and the board voted 7-0 to amend and 6-1 to direct administration to present a funded plan on December 2 covering pre-2013 DPI certified teachers and instructional staff with 2024-25 back pay.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Tabling failed 2-5; Amendment passed 7-0; Main motion as amended passed 6-1

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and November 21, 2024 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session at 03:52:21 on a unanimous voice vote. Returning to open session at 04:25:46, the board approved the November 21, 2024 personnel report as amended and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Remove Non-Urgent Items Due to Power Outage
votes.notes: Removed Consent Item D (Superintendent Evaluation Tool), Item 3 (DPS Foundation Report), Academic Services 4A-C, and Operation Services 5 (Master's pay budget impact & change orders), targeting Dec 2 rescheduling.
votes.discussion_detail: Opening the meeting amid a power outage that left the Fuller Building without air conditioning, full lighting, or working Spanish interpretation, Chair Millicent Rogers asked the board to streamline the agenda to essential items. Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved to remove Consent Item D, the DPS Foundation Report, Academic Services 4A-C, and Operation Services Item 5 (which included the Master's pay budget impact update and monthly change orders) and reschedule most items to December 2. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. All seven board members voted Aye by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 24, 2024 Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: The board reviewed the draft minutes from its October 24, 2024 meeting immediately after amending the agenda. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the minutes as presented, and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. Hearing no corrections or objections, Chair Millicent Rogers called for a voice vote, and the minutes passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Reconsider Removal of Local Master's Pay Budget Impact Item from Agenda
votes.notes: Followed restoration of Spanish interpretation at 00:12:46 and extensive public comment by social workers and DAE members.
votes.discussion_detail: After Spanish interpretation was restored and nearly an hour of public comment featured school social workers and DAE members urging immediate action on Master's pay parity, Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved to reconsider removing the Local Master's Pay budget impact item from the agenda. Emily Chávez seconded the motion, noting that members of the public had waited specifically to hear the financial breakdown. Natalie Beyer opposed reopening the agenda, arguing the item was originally informational and that the building remained dark without air conditioning. Six members voted Aye and Beyer voted Nay, passing reconsideration 6-1.

votes.item_title: Restore Local Master's Pay Budget Impact to Agenda Following Transportation Update
votes.discussion_detail: Once the board voted to reconsider removal of the Master's pay item, Natalie Beyer moved to place the Local Master's Pay budget impact item back onto the agenda directly following the Transportation update. Emily Chávez seconded the placement motion. With the schedule now settled, all seven board members voted Aye on voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Table Master's Pay Expansion Motion Pending Budget and Audit Clarity
votes.notes: Sought to postpone Emily Chávez's motion mandating Master's pay expansion for 2024-25 until finance staff could identify funding amid an existing $1.258M shortfall and incomplete FY24 audit.
votes.discussion_detail: CFO Jeremy Teeter reported that 358 classroom teachers receiving Master's pay cost $2.517 million against a $1.259 million budget—creating a $1.258 million shortfall covered by withholding 15% of local department budgets—while adding social workers and other certified instructional staff would cost at least $272,000 more amid an incomplete FY24 audit. Emily Chávez moved (seconded by Wendell Tabb) to grant Master's pay per pre-2013 DPI standards for 2024-25 with back pay for certified teachers and instructional staff including social workers, instructional coaches, specialists, and coordinators. Bettina Umstead moved to table that motion until finance staff identified viable funding sources, seconded by Natalie Beyer, warning against unfunded commitments. Five board members voted Nay and only Umstead and Beyer voted Aye, defeating the tabling motion 2-5.

votes.item_title: Amend Compromise Directive to Specify Pre-2013 DPI Certified Instructional Staff and 2024-25 Back Pay Plan for December 2
votes.notes: Followed attorney guidance that Chávez's earlier motion had reached its amendment limit and Wendell Tabb's appeal for compromise.
votes.discussion_detail: After legal counsel noted that Emily Chávez's original motion had reached the parliamentary limit of two amendments and Wendell Tabb urged board unity, Natalie Beyer introduced a new compromise motion (seconded by Bettina Umstead) directing the Superintendent to bring Master's pay budgetary solutions to the December 2 meeting. Emily Chávez moved an amendment, seconded by Umstead, specifying that the December 2 plan cover paying everyone on the certified teacher and certified instructional pay scales who would have qualified under pre-2013 DPI guidelines—including instructional specialists, instructional coaches, coordinators, and school social workers—for the 2024-25 school year including back pay. Board members embraced the clear scope for financial modeling, passing the amendment 7-0.

votes.item_title: Direct Superintendent to Bring Comprehensive Budgetary Plan for Expanding 2024-25 Master's Pay to December 2 Special Meeting
votes.notes: Compromise motion replaced the prior pending motion without voting on the prior motion directly.
votes.discussion_detail: Following unanimous adoption of Emily Chávez's clarifying amendment, the board voted on Natalie Beyer's amended main motion directing the Superintendent to bring back concrete funding options and budget implications on December 2 for expanding 2024-25 Master's pay with back pay to all eligible pre-2013 DPI certified teachers and instructional staff. The motion bridged the divide between members insisting on immediate fulfillment of spring expectations and those demanding verified budget offsets before authorizing expenditures. The main motion as amended passed 6-1 on an unrecorded voice vote.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: After concluding the Master's pay debate at 03:52:21, Bettina Umstead moved that the board enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. All seven board members voted Aye by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Personnel Report Dated November 21, 2024 as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Returning to open session at 04:25:46, the board took action on the November 21, 2024 personnel report as amended in closed session. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the amended personnel report, and Emily Chávez seconded the motion. All seven board members voted Aye on voice vote before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/21/24
disagreements.issue: Reconsidering Removal of Master's Pay Item During Fuller Building Power Outage
disagreements.summary: Board members split 6-1 over whether to add the Local Master's Pay update back onto the agenda after building conditions stabilized enough to restore interpretation.
disagreements.side_a_position: Restore the Master's Pay budget update immediately so employees waiting in the room hear the fiscal report.
side_a_arguments: Spanish interpretation was restored at 00:12:46, removing the primary barrier cited for postponement.
School social workers and DAE members turned out in force during public comment specifically for Master's pay accountability.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep the item deferred to December 2 due to the building outage and its informational status.
side_b_arguments: The Fuller Building remained without lights and air conditioning.
The item was originally scheduled as informational without a scheduled vote.
disagreements.resolution: Reconsideration passed 6-1, and the board voted 7-0 to place the item after Transportation.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 11/21/24
disagreements.issue: Expanding 2024-25 Local Master's Pay to Certified Instructional Support Staff Amid Existing Budget Shortfall
disagreements.summary: Following revelation of a $1.258M shortfall on classroom-teacher Master's pay and an incomplete FY24 audit, board members clashed over voting immediately to grant Master's pay with back pay to social workers and instructional staff versus requiring a funded budget plan first.
disagreements.side_a_position: Direct immediate equity and 2024-25 Master's pay coverage for all pre-2013 DPI certified teachers and instructional staff (including social workers, coaches, specialists, and coordinators).
side_a_arguments: Spring 2024 board messaging promised 'teachers' Master's pay under state rules, and social workers were sent conflicting confirmation and retraction emails.
Withholding Master's pay from non-classroom certified staff who serve high-need students harms morale and retention.
disagreements.side_b_position: Table or defer any binding commitment until CFO Jeremy Teeter identifies funding offsets and completes FY24 audit clarity.
side_b_arguments: Classroom teacher Master's pay alone is already $1.258M over budget ($2.517M vs $1.259M), requiring 15% department budget holds.
Expanding to additional roles adds at least $272k+ and an unknown liability without verified local revenue.
disagreements.resolution: A tabling motion failed 2-5, after which the board adopted a 7-0 amended compromise motion (passed 6-1) directing administration to present a funded plan for full pre-2013 DPI coverage with 2024-25 back pay at a December 2 special meeting.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Joint Quarterly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham County Board of County Commissioners held their Joint Quarterly Meeting on November 13, 2024, presided over by Chair Millicent Rogers, welcoming newly appointed County Manager Claudia Hager and new DPS Chief Operating Officer Dr. Larry Webb and Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Teeter. Both boards unanimously approved the agenda, amended and approved the August 6, 2024 joint minutes to clarify superintendent titles, and adopted an amended 2025 joint meeting calendar moving the November 2025 session to November 12 to avoid a state school board conference conflict. Operational Services staff presented a comprehensive update on universal Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) school meals, student-driven menus, and $13 million in deferred school nutrition kitchen infrastructure needs alongside $1.6 million earmarked in FY 2024-25 operational capital outlay. Commissioners and board members also reviewed enrollment forecasts, Dr. Anthony Lewis's first four months as superintendent, staff compensation implementation, Alliance mental health funding, and teacher housing before closing without public comment as county commissioners neared loss of quorum.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome to County Manager Claudia Hager, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The joint quarterly session of the BOCC and DPS Board of Education was called to order, and Board members welcomed newly appointed County Manager Claudia Hager. Commissioner Jacobs moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the meeting agenda.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 6, 2024 Joint Meeting Minutes and Capital Planning Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members discussed follow-up items from the August 6 minutes, including a pending Durham Pre-K agreement update and coordination with city and county planning departments on adequate school facilities and growth tracking ahead of a February capital planning update. An amendment was approved to clarify Dr. Anthony Lewis as incoming superintendent and Kathy Moore as interim superintendent in the August 6 minutes before approving the minutes as amended.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amendment and amended minutes passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Introduction of DPS Chief Operating Officer Dr. Larry Webb and Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Teeter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Anthony Lewis introduced two key cabinet hires: Dr. Larry Webb as Chief Operating Officer effective November 18 (joining from Franklin County) and Jeremy Teeter, MBA, as Chief Financial Officer effective November 4.

agenda_items.title: Approval of 2025 BOCC/BOE Joint Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board member Jessica Carda-Auten flagged a conflict between the proposed November 18, 2025 joint meeting date and the North Carolina School Boards Association conference. Members agreed to shift the November 2025 joint meeting to Wednesday, November 12 and approved the calendar as amended.

agenda_items.title: Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) Meal Participation Update and Kitchen Infrastructure Needs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matthew Palmer and nutrition leadership reported on student-led scratch cooking and DPS becoming the largest North Carolina district to implement universal CEP free breakfast and lunch effective July 1, budgeting conservatively for a 14% lunch participation increase. Officials detailed $13 million in deferred kitchen infrastructure needs and $1.6 million earmarked in FY 2024-25 operational capital outlay, while commissioners questioned whether to pursue a public-private partnership central kitchen feasibility study versus prioritizing repairs to existing school kitchens.

agenda_items.title: District Enrollment Forecast, Superintendent Entry Update, Budget Implementation, and Mental Health
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff shared Pre-K through high school enrollment growth and capacity forecasts, and Dr. Lewis reflected on entering his fourth month as superintendent. Commissioners and board members requested follow-up reporting on FY 2024-25 certified, classified, and Master's pay budget implementation, discussed Alliance mental health funding and teacher housing, and deferred the Durham Pre-K MOA until staff prepares materials for a future joint meeting.

votes.item_title: Approve Joint Quarterly Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; individual BOE roll call not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Following welcoming remarks for County Manager Claudia Hager, Commissioner Jacobs moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the November 13, 2024 joint quarterly meeting agenda. No objections were raised and the voice vote carried unanimously.

votes.item_title: Amend August 6, 2024 Minutes to Clarify Superintendent Titles
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; individual BOE roll call not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: During discussion of the August 6, 2024 joint meeting minutes, a board member requested clarifying edits to distinguish Dr. Anthony Lewis as incoming superintendent and Kathy Moore as interim superintendent for historical clarity. Commissioner Jacobs moved the revision and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded; the amendment passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve August 6, 2024 Joint Meeting Minutes as Amended
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; original main motion moved at 00:13:48 by Joy Harrell-Goff and seconded by Commissioner Jacobs.
votes.discussion_detail: After adopting the title-clarification amendment and discussing upcoming February capital planning updates with county and city planning staff, the joint bodies voted unanimously by voice vote to approve the August 6, 2024 minutes as amended.

votes.item_title: Approve 2025 BOCC/BOE Joint Meeting Calendar as Amended (Moving November Meeting to Nov. 12)
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; individual BOE roll call not taken.
votes.discussion_detail: Following an initial motion by Commissioner Jacobs seconded by Natalie Beyer to approve the 2025 joint meeting calendar, Jessica Carda-Auten identified a conflict between November 18, 2025 and the state school board association conference. Commissioner Jacobs moved to amend the calendar to move the November 2025 meeting to Wednesday, November 12, seconded by Emily Chávez (with Natalie Beyer concurring), and the amended calendar passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/7/24
meetings.executive_summary: With Natalie Beyer absent, the six-member board held a 6.5-hour work session focused on the superintendent evaluation framework, facility naming policy, the bus driver crisis, and Master's pay disparities. The board unanimously directed staff to return proposals for an anonymous 360 evaluation survey with optional comments, and advanced revisions to Policy 9300 to eliminate the requirement that an honoree be deceased five years before an entire facility can be named after them. After extensive debate over six transportation triage tactics—including Wendell Tabb's opposition to walk zones and rotational coverage in favor of church buses/contracting, and board equity/safety concerns—members crossed off expanded bell times via informal thumb polling while directing staff to prepare rotational coverage and evaluate the remaining options. Members also clashed over expanding Master's pay to social workers and instructional coaches amid a projected $1.8M-plus cost over the $1.2M budget.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, John Lucas Tribute, Agenda & Minutes Approvals
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers opened with a moment of silence reflecting on the election and recognized former Hillside principal John Lucas's 104th birthday. With Natalie Beyer absent, the board removed unready Consent Items 2B, 2C, and 2D, deferred Items 6A-6B to November 21, approved the amended agenda, and approved minutes from Sept 19, Sept 26 (with a minor Policy 2130 typo edit), and Oct 10.
agenda_items.vote_summary: All procedural agenda & minutes votes approved 6-0

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment & Leadership Introductions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters included Brogden ESL teachers citing a survey of 173 ELL students experiencing 101 midday bus cancellations, student letters, parent complaints over starting driver pay and proposed 1-mile walk zones, and Bill Bell naming advocates. Dr. Lewis then introduced incoming COO Dr. Larry Webb (starting Nov 18) and CFO Jeremy Teeter (started Nov 4) while thanking outgoing interim CFO Sierra Ojuigo.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items A, E, F, and G)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the remaining consent items by voice vote, after which Dr. Lewis highlighted the newly adopted Legislative Agenda prioritizing pay raises for all school employees with added focus on STEM teachers, EC teachers, and bus drivers.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent Evaluation Tool (McREL and 360 Survey)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers and Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten outlined the evaluation calendar combining the state McREL rubric, Strategic Plan metrics, and an anonymous 360 survey of principals, cabinet, and directors. The board voted to have staff bring internal and external 360 administration proposals ensuring anonymity and to include an optional comments box.

agenda_items.title: Policy 9300: Naming Facilities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Tanya Giovanni reviewed Policy 9300, prompting Wendell Tabb, Emily Chávez, Jessica Carda-Auten, and Bettina Umstead to urge eliminating the requirement that a person be deceased for five years before an entire school facility can be named for them (citing past waivers for John Lucas and Minnie Forte-Brown and community momentum for former mayor William 'Bill' Bell). The board voted 6-0 to move Policy 9300 to an action item and adopt that revision.

agenda_items.title: Transportation Supply/Demand Review and Six Triage Tactics
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After reordering the agenda 6-0 to take Transportation first, Director Joe Harris and Matthew Palmer reported 22,732 ride requests versus 134 drivers (165 needed) and presented rotational coverage plus six tactics: 1.5-mile/1-mile walk zones (~22 routes), regional Express Stops (~8 routes), expanded bell times, increased before/after-school supervision, dual employment CDL hires, and incentivizing 60 existing CDL-licensed staff. Following vigorous debate, Emily Chávez moved (Rogers seconded) to ask families who do not need buses to opt out—which Dr. Lewis accepted as administrative direction without a formal vote—and informal thumb polling ruled out expanding bell times while keeping rotational coverage and the other tactics under review.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda reorder 6-0; Informal thumb poll eliminated Tactic 3 (bell times); administrative follow-ups directed

agenda_items.title: Local Master's Pay Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Alvera Lesane and Michelle Hayes reviewed 583 unique survey submissions and 358 approved classroom teachers receiving local Master's pay, noting actual costs already exceeded the $1.2M budget (projected above the $1.87M 2022-23 estimate for 372 staff) while ~35-38 non-classroom certified staff (including 14 social workers) would add roughly $245,000+ at $7,000/person. Board members split over whether to absorb the cost to repair broken promises to social workers and instructional staff this year or hold the line given existing budget overruns, directing staff to bring detailed costs and legislative advocacy recommendations back.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and November 7, 2024 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Dr. Pittman's recap of board follow-up directives on Transportation and Master's pay, the board voted 6-0 to enter closed session at 06:02:21. Returning at 06:36:38, the board approved the November 7 personnel report 6-0 and adjourned.

votes.item_title: Defer Items 6A and 6B to November 21, 2024 Formal Meeting
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent; moved due to delayed availability of presentation materials.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after adjusting the consent agenda, Chair Millicent Rogers moved to remove Items 6A and 6B (Academic Services items) from the work session agenda because supporting materials arrived late, and to place them onto the November 21, 2024 formal board meeting agenda. Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten seconded the motion. The six board members present approved the deferral unanimously 6-0 on a voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve November 7, 2024 Work Session Agenda as Amended
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent.
votes.discussion_detail: With Consent Items 2B-2D pulled and Items 6A-6B moved to November 21, Emily Chávez moved to approve the November 7, 2024 work session agenda as amended. Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. No further changes were proposed at that point, and the six members present voted Aye unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Meeting Minutes from September 19, September 26 (Amended), and October 10, 2024
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten moved approval of the minutes from September 19, September 26, and October 10, 2024, initially seconded by Chair Millicent Rogers. During discussion, Emily Chávez flagged a typographical artifact in the September 26 minutes—the stray words 'updating the policy is' preceding her motion to waive Policy 2130(B)(3). Carda-Auten accepted the friendly amendment to approve the September 26 minutes as amended along with the September 19 and October 10 minutes, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff, and the motion passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Direct Administration to Bring In-House and External Proposals for Anonymous 360 Superintendent Survey
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent; covers director-level staff and above (including cabinet, principals, and APs if included).
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Millicent Rogers and Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten walked the board through a proposed annual superintendent evaluation framework combining the state-approved McREL rubric, Strategic Plan metrics, and a 360-degree survey open for 30 days in mid-May. Board members raised strong concerns about whether internal IT distribution via unique links could compromise participant anonymity and discourage candid feedback from principals, cabinet, and directors. Emily Chávez moved that administration bring back proposals—evaluating both in-house safeguards and external vendor options—to administer the 360 survey to director-level staff and above anonymously and safely, seconded by Rogers, passing 6-0.

votes.item_title: Include Optional Comments Section in Superintendent 360 Evaluation Survey
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent.
votes.discussion_detail: After deciding to solicit anonymous administration proposals for the 360-degree superintendent evaluation survey, board members debated whether respondents should only answer 1-to-5 quantitative items or also be permitted to submit qualitative comments. Proponents argued open-ended comments give essential context to numeric scores, while noting anonymity protections would remain crucial. Emily Chávez moved to include an optional comments section in the 360 survey tool, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff, and the motion passed 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Move Policy 9300 (Naming Facilities) to Action Item and Revise to Remove Five-Year Deceased Requirement
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent. Removes sentence barring naming an entire facility for an individual until five years after their death.
votes.discussion_detail: Chief Legal Officer Dr. Tanya Giovanni presented Policy 9300 on facility naming alongside public advocacy urging the district to name a facility after former Durham Mayor William 'Bill' Bell while he is still living. Wendell Tabb, Emily Chávez, Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten, and Bettina Umstead spoke passionately in favor of honoring living community icons and noted the board had already issued repeated policy waivers for John Lucas and Minnie Forte-Brown. Chávez moved to elevate Policy 9300 to an action item and delete the provision prohibiting an entire facility from being named for someone until five years after death, seconded by Tabb, and the motion passed 6-0.

votes.item_title: Amend Agenda to Move Operation Services (Transportation) Ahead of Master's Pay Update
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent.
votes.discussion_detail: With numerous transportation staff and community members waiting in the room, Emily Chávez moved to amend the agenda order to hear Operation Services Item A (Transportation Supply/Demand Review) ahead of the Deputy Superintendent Update (Local Master's Pay). Chair Millicent Rogers seconded the motion. The six members present voted unanimously 6-0 by voice vote to reorder the items.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent. Preceded by Dr. Pittman's verbal recap of board follow-up directives on Transportation and Master's Pay.
votes.discussion_detail: At the close of the Master's pay discussion at 05:58:14, Emily Chávez moved to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda, and Wendell Tabb seconded the motion (after Joy Harrell-Goff also reached for her microphone). Before voting, Dr. Pittman read back a detailed summary of staff follow-ups requested during the work session for both Transportation and Master's pay, with board members adding the 360 evaluation plan and standing transportation updates. The board then approved entering closed session 6-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Personnel Report Dated November 7, 2024
votes.notes: Natalie Beyer absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening in open session at 06:36:38 after roughly 34 minutes in closed session, Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis requested board action on the November 7, 2024 personnel report. Chair Millicent Rogers moved approval of the personnel report, and Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. The six board members present voted Aye 6-0 on voice vote, and the meeting adjourned.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/7/24
disagreements.issue: Transportation Crisis Mitigation: Walk Zones, Express Stops, and Rotational Coverage vs. Contracting/Vans
disagreements.summary: Board members diverged sharply on which short-term and structural transportation tactics to pursue, splitting in an informal thumb poll over immediate Express Stops and expressing competing concerns over walk zones, rotational coverage, and private/church bus contracting.
disagreements.side_a_position: Reject rotational coverage and elementary walk zones; prioritize private contracting, additional non-CDL vans, and partnering with churches that own 16+ passenger buses.
side_a_arguments: Cutting scheduled bus days via rotational coverage or forcing elementary children to walk a mile in winter weather imposes unacceptable hardship.
DPS already uses private contractors and owns seven 7-passenger vans not requiring CDLs, while church buses >15 passengers are legally usable.
disagreements.side_b_position: Endorse advance-notice rotational coverage as the most equitable immediate bridge while carefully vetting walk zones, Express Stops, CDL incentives, and family opt-outs.
side_b_arguments: Without 31 needed drivers, failing to rotate uncovered routes leaves low-income and ESL families disproportionately stranded without notice.

Informal polling showed only 2 up, 3 down, and 1 middle on immediate Express Stops and mixed middle/down views on walk zones, prompting consensus to rule out bell-time changes and require community feedback and safety analysis before any formal vote.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote taken; informal board polling crossed off Tactic 3 (expanding bell times) and authorized rotational coverage plus further data on Tactics 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/7/24
disagreements.issue: District Liability for Community-Organized Carpools and Walking Groups
disagreements.summary: Board members questioned whether DPS could actively organize parent volunteers and neighborhood walking/carpool networks to offset walk zones and bus shortages, drawing legal caution from staff.
disagreements.side_a_position: Assess DPS capacity to mobilize and organize volunteers, churches, and carpool/walking networks quickly.
side_a_arguments: Working families need practical carpool and walking-group support if elementary walk zones are introduced.
Community members offered to volunteer and step up to help alleviate the crisis.
disagreements.side_b_position: DPS cannot formally organize or guarantee parent-led carpools/walks due to legal and insurance liability.
side_b_arguments: Chief Legal Officer Tanya Giovanni and Chair Millicent Rogers noted a major legal distinction between parents informally forming phone trees and the school district organizing student rides.
Unvetted non-school rides create serious accident and supervision liability risks for the district.
disagreements.resolution: Staff directed to consult legal and insurance counsel on liability boundaries for volunteer driving and church partnerships.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 11/7/24
disagreements.issue: Expanding 2024-25 Master's Pay Beyond Classroom Teachers Despite Existing Budget Deficit
disagreements.summary: Following Dr. Alvera Lesane's report that 358 classroom teachers already pushed Master's pay toward $1.8M+ against a $1.2M budget, board members split over whether DPS is obligated to absorb another ~$245k+ this year for social workers, coaches, and specialists.
disagreements.side_a_position: Cost out and pursue 2024-25 coverage for the ~35-38 excluded certified instructional staff (including 14 social workers) to repair broken trust.
side_a_arguments: Spring 2024 board discussions said 'teachers' broadly without limiting to classroom teachers of record.
Social workers serve hundreds of high-need students and suffered emotional whiplash from contradictory HR eligibility emails.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid raising false expectations of mid-year expansion when Master's pay is already over budget and sustainable funding is lacking.
side_b_arguments: Classroom teacher Master's pay already exceeded the $1.2M budget by roughly $600k+, and Wake County saw costs jump by millions.
Promising mid-year pay without an identified funding source risks repeating past fiscal crises; focus should include legislative advocacy to restore state Master's pay.
disagreements.resolution: Staff directed to bring exact cost estimates and potential budget offsets back in December while adding Master's pay to the legislative agenda.
