meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 10/24/24
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 24, 2024 monthly meeting chaired by Millicent Rogers with Joy Harrell-Goff absent, the DPS Board of Education celebrated students and educators—including 2024-25 Principal of the Year Dr. Theresa McGowan—and heard Superintendent Anthony Lewis announce an $11.4 million five-year U.S. Department of Education grant and his ongoing Listening and Learning tour. The Board voted 6-0 to move Item 4C on 2024-25 transportation service shortage options to the November 7 work session to ensure complete staff data and returned the September 26 meeting minutes to November 7 for corrections regarding Meet and Confer motion wording. In later budget and compensation discussions, members pressed finance staff on position control—noting 5,104 active FTEs compared to 5,037 budgeted FTEs—and on Master's pay estimates rising to roughly 350 employees versus 200 budgeted, without taking formal action before entering closed session 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Monthly Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers opened the meeting and held a moment of silence before Ms. Cooper led monthly recognitions. Honorees included Student of the Month recipients, 2024-25 Principal of the Year Dr. Theresa McGowan of Lakeview School, October Teacher of the Month Wannima Jackson of Morehead Montessori School, Dr. Rathbone, and Employee of the Month Eduardo Garcia.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Anthony Lewis announced that DPS received an $11.4 million five-year Department of Education grant and recognized October Principals Month. Approaching his 60-day mark, he noted completion of six of seven Listening and Learning sessions, with the final session scheduled for November 12 at Northern High School and a future school safety forum planned.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Deferral of Item 4C (Transportation Service Shortage Options)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Rogers noted Joy Harrell-Goff was absent due to illness. Natalie Beyer moved to move Item 4C on options to address the 2024-25 transportation service shortage to the November 7 work session so appropriate staff and complete information could answer board questions, and the Board approved both the deferral and the amended agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Correction of September 26, 2024 Monthly Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jessica Carda-Auten noted minor and substantial errors in the September 26, 2024 meeting minutes, specifically regarding the exact wording of motions on the Meet and Confer policy. The Board voted 6-0 to bring the corrected minutes back to the November 7 work session.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Rogers reviewed public comment rules (two-minute speaking limit) before the digest truncated the middle portion of the meeting.

agenda_items.title: FY 2024-25 Position Control, Compensation Schedule Reconciliation, and Master's Pay Costs
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members questioned finance staff regarding how the $1.5 million item fit within the $8.8 million budget ask and raised concerns over position control after staff reported 5,104 active FTEs (some pending inactivation) compared to 5,037 budgeted FTEs. Members also sought clarity on reconciling pre-September 19 controller schedules with the new schedule, job description reviews, and projected Master's pay eligibility reaching roughly 350 employees versus 200 budgeted; no action was taken.

agenda_items.title: Change Order Report and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board acknowledged the construction change order report as an informational item requiring no vote. With Emily Chávez having stepped away and Joy Harrell-Goff absent, the remaining five members voted 5-0 to enter closed session.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 10/10/24
meetings.executive_summary: With Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten presiding, the board removed a hurricane makeup-day item rendered moot by NC House Bill 149 and heard pointed public criticism from DAE members regarding retro pay, disappearing pay scales, Hurricane Helene workday messaging, and live consultant edits to salary spreadsheets. Academic Services reported 2023-24 ESSA accountability results showing 42 of 52 schools (80.8%) met or exceeded growth even as A/B/C school counts fell from 33 to 28 and low-performing designations rose from 15 to 20. Operations and HR staff detailed opening-of-school metrics—including 110 classroom vacancies, 31,165 enrollment, 22,000 bus requests served by 131 drivers with 20-30 daily callouts, and a $15.4M Child Nutrition equipment deficit—before the board entered closed session and approved the October 10 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and September 12 Minutes Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten presided over the work session. The board removed Consent Item 2A (hurricane makeup date) after Dr. Lewis read NC House Bill 149 Section 8.1 waiving lost Hurricane Helene instructional days and guaranteeing employee pay, and approved the September 12 minutes 6-0.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Physical therapist and DAE member Christy Clem, using ceded speaker time, detailed four trust failures since September 12: classified retro pay omitting the 'higher of last year + 3% or new scales' promise, scales disappearing from the website, conflicting Hurricane Helene workday emails, and watching a consultant lower scale numbers in a live Google Doc at 10:30 p.m. Kristen Southworth urged stronger dyslexia screening and EC literacy support.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items B and C)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Item 2A already removed from the agenda, the board approved Consent Agenda Items B and C without further discussion.

agenda_items.title: Conference Updates and Classified Salary Schedule Governance Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members shared takeaways from NCSBA Core Training, School Board Partners' Our Collective Power conference, and the Minneapolis Chamber Interlocal visit, emphasizing multi-year budgeting, fund balance policy, and conflict resolution. Chief Legal Officer Dr. Tanya Giovanni then addressed Christy Clem's concerns, attributing spreadsheet changes to minor formula cleanup rather than malice while board members pressed HR/finance to post locked PDFs with clear revision dates and honor every retro-pay commitment.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: 2023-24 ESSA Accountability Results
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Al Royster and Dr. Julius King presented 2023-24 state accountability data showing 80.8% of DPS schools (42 schools) met or exceeded academic growth—with J.D. Clement Early College ranking #7 statewide—while overall GLP stood at 47%, A/B/C schools dipped from 33 to 28, and low-performing schools rose from 15 to 20 (with C.C. Spaulding and Forest View exiting). Board members probed ESL exit timelines, socioeconomic bias in NC A-F grades, and AIG demographic equity.

agenda_items.title: Opening of Schools Update (HR, Enrollment, Transportation, Child Nutrition)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Alvera Lesane reported 110 classroom vacancies (similar to 108 last year), and Matthew Palmer presented 31,165 enrollment alongside acute bus strain: 21,672-22,000 bus riders served by only 131 drivers facing 20-30 daily absences, forcing multi-tier routes alongside a 40% (~171-bus) ride load within 1.5 miles under Policy 6322. Child Nutrition reported adding 3,000+ daily free meals under CEP while carrying a $15.4M equipment deficit; board members pushed for accurate bus-related tardy coding, childcare/housing outreach, and temporary call-center staffing.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and October 10, 2024 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session at 03:44:35. Returning to open session at 05:20:49, the board approved the October 10, 2024 personnel report unanimously and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session unanimous; Personnel Report unanimous

votes.item_title: Remove Item 2A (Hurricane Makeup Date) and Approve October 10, 2024 Agenda as Amended
ayes: 6 present board members (unrecorded voice vote; one member arrived later)
votes.notes: House Bill 149 Sec. 8.1 waived instructional day makeups for Hurricane Helene and guaranteed employee/contractor pay.
votes.discussion_detail: With Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten presiding for the evening, Chair Millicent Rogers moved to remove Consent Item 2A regarding the hurricane makeup date and approve the October 10, 2024 agenda as amended. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion, and all six members present voted Aye by voice vote. Immediately after the vote, Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis read Section 8.1 of newly passed House Bill 149 confirming that public school units did not have to make up Hurricane Helene days and that all staff and contractors would be compensated as if worked.

votes.item_title: Approval of September 12, 2024 Meeting Minutes
ayes: 6 present board members (unrecorded voice vote; one member arrived later)
votes.discussion_detail: Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten called for action on the draft September 12, 2024 meeting minutes. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the minutes as presented, and Emily Chávez seconded the motion. With no discussion or amendments requested, the motion passed 6-0 on a voice vote.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: All seven board members were active during the preceding work session discussions.
votes.discussion_detail: At the conclusion of the Opening of Schools and transportation crisis Q&A at 03:44:35, Chair Millicent Rogers moved from the floor that the board go into closed session for the statutory reasons stated on the agenda. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. With no further discussion, all seven board members voted Aye by voice vote to enter closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve Personnel Report Dated October 10, 2024
votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening in open session at 05:20:49 after closed session, Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis asked Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten for board action on the October 10, 2024 personnel report. Emily Chávez moved approval of the personnel report, and Chair Millicent Rogers seconded the motion. The board approved the report unanimously by voice vote before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Work Session | 10/10/24
disagreements.issue: Classified Salary Schedule Revisions, Live Spreadsheet Edits, and Retro Pay Implementation
disagreements.summary: Public testimony from DAE physical therapist Christy Clem triggered sharp board questioning of HR and legal counsel over unannounced edits to live Google Doc salary scales, temporary removal of scales from the website, and delayed or omitted classified retro pay under the 'higher of last year + 3% or new scale' policy.
disagreements.side_a_position: Unannounced live edits, missing website scales, and unfulfilled retro pay promises represent ongoing breaches of employee trust requiring locked documentation and transparent fixes.
side_a_arguments: Watching a consultant adjust pay numbers on a live Google Doc after board adoption eroded confidence that adopted pay scales were authoritative.
Employees received no retro pay for the 'higher of' option, experienced up to multi-week HR email delays, and got contradictory Hurricane Helene workday directives.
disagreements.side_b_position: Spreadsheet adjustments reflected routine post-vote error cleanup rather than intentional deception, and staff are actively working through hundreds of individual payroll tickets.
side_b_arguments: Chief Legal Officer Tanya Giovanni explained consultants corrected minor formula errors without changing core adopted pay logic and re-uploaded scales once reviewed.
HR and finance faced severe backlog volume and legacy payroll system limitations while working to audit individual Master's, EC, and classified retro inquiries.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote; board members directed staff to replace live editable Google Docs with locked, date-stamped PDFs and clarify written communication on retro pay and pay-scale updates.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 9/26/24
meetings.executive_summary: With Wendell Tabb attending virtually and all votes conducted by roll call, the board heard public appeals to name a facility after former Mayor Bill Bell, fund Master's pay for school social workers, and adopt a strong Meet and Confer policy with DAE. After receiving an ad hoc committee report and legal cautions under NCGS 95-98 and NCGS 115C-335.9, the board unanimously referred Meet and Confer drafting to the Superintendent, DAE president, board officers, and legal counsel, before voting 4-3 to mandate establishing regular meetings with an Employee Representative Organization (ERO) demonstrating 50% membership among eligible staff. The board also waived Policy 2130(B)(3) to allow district phones or $50/month reimbursements for board members, approved a $400,000 lottery repair request, and passed the September 27 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers convened the meeting with Wendell Tabb virtual and recognized Student, Alum, Teacher, Employee, and Spark Pin honorees including Swim for Charlie founder Dr. John Klein. Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis reported 58 school threat/Guardian calls (vs. 7 the prior year), Edulog routing rollouts, 3,000+ added daily CEP free meals, 80%+ schools meeting/exceeding growth, and Listening & Learning community sessions.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, August 22 Minutes, Public Comment, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board pulled Consent Item 2C ($400,000 lottery repair request) to Item 5B, approved the amended agenda and August 22 minutes 7-0, and heard public comments supporting Bill Bell facility naming (400+ signatures), social worker Master's pay, and a DAE Meet and Confer policy before adopting the remaining consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Swim for Charlie Partnership Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. John Klein presented the Swim for Charlie water-safety partnership, targeting 1,800 DPS second graders during the school year and highlighting an 88% reduction in drowning risk.

agenda_items.title: Policy 2130: Board Member Communication Expenses
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT Director Susan Malone presented costs for issuing district iPhones ($42.39/month plus $13.62 hotspot) versus personal phone reimbursement. The board voted 7-0 to waive Policy 2130(B)(3) to allow district-issued phones reviewed annually with the budget and voted 7-0 to establish an optional $50/month personal phone reimbursement.

agenda_items.title: Ad Hoc Committee Update on Meet and Confer Policy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Lori McNulty, Dr. Lewis, and legal counsel presented NCGS 95-98 (public-sector collective bargaining ban) and Equal Access Act (NCGS 115C-335.9) cautions, an initial ERO motion by Joy Harrell-Goff died for lack of a second. The board then unanimously referred compliant drafting to the Superintendent, DAE president, board chair/vice chair, and attorneys, followed by a 4-3 split vote directing a policy establishing regular meetings with an ERO demonstrating 50% membership.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Drafting referral approved 7-0; 50% ERO policy directive approved 4-3

agenda_items.title: Operations Services: Change Orders, Work Orders, and $400,000 Lottery Fund Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a recess, Clifton Williams presented the monthly change order report and Pulled Item 5B ($400,000 from NC Education Lottery Repair & Renovation funds for roofing, life safety, and flooring). The board directed a staff follow-up report on daily open work orders and oldest open tickets (7-0) and approved the $400,000 request (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and September 27, 2024 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session 7-0 at 04:16:54. Returning at 05:04:19, the board initially approved the September 27 personnel report 6-0 while Wendell Tabb was briefly disconnected virtually, then reconfirmed his Aye vote at 05:05:29 for a unanimous 7-0 approval before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Pull Consent Item 2C to Action Item 5B and Approve September 26, 2024 Agenda as Amended
votes.notes: Wendell Tabb participated virtually; all votes conducted by roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Opening the business portion of the meeting with Wendell Tabb participating virtually, Natalie Beyer moved to pull Consent Agenda Item 2C (Repair and Renovation Lottery Fund Request) to Operations Services Item 5B for discussion and approve the September 26, 2024 agenda as amended. Emily Chávez seconded the motion. With no objections, all seven board members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approval of August 22, 2024 Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Following agenda approval, the board considered the draft minutes from its August 22, 2024 monthly meeting. Natalie Beyer moved to approve the minutes as submitted, and Emily Chávez seconded the motion. No revisions were requested, and the roll call vote carried unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Waive Policy 2130(B)(3) to Allow District-Issued Cell Phones for Board Members
votes.notes: Includes annual budget review; IT Director Susan Malone cited ~$42.39/mo device plan plus $13.62/mo hotspot for iPhone 12s.
votes.discussion_detail: IT Director Susan Malone briefed the board on costs for district-issued iPhone 12 devices ($42.39/month plus $13.62/month for hotspot service) under Policy 2130 governing board communication expenses. Members discussed public-records compliance and the burden of using personal devices for official school board business. Emily Chávez moved to waive Policy 2130(B)(3) so board members may receive district-issued cell phones subject to annual budget review, seconded by Joy Harrell-Goff, passing 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Adopt Optional $50 Monthly Technology Supplement Reimbursement for Board Members
votes.notes: Reimburses up to $50/month for personal cell phone use for members opting not to carry a separate district phone.
votes.discussion_detail: After waiving Policy 2130(B)(3) to allow district-issued phones, members noted that some trustees preferred using a single personal device rather than carrying two phones. Natalie Beyer moved to establish an optional monthly technology supplement reimbursement of up to $50 per month for board members seeking personal phone reimbursement instead of a district phone. Bettina Umstead seconded the motion, and it passed unanimously 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Refer Meet and Confer Draft Policy Development to Superintendent, DAE President, Board Leadership, and Attorneys
votes.notes: Preceded by a separate Joy Harrell-Goff motion at 02:39:14 that failed for lack of a second at 02:42:12.
votes.discussion_detail: Following public comment from over a dozen DAE educators and parents alongside legal counsel warnings about NCGS 95-98 (prohibiting public-sector collective bargaining) and NCGS 115C-335.9 (equal-access protections), an initial ERO motion by Joy Harrell-Goff died for lack of a second. Natalie Beyer then moved, seconded by Bettina Umstead, to refer Meet and Confer policy drafting to Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis based on ad hoc committee feedback to return a legally compliant draft. With friendly amendments from Wendell Tabb and Emily Chávez formally bringing the DAE president, board chair, board vice chair, and district attorneys into the drafting group alongside community input, the referral motion passed unanimously 7-0.

votes.item_title: Direct Meet and Confer Policy Establishing Regular Meetings with an ERO at 50% Membership Threshold
votes.notes: Covers non-administrative and non-managerial active DPS employees as of the end of the prior school year.
votes.discussion_detail: Even after referring collaborative drafting to the Superintendent and DAE leadership, board members remained divided over whether to give explicit policy direction recognizing an Employee Representative Organization (ERO) based on majority membership. Joy Harrell-Goff moved, seconded by Emily Chávez, to direct development of a Meet and Confer policy establishing regular meetings with an ERO demonstrating 50% membership among non-administrative, non-managerial active DPS employees as of the end of the prior school year. Supporters argued clear democratic benchmarks honor unionized workers and prevent exclusion, while opponents warned against legal exposure under NCGS 95-98/115C-335.9 and potential exclusion of non-member employee groups. On roll call, Chávez, Carda-Auten, Harrell-Goff, and Umstead voted Aye while Tabb, Beyer, and Chair Rogers voted Nay, carrying the motion 4-3.

votes.item_title: Five-Minute Recess
votes.notes: Reconvened at 04:06:35.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the extended Meet and Confer debate and 4-3 vote, Natalie Beyer moved that the board take a five-minute recess. Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion. Conducted by roll call due to Wendell Tabb's virtual attendance, all seven members voted Aye.

votes.item_title: Direct Staff Report on Average Open Work Orders Per Day and Age of Oldest Open Work Order
votes.discussion_detail: During the Operations Services update by Clifton Williams covering maintenance change orders and pulled lottery repair requests, board members asked about maintenance backlogs across aging campuses. Chair Millicent Rogers moved that staff return a follow-up report showing the average number of open work orders per day and the age of the oldest open work order in the district's system. Joy Harrell-Goff seconded the motion, which passed unanimously 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve $400,000 Repair and Renovation Lottery Fund Request (Item 5B)
votes.notes: Allocates $150,000 for roofing, $150,000 for life safety, and $100,000 for flooring.
votes.discussion_detail: Addressing Consent Item 2C after it was moved to Item 5B, Operations staff presented the $400,000 North Carolina Education Lottery Repair and Renovation Fund request, earmarking $150,000 for roofing, $150,000 for life safety, and $100,000 for flooring repairs. Board members verified the project priorities and work-order tracking context before acting. Natalie Beyer moved approval of the $400,000 lottery fund request, Joy Harrell-Goff seconded, and the motion passed 7-0 on roll call.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after approving the $400,000 facilities lottery request, Emily Chávez moved that the board enter closed session for the statutory purposes stated on the meeting agenda. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. All seven board members voted Aye on roll call.

votes.item_title: Approve Personnel Report Dated September 27, 2024
votes.notes: Initially approved 6-0 at 05:04:57 while Wendell Tabb had not yet reconnected from closed session; Tabb rejoined at 05:05:29 and recorded his Aye vote for a final 7-0 tally.
votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening in open session at 05:04:19, Natalie Beyer moved approval of the personnel report dated September 27, 2024, seconded by Emily Chávez. With Wendell Tabb temporarily disconnected virtually after closed session, the six members in the boardroom approved the report 6-0 at 05:04:57. Thirty seconds later, at 05:05:29, Tabb reconnected to the call and recorded his Aye vote, finalizing the approval as 7-0 before adjournment.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Monthly Meeting | 9/26/24
disagreements.issue: Meet and Confer Policy: 50% ERO Membership Threshold vs. Inclusive Multi-Group Consultation and Statutory Caution
disagreements.summary: Following a unanimous referral for collaborative policy drafting, the board split 4-3 on explicitly directing a Meet and Confer policy centered on an Employee Representative Organization (ERO) with 50% employee membership.
disagreements.side_a_position: Mandate a Meet and Confer policy establishing regular meetings with an ERO representing at least 50% of eligible non-administrative DPS employees.
side_a_arguments: Recognizes the democratic majority voice of workers organized through DAE after months of compensation turmoil.
Sets a clear, verifiable threshold rather than watering down representation across small or ad hoc groups.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid locking in a 50% ERO exclusivity directive before legal review and input from non-DAE workers.
side_b_arguments: Attorney raised legal concerns under NCGS 95-98 (public bargaining prohibition) and NCGS 115C-335.9 (equal-access obligations).
Setting a strict 50% ERO rule could exclude other employees or organizations (such as Teamsters or non-union workers) before the Superintendent's working group drafts a policy.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-3 directing development of the 50%-threshold ERO Meet and Confer policy alongside the 7-0 drafting referral.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Special Called Meeting | 9/19/24
meetings.executive_summary: At a Special Called Meeting on September 19, 2024 presided over by Chair Millicent Rogers with Bettina Umstead absent, the Board of Education tackled FY 2024-25 compensation schedules, local supplements, and Master's pay following an overview from consultant Ms. Price on aligning Finance and HR and reducing schedule variability. During public comment, school social workers and union supporters urged the Board to pass Meet and Confer and extend Master's pay beyond classroom teachers to social workers and other instructional support staff. After Natalie Beyer objected to granting administration open discretion over who would receive the $3 million local supplement pool—forcing a 30-minute recess—the Board unanimously passed four compensation motions 6-0: an $80/month local supplement increase for specified certified and support roles, $200-$350/month EC and ESL supplements, a 10% Master's pay differential for NC DPI-aligned classroom teachers, and placement of uncovered existing employees onto the most employee-favorable 2024-25 schedule.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Absence Acknowledgment, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers opened the special meeting, noted Bettina Umstead was unavailable due to a prior work commitment, and held a moment of silence. The Board approved the agenda unanimously 6-0.

agenda_items.title: 2024-25 Compensation Schedules Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultant Ms. Price presented key findings for the 2024-25 compensation schedules, emphasizing reduced variability over time and resolving functional ownership confusion between Finance and Human Resources so both divisions communicate consistent budget and personnel implications.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment on Master's Pay, Local Supplements, and Meet and Confer
agenda_items.discussion_summary: School social workers (including Parkwood Elementary social worker Sydney Schildnacht) and DAE advocates criticized limiting Master's pay to classroom-based teachers, noted social worker caseloads far exceeding the 1:250 NASW guideline, cited panic over potential pay cuts for SLPs and school psychologists, and urged the Board to pass Meet and Confer.

agenda_items.title: Local Supplement Increase ($80/Month) and Recess to Define Eligible Staff
agenda_items.discussion_summary: When staff noted the 12.5% / $3M local supplement ask covered ~2,900 employees without specifying recipients, Natalie Beyer objected to giving administration open discretion and moved a five-minute recess (extended ~30 minutes). Upon returning, the Board unanimously approved an $80/month supplement increase specifically for SLPs, psychologists, audiologists, school counselors, teachers, nurses, and instructional support personnel.

agenda_items.title: EC and ESL Monthly Supplements and Differentials
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following clarification from Ms. Price, the Board unanimously approved $200/month supplements for regular EC resource and ESL teachers, $350/month total ($200 plus $150 differential) for self-contained EC specialized program teachers, and a $200/month EC classified differential for sign language, deaf/hard of hearing, visually impaired, and spoken language staff, directing implementation in September payroll without hurting retirement.

agenda_items.title: 10% Master's Pay Differential for Classroom-Based Teachers (NC DPI Aligned)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: District staff sought Board guidance on aligning Master's pay to NC DPI guidelines (covering 189 classroom-based teachers vs. 237 broader staff), and Jessica Carda-Auten asked for clarity on which educators would be excluded under DPI's June 2013 and subject-area rules. The Board unanimously approved a 10% pay differential for relevant Master's degrees for classroom-based teachers aligned to NC DPI guidelines, while requesting a list of other roles for the next budget cycle.

agenda_items.title: Most Employee-Favorable Schedule Placement Authorization and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously authorized administration to place any existing employees not covered by the previously approved schedules onto the most employee-favorable schedule for the 2024-25 school year before adjourning to reconvene the 4:30 PM panel meeting into closed session.

votes.item_title: Approve Special Called Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: After acknowledging Bettina Umstead's absence due to a prior work commitment, Joy Harrell-Goff moved and Jessica Carda-Auten seconded approval of the September 19, 2024 special called meeting agenda. The voice vote passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Recess to Identify Eligible Local Supplement Recipients
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: When discussion of the $3 million local supplement ask revealed that eligible employee categories had not yet been finalized, Natalie Beyer stated she was uncomfortable granting administration discretion to choose recipients and moved a five-minute recess so staff could identify who was covered. Emily Chávez seconded, and the motion passed unanimously 6-0; the Board reconvened roughly 29 minutes later.

votes.item_title: Approve $80/Month Local Supplement Increase for Specified Certified and Instructional Support Staff
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately following the recess, Natalie Beyer moved and Emily Chávez seconded approving an additional $80 per month local supplement increase for speech-language pathologists, psychologists, audiologists, school counselors, teachers, nurses, and instructional support personnel. The motion passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve EC and ESL Monthly Supplements and Specialized Differentials
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent; transcript digest did not capture the explicit mover/seconder roll call attribution for this motion.
votes.discussion_detail: After Ms. Price clarified the breakdown—$200/month for regular EC resource and ESL teachers, $350/month total for self-contained EC specialized program teachers, and $200/month EC classified differential for sign language, deaf/hard of hearing, visually impaired, and spoken language staff—a motion was made to approve the supplements with direction to implement them in September payroll without harming employee retirement. The voice vote passed unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Approve 10% Master's Pay Differential for Classroom-Based Teachers Aligned to NC DPI Guidelines
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Following questions on whether to align eligibility to NC DPI guidelines (covering 189 classroom-based teachers) and clarification that the differential applies per individual paycheck rather than being modeled on base salary schedules, Natalie Beyer moved and Emily Chávez seconded approving a 10% pay differential for relevant Master's degrees for classroom-based teachers aligned with NC DPI standards, with a broader list to be compiled for next year's budget. The motion carried unanimously 6-0.

votes.item_title: Authorize Placement of Uncovered Existing Employees on Most Employee-Favorable 2024-25 Schedule
votes.notes: Bettina Umstead absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Jessica Carda-Auten moved and Natalie Beyer seconded authorizing administration to place any existing employees not covered by a schedule previously approved at the meeting onto the most employee-favorable schedule for the 2024-25 school year. The voice vote passed unanimously 6-0.

Public commenters raised sharp complaints over Edulog bus-routing failures and withheld October market-pay increases forcing staff to work second jobs, while Dr. Lewis addressed recent school threat surges and Edulog parent portal visibility issues. meetings.title: Board of Education Special Called Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At a Special Called Meeting on August 2, 2024 chaired by Millicent Rogers, the Board of Education approved the agenda and consent agenda 7-0 before holding a statutory presentation and public hearing on the new Durham School of the Arts (DSA) under N.C.G.S. 115C-72 and 115C-521(c). Operational Services officials explained that building a new DSA under the 2022 bond costs roughly $213 million compared to $269.4 million ($213 million plus $56 million in site and traffic improvements) to place equivalent capacity on the existing downtown campus, while noting the district is building a new campus rather than closing DSA. Six public hearing speakers—including Durham for DSA representatives, a retired teacher, a nearby ballet studio founder, and a DSA student—challenged the adequacy of public notice, disputed the renovation cost comparison as outdated, and urged renovating the historic downtown campus to save over $50 million and preserve downtown walkability. After Natalie Beyer requested expanded social media outreach ahead of the August 8 agenda, the Board entered closed session 7-0 and returned to approve the August 1, 2024 personnel action report 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers opened the special meeting and led a moment of silence. The Board unanimously approved the agenda 7-0 and the consent agenda 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Durham School of the Arts Statutory Closure Study and Cost Feasibility Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. LaFries, Matthew Palmer, and Ms. Williams presented the DSA study under N.C.G.S. 115C-72 and the apples-to-apples cost feasibility comparison submitted to NCDPI under N.C.G.S. 115C-521(c). Staff reported that fitting the newly designed 1,850-student facility onto the existing campus—which holds only 13 of 1,000 daily car riders—would add $56 million in site and traffic upgrades for a $269,439,861 total versus $213 million for the new site, plus two to three years of inflation and existing design/CMAR contracts.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing on Durham School of the Arts (N.C.G.S. 115C-72)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six speakers—including Jane Wheeler and Julia Borbely-Brown (Durham for DSA), Willen Willis (Durham School for Ballet and the Performing Arts), Brian Calloway, and a DSA student—criticized short public notice (citing DSA's PTSA not being informed), questioned the financial numbers, argued renovating the 100-year-old downtown campus would save $50 million and protect walkable downtown businesses and students, and noted State Historic Commission review requirements. Natalie Beyer asked administration to deepen public outreach via social media ahead of the August 8 work session.

meetings.title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Organizational Meeting | 7/1/24
meetings.executive_summary: At its annual organizational meeting, Judge Josephine Davis administered oaths of office to reelected members Millicent Rogers and Jessica Carda-Auten and newly elected members Wendell Tabb and Joy Harrell-Goff. Under Policy 2200, Millicent Rogers was elected Board Chair (5-1 with Wendell Tabb abstaining), followed by a divided Vice Chair election pitting institutional continuity (Bettina Umstead, backed by Natalie Beyer) against leadership succession (Jessica Carda-Auten, backed by Joy Harrell-Goff and the board majority). After Attorney Rod Malone ruled that unexcused abstentions count as affirmative votes under board policy, Bettina Umstead's nomination failed 3-4 and Jessica Carda-Auten was elected Vice Chair 6-1, before the board unanimously approved its 2024-25 meeting schedule and interim superintendent Catty Moore's contract addendum.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Swearing-In of Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Chair Bettina Umstead called the organizational meeting to order and held a moment of silence. Judge Josephine Davis administered oaths of office to returning members Millicent Rogers and Jessica Carda-Auten alongside incoming members Wendell Tabb and Joy Harrell-Goff, who each offered brief remarks to family and community members.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair and Board Vice Chair (Policy 2200)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Superintendent Catty Moore conducted the Chair election under Policy 2200, with Millicent Rogers nominated unopposed and elected 5-1 (with Wendell Tabb abstaining). Rogers then presided over a contested Vice Chair election between former Chair Bettina Umstead and Jessica Carda-Auten (after a third nominee withdrew); Attorney Rod Malone clarified that unexcused abstentions count as affirmative votes, yielding a 3-4 defeat for Umstead and a 6-1 election for Carda-Auten.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Chair Rogers 5-1 (1 abstention); Vice Chair Umstead failed 3-4; Vice Chair Carda-Auten passed 6-1

agenda_items.title: Adoption of 2024-25 Board of Education Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Millicent Rogers presented the proposed 2024-25 regular board meeting and work session calendar for adoption.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Catty Moore Interim Contract Addendum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board entered closed session at 00:57:31 for personnel matters. Returning at 01:29:40, members unanimously approved the second addendum to Interim Superintendent Catty Moore's contract and an interim employment contract for the week of August 10, 2024 before adjourning at 01:30:20.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session 7-0; Catty Moore contract addendum 7-0

votes.item_title: Election of Millicent Rogers as Board Chair for 2024-2025
votes.notes: Conducted by Interim Superintendent Catty Moore under Policy 2200 (nominations require no second). Announced as 5-1 with 1 abstention (Wendell Tabb); Attorney Rod Malone later noted board policy treats unexcused abstentions as affirmative votes, though five affirmative votes already carried the majority.
votes.discussion_detail: Interim Superintendent Catty Moore presided over the Board Chair election under Policy 2200, explaining that nominations did not require a second. Millicent Rogers was the sole nominee for Board Chair. On a voice vote, five members voted Aye, one member voted No, and newly sworn member Wendell Tabb abstained—explaining shortly afterward that he chose to abstain because the board had not reached unanimous leadership consensus. Moore declared Rogers elected Chair 5-1 with one abstention and passed the gavel.

votes.item_title: Nomination of Bettina Umstead for Board Vice Chair for 2024-2025
votes.notes: Initially counted 2-4 with 1 abstention (Bettina Umstead confirmed voting for herself; Natalie Beyer nominated and spoke for her). Under Attorney Rod Malone's ruling on board policy, Wendell Tabb's unexcused abstention counted as an affirmative vote, making the recorded tally 3-4 (Failed).
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer nominated outgoing Chair Bettina Umstead for Vice Chair, delivering an extended speech arguing that incoming Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis needed Umstead's institutional memory, external relationships, and experience navigating the 2024 pay crisis. Umstead accepted the board's will while highlighting the $27M county budget expansion and pandemic recovery under her tenure, whereas Joy Harrell-Goff spoke in favor of leadership succession and Wendell Tabb explained he would abstain on non-unanimous officer votes. Prior to voting, Attorney Rod Malone advised that board policy requires voting separately on each nominee and treats any unexcused abstention as an affirmative vote. The voice vote on Umstead yielded two Ayes (Beyer and Umstead), four Nays, and Tabb's abstention—recorded officially under policy as 3-4, failing to win a majority.

votes.item_title: Election of Jessica Carda-Auten as Board Vice Chair for 2024-2025
votes.notes: Voice vote had 4 Aye, 1 Nay, and 2 abstentions (Wendell Tabb and one silent member); Attorney Rod Malone and Chair Rogers corrected the initial 4-1-2 / 4-3 announcement to 6-1 because both unexcused abstentions count as affirmative votes under board policy.
votes.discussion_detail: Following the 3-4 defeat of Bettina Umstead's nomination, the board voted on the second nominee, Jessica Carda-Auten (after a third member had withdrawn from nomination). Carda-Auten received four audible Aye votes (including her own and Joy Harrell-Goff, who had spoken in support of succession), one audible No vote, and two abstentions—Wendell Tabb plus one member who remained silent. Chair Millicent Rogers initially announced the tally as 4-1 with two abstentions and Attorney Rod Malone briefly misstated it as 4-3 before correcting the math on the record: because board policy records unexcused abstentions as affirmative votes, both abstentions counted as Ayes for a final official vote of 6-1 electing Carda-Auten as Vice Chair.

votes.item_title: Approve 2024-2025 Board of Education Meeting Schedule
votes.discussion_detail: After Chair Millicent Rogers and Vice Chair Jessica Carda-Auten delivered their leadership remarks emphasizing governance frameworks and collaboration, the board turned to the proposed 2024-25 meeting schedule. Emily Chávez moved approval of the 2024-25 meeting calendar, and Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. No revisions were requested, and all seven board members voted Aye unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Enter Closed Session for Personnel Matters
votes.discussion_detail: Immediately after adopting the annual meeting calendar, Natalie Beyer moved that the board go into closed session for the statutory personnel reasons stated on the agenda. Bettina Umstead seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously 7-0 by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approve Second Addendum to Catty Moore's Employment Contract and Interim Contract for Week of August 10, 2024
votes.notes: Meeting adjourned at 01:30:20.
votes.discussion_detail: Returning to open session at 01:29:40 after roughly 32 minutes in closed session, Bettina Umstead moved approval of the second addendum to Interim Superintendent Catty Moore's employment contract along with an interim employment contract covering the week of August 10, 2024. Natalie Beyer seconded the motion. All seven board members voted Aye on voice vote, passing the contracts unanimously before Chair Millicent Rogers adjourned the meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: #DPSCommunity | DPS Board of Education Organizational Meeting | 7/1/24
disagreements.issue: Board Vice Chair Election: Institutional Memory vs. Leadership Succession
disagreements.summary: Following Millicent Rogers's election as Chair, board members split publicly over whether former Chair Bettina Umstead or newly reelected Jessica Carda-Auten should serve as Vice Chair during Superintendent Dr. Anthony Lewis's onboarding.
disagreements.side_a_position: Elect outgoing Chair Bettina Umstead as Vice Chair to preserve institutional memory and external stakeholder relationships.
side_a_arguments: After the pay crisis and rapid superintendent transition, Dr. Anthony Lewis needs seasoned board leadership continuity alongside Chair Rogers.
Umstead brought deep relationships with Durham County Commissioners, city officials, community organizations, and DAE/Teamsters.
disagreements.side_b_position: Elect Jessica Carda-Auten as Vice Chair to support leadership succession and structured governance.
side_b_arguments: Joy Harrell-Goff emphasized that leadership rotation and succession planning strengthen an equally weighted seven-member governing body.
Carda-Auten advocated establishing clear governance frameworks and board-superintendent accountability systems.
disagreements.resolution: Wendell Tabb abstained on non-unanimous leadership votes (counted as affirmative under board policy); Bettina Umstead's nomination failed 3-4 and Jessica Carda-Auten was elected Vice Chair 6-1.
